# Red Wood Farm (full text)

> Garden family restaurant and party lawn on outer Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana, Punjab. Garden family restaurant and party lawn. Tandoor, North Indian and Indo-Chinese food, 187 priced dishes, open every day. Short index: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/llms.txt

## Key facts
- Address: 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, Opp. Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana, Punjab 142022
- Phone and bookings: 096467 13555
- Hours: 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day
- Service: dine-in on a garden lawn with fairy lights, takeaway, Wi-Fi. No wheelchair access.
- Google rating: 4.2 from 72 reviews (as of 17 Nov 2026)
- Not published (ask us): guest capacity, per-plate and package prices

# Guides

## A family outing near Ludhiana with kids: an afternoon at Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/family-outing-with-kids/

In short: for a family outing near Ludhiana, spend an afternoon or evening at Red Wood Farm, a garden restaurant at Daad on outer Pakhowal Road, about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar. Children get open grass to move around on and the menu runs from fries and noodles to tandoor and curries. We are open 10 AM to 11 PM every day, with no wheelchair access.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm good for children?
A: There is space on the grass for children, and the menu has French Fries at ₹195, Hakka Noodles at ₹255 and ice cream from ₹50 a scoop. There is no play area or rides.

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from the centre of Ludhiana?
A: By road it is about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar and 10.7 km from Ludhiana Railway Station, roughly 11 and 16 minutes by OSRM routing without traffic. Leave extra time.

Q: Can grandparents who use a wheelchair visit?
A: Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. Please message us at 096467 13555 if you have questions about getting around.

Q: Should a big family book ahead?
A: Yes, for a group send the date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555 and we will confirm.

For a family outing near Ludhiana, plan an afternoon or evening at Red Wood Farm, a garden restaurant at Daad on outer Pakhowal Road. It is about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar. Children have open grass to roam, adults get a full North Indian menu, and we are open from 10 AM to 11 PM every day.

## How far is it from your part of Ludhiana?

Red Wood Farm sits where the city starts to thin out, on the stretch of Pakhowal Road that OpenStreetMap labels Jodhan - Ludhiana Road. Most of the drive is on Pakhowal Road itself. These road distances and times come from OpenStreetMap and OSRM routing, checked on 17 November 2026. The times assume empty roads, so add a margin for traffic.

| Starting point | Distance | Time with no traffic |
|---|---|---|
| Hero Bakery Chowk, Pakhowal Road | 6.1 km | about 10 min |
| Dugri | 6.5 km | about 12 min |
| Sarabha Nagar | 6.8 km | about 11 min |
| Model Town | 6.9 km | about 11 min |
| ISBT bus stand | 8.2 km | about 13 min |
| Bharat Nagar Chowk, Ferozepur Road | 9.5 km | about 14 min |
| Ludhiana Railway Station | 10.7 km | about 16 min |

Route details for each starting point are on our [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/).

## An afternoon plan that works with small children

1. **Arrive around lunchtime.** In daylight the lawn is set with long wooden tables and lounge seating, so a family can spread out.
2. **Order early.** Children get hungry faster than adults admit. Put in their food first, then take your time with the rest.
3. **Let them use the grass.** While the curries cook, the kids can stretch their legs on the lawn within sight of your table.
4. **Take a slow walk.** The stone garden path winds through the grounds, and the hedge entrance arch with its flowers makes an easy family photo.
5. **Leave before naps go wrong.** An early afternoon visit gets everyone home before the evening.

## An evening plan for older children

Older kids tend to like the lights. Arrive a little before sunset so they can see the lawn by day first. After dark the fairy-light tunnel is lit, with warm white bulbs over a red carpet and green uplights in the trees, and most visitors stop there for a photo. Have dinner, then head home before our 11 PM closing.

## What is there for children, and what isn't?

There is space on the grass. That is the honest list. Red Wood Farm has no play area, no kids' zone and no rides, so plan on the lawn and the food doing the work. Keep an eye on small children near the paths and the lit decorations, and bring anything that usually keeps them busy at a restaurant table. A spare set of clothes helps too, since grass and small children tend to meet. If a child has a food allergy, message us before the visit and ask about the dishes you plan to order.

## Food that keeps a mixed table happy

Children often lean toward the snack section. French Fries are ₹195, Cheesy Fries ₹225 and Peri Peri Fries ₹225. Honey Chilli Potato and Hakka Noodles are ₹255 each, Cheese Fingers ₹315 and Chicken Popcorn ₹385. A Cheese Naan at ₹80 is a safe bet for picky eaters.

For the adults, Dal Makhni at ₹275 and a half Kadhai Paneer at ₹225 make a solid vegetarian base. Butter Chicken is ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full. Finish with ice cream by the scoop: Vanilla and Strawberry are ₹50, Chocolate and Tutti Frutti are ₹55. See more ideas in our guide to [kid-friendly dishes](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/kids-favourites/).

## Bringing grandparents along

Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access, and we would rather you know that before you set out. The seating is outdoors on a lawn, and you reach it on garden paths. If an older family member finds walking hard, message us and ask which table is easiest to reach.

## Other good places to visit in Ludhiana with family

Ludhiana has well-known city parks, such as Nehru Rose Garden and Rakh Bagh, and some families pair a park visit with a meal later in the day. Check their timings before you go, since we do not keep track of them.

Closer to us, OpenStreetMap shows Gurdwara Bhai Bala Sahib Ji about 1.6 km away and Gurudwara Harkiratgarh Tibbi Sahib about 2.3 km away. Our page on [weekend plans near Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/weekend-plans-near-ludhiana/) lays out a few half-day plans around Daad.

## Booking for a family group

For a large family, send us your date, time and number of guests at 096467 13555. If the outing is really a birthday in disguise, our page on [birthday party venues in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/birthday-party-venues-ludhiana/) explains how we host those on the lawn. Our address is 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats.

## An evening on the lawn at Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/an-evening-on-the-lawn/

In short: an evening at Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road means dinner on an open garden lawn after a walk through a tunnel of warm white fairy lights. You can sit on the grass, under lit palms or in a lounge corner under string lights, and order from the tandoor and the curry menu. We are open every day until 11 PM, and tables are booked by message at 096467 13555.

Q: When is the best time to arrive for dinner on the lawn?
A: Come around sunset if you want to watch the garden go from daylight to fairy lights. We stay open until 11:00 PM every day.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm only for parties in the evening?
A: No. Red Wood Farm is a family restaurant first, and the lawn is open for ordinary dinners every evening, with parties booked separately.

Q: Can a couple ask for a quieter table?
A: Yes, ask for a table under the palm trees when you book with a message at 096467 13555, and we will tell you what we can arrange.

Q: Is there Wi-Fi at Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes, Wi-Fi is available for guests.

Dinner on the lawn at Red Wood Farm begins at the gate on outer Pakhowal Road and leads through a tunnel of warm white fairy lights to tables on open grass, under lit palms or in a lounge corner. Order from the tandoor, take your time over the meal, and keep in mind that we close at 11 PM.

## Arriving after dark

You will find us at 676, VPO Daad, on Pakhowal Road, across from Cerajot Tiles and close to Omaxe Flats. The first thing you notice from the driveway is the palms, each one wrapped in fairy lights, and the green neon sign that spells out RED WOOD FARM.

Past the garden gate and the green hedge arch with its flowers, the path takes you into the tunnel. You walk along a red carpet with a canopy of warm white bulbs overhead, while green uplights pick out the trees around you. It is the spot guests photograph most, so give yourself a minute here before you go and find a table. We have a whole page on the [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/fairy-light-tunnel/) if you want to plan a picture.

Beyond the tunnel, lit paths with lamp posts lead out to the lawn. Trees wrapped in lights mark the edges of the grass, so even the far tables have a glow around them.

## Picking your spot

The lawn has three kinds of seating, and each suits a different kind of evening.

- **Tables on the open lawn.** Pick these when a family wants room to spread out and a full view of the lights. Children can step onto the grass between courses.
- **Tables under the palms.** Each trunk glows with fairy lights, and these tables feel more tucked away from the middle of the lawn. They suit two people celebrating something, or parents with one or two children.
- **Lounge seating under string lights.** The seats sit low, and the corner works best for friends who plan to keep talking long after the plates are cleared.

If you have a preference, mention it when you book, and we will tell you what is free that evening. All of it is outdoors. For a broader look at eating outside in the city, read our guide to [open-air dining in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/open-air-dining-ludhiana/).

## What to order for a table outside

Start with the tandoor, because those plates travel well to an outdoor table and are easy to share. Paneer Tikka and Tandoori Chicken are ₹375 each. Soya chaap fans should try the Afghani Champ at ₹275. For four or more, a platter gets everyone eating at once: the Chinese Veg Platter is ₹575 and the Non-Veg Platter is ₹775. Our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/tandoor-guide/) has the full list.

For the main course, try our house signature first. Farm to Table Special Chicken costs ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full. Vegetarians can share Dal Makhni at ₹275 and Paneer Lababdar at ₹255 for a half or ₹395 for a full. If the table is up for something different, Atta Chicken at ₹925 is chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough. Ask how long it takes when you order.

Garlic Naan at ₹55 and a bowl of our own herb chutney at ₹75 round it out. To finish, Paneer Jalebi with Rabri and Kesar Kheer are ₹75 each. Every price includes GST, and the [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists all 187 dishes with veg and non-veg marks.

## What guests have said about the evenings

On Google, Red Wood Farm showed a 4.2 rating from 72 reviews on 14 November 2026. Two short lines from those reviews describe the place well. Isha wrote: "Very good place awesome decor yummy food". Sanjeev Kumar called it a "Crazy location for casual parties and events..staff is also friendly".

## Good to know before you go

- **Hours:** 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day.
- **Booking:** message the date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call the same number.
- **Takeaway:** order by phone or message and collect.
- **Wi-Fi:** available.
- **Access:** there is no wheelchair access.
- **Cold months:** December and January nights get cold on an open lawn. Our page on [winter evenings on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/winter-evenings-on-the-lawn/) covers what to wear and what to order.

## The same lawn by daylight

If an evening visit goes well, the lawn is worth seeing in daylight too. We open at 10 AM, and by day the grass is set with long wooden tables and lounge seating, with the stone garden path winding through the grounds. A daytime meal feels quite different from a dinner under the lights, and it is worth trying both.

## When an evening turns into a party

The same lawn hosts birthdays, kitty parties and family functions, with set-ups that have included balloon arches, a mehndi stage and buffet counters on the grass. If you are thinking of booking one, start on our [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/).

## Anniversary Dinner in Ludhiana: A Garden Table Under the Lights
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/anniversary-dinner-ludhiana/

In short: for an anniversary dinner with an outdoor feel, book an evening table on Red Wood Farm's garden lawn on Pakhowal Road, under palms and string lights, with a full North Indian menu. We don't offer private dining or candle set-ups. Family anniversaries for bigger groups can be planned on the lawn by message.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm offer a private candle light dinner?
A: No. We don't offer a private dining area or a candle set-up. Couples dine at garden tables under palms and string lights, with other guests around.

Q: What time should we book an anniversary dinner?
A: Book for after sunset if you want the lights at their best. We're open until 11:00 PM every day.

Q: Can we celebrate our parents' anniversary on the lawn?
A: Yes. Send the date, time and number of guests on 096467 13555, and we'll tell you what set-up is possible that evening.

Q: Is the dinner outdoors in winter?
A: The tables are on the open lawn, so dress warmly on winter evenings. Ask us what seating is available for your date.

For an anniversary dinner in Ludhiana with an outdoor feel, book an evening table on our garden lawn on Pakhowal Road. You sit under palms wrapped in fairy lights, order from a full North Indian menu, and walk through the fairy-light tunnel afterwards. We can't promise private dining or a candle set-up, so here is what we do offer.

## What we can promise, and what we can't

Red Wood Farm is a family restaurant first and a party lawn second. On most evenings other families are dining nearby, and some nights a party is booked on the lawn. We don't have a private dining area, and we don't arrange candle light dinners.

What you do get is the garden itself:

- round tables under palm trees
- low lounge seating under string lights
- palms along the driveway wrapped in fairy lights
- the walk-through fairy-light tunnel over a red carpet
- the green neon RED WOOD FARM sign

If a quiet evening matters to you, ask us whether a party is booked on your date. Then pick another night if one is.

## Candle light dinner for couples in Ludhiana: our honest answer

Plenty of couples search for a candle light dinner. We don't sell one. Our light comes from fairy lights in the trees, string lights over the lounge seating and lamp posts along the garden paths. It's warm and soft after dark. If you want to bring a small candle for your own table, ask us first.

## Choosing your table

**Under the palms.** A round table beside an uplit palm is the most photographed spot for couples. It feels set apart from the rest of the lawn without being private.

**Low lounge seating.** These seats sit lower under string lights and suit a long, slow meal with plenty of talking.

**When to arrive.** Come just after sunset so you see the lights come up. In the cooler months that is early evening, which also leaves time for photos in the tunnel before you order.

**What to wear.** Ludhiana evenings from November to February get cold on an open lawn. Bring a shawl or a jacket, even if the afternoon was warm.

## What to order for two

All prices are from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) and include GST. Many main dishes come in Half and Full portions, and a half portion with breads usually suits two people.

**To start, pick one:**

- Paneer Tikka (₹375) or Tandoori Chicken (₹375)
- Veg Sizzler (₹395) or Non-Veg Sizzler (₹475), which arrive on a hot plate and feel like an occasion

**Mains:**

## Put the mother-to-be's comfort first

Every other choice follows from this one.

- **Daytime works best.** A late-morning or early-afternoon start means she can rest before and get home well before evening.
- **A real chair.** Our lawn has dining tables and low lounge seating. Ask for a regular dining chair for her, because low seats are hard to rise from late in pregnancy.
- **Keep her in one place.** Seat her near the table where gifts are opened and the cake is cut, so guests come to her.
- **Mind the season.** In the hot months, a late-morning start is kinder than mid-afternoon. In winter, the midday sun on the lawn is pleasant.
- **Plan the walk.** Guests reach the lawn along garden paths and grass, and there is no wheelchair access.
- **Two to three hours is enough.** Long enough for food, a few games and photos.
- **Let her choose.** The guest list, the games and the menu should suit her, not the loudest aunt.

## What is a normal budget for a baby shower?

There is no single normal figure. The total depends mostly on how many people come, because food for each guest is usually the biggest cost. Decoration, the cake and small return gifts come next.

Start by fixing the guest count, then set a ceiling for each of those four items. A small lunch and a large party are different budgets, even at the same venue.

We don't publish package or per-plate prices. As a reference, our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists every dish with its exact price, GST included. Send your date and guest count and we'll talk through options.

## In which month is a baby shower usually held?

Many families hold it in the third trimester, often around the seventh month, when the pregnancy shows but going out is still manageable. Customs differ from family to family and between communities, so follow what your own family prefers. If the mother-to-be has been told to rest, check with her doctor before fixing the date.

## Who usually pays for a baby shower?

There is no fixed rule. Sometimes close friends or a sister host it. Sometimes it's one set of grandparents-to-be, and sometimes the couple hosts it themselves. Agree on it early in the family group chat, so the bill doesn't become a surprise on the day.

## Games and small touches

Keep games gentle and seated. A few that work at any baby shower:

- **Wishes jar.** Guests write a wish for the baby on a slip of paper. The parents read them later.
- **Bump guess.** Each guest cuts a length of ribbon to the size they think fits around the bump. The closest one wins.
- **Parents' baby photos.** Show one baby photo of each parent and let guests guess whose features the baby will get.
- **Advice cards.** Every guest writes one practical tip for the first month.

For more quick games, see our page of [kitty party games and themes](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/kitty-party-themes-and-games/). Most of them adapt well.

## Birthday Party Budget Planning: A Method That Holds Up
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/birthday-party-budget/

A birthday party budget is your confirmed headcount multiplied by the venue's per-plate quote, plus decor, cake, return gifts and a buffer for late changes. Get every quote in writing with the same questions answered. Red Wood Farm shares per-plate prices, and our à la carte prices are public on the menu page.

Q: What is a normal budget for a birthday party in Ludhiana?
A: There's no honest single figure. The total depends almost entirely on how many people come and the per-plate rate, so collect two or three written quotes for your guest count and compare them line by line.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm publish per-plate prices?
A: No. Per-plate prices are shared on 096467 13555 once you send your date, time and guest count. Our à la carte menu prices are public on the menu page.

Q: Do Red Wood Farm menu prices include GST?
A: Yes. Every price on our menu includes GST. When you get a per-plate quote from any venue, ask in writing whether tax is included.

Q: How can I keep a birthday party budget low?
A: Cut the guest list first, because every head multiplies the food cost. After that, keep decor to one photo spot, order one cake that fits the real headcount, and skip extras guests won't notice.

The simplest way to budget a birthday party is one line of arithmetic: confirmed guests multiplied by the venue's per-plate quote, plus decor, plus the cake, plus extras like return gifts, plus a buffer of about 10 percent for late additions. Food usually takes the biggest share, so the headcount drives everything else.

## The formula, term by term

Write it down before you call anyone:

**Total = (guests × per-plate quote) + decor + cake + extras + buffer**

- **Guests.** Use the number you expect to show up. The invite list is always longer than the turnout. Count children separately, because some venues quote a different rate for them.
- **Per-plate quote.** The price the venue gives for one person's food. Ask exactly what it includes: how many starters, main dishes, breads and desserts.
- **Decor.** Balloons, a backdrop, a name board, table flowers. Find out whether the venue arranges it or you bring your own decorator.
- **Cake.** Priced by weight at most bakeries. Order for the guests who will actually eat it.
- **Extras.** Return gifts, a photographer, a music system, printed invitations, cab fares for older relatives.
- **Buffer.** Somebody always brings a cousin. A buffer stops that from breaking the plan.

Say 40 guests confirm and the per-plate quote is P. Food alone is 40 × P. If 6 more people arrive, that's 6 × P you didn't plan for. That's why the buffer exists.

## How do you count heads honestly?

Send the invitation with a clear reply-by date, then make your own list from the replies. A group-chat poll with "coming", "not coming" and "maybe" options makes the count easier to read.

Treat every "maybe" as half a guest when you estimate. Ask parents of small children whether the kids are coming. Then give the venue a final number a few days before the party and ask what happens if the count goes up or down after that.

## How to get quotes you can compare

Venues quote in different ways, which makes comparing them hard. Fix that by sending every venue the same written message with the same questions:

1. Date, time slot and expected guest count.
2. What exactly is in the per-plate menu, dish by dish.
3. Is tax included in the quoted rate.
4. How long the slot is, and what an extra hour costs.
5. Is decor included, and if not, can you bring your own decorator.
6. Can you bring an outside cake.
7. Is there a charge for music or a speaker.
8. What changes if the guest count drops or rises.

Ask for the answers, in writing. A quote you can scroll back to is worth more than one you heard on a call. Lay the replies side by side in a notebook or spreadsheet, one row per venue, and the real differences show up fast.

## Where do party costs hide?

Most budgets go over in the same places:

- **Tax added on top** of a per-plate rate that looked lower than the rest.
- **Extra starters** ordered on the day because the first round ran out.
- **Overtime** when the party runs past the slot.
- **Decor upgrades** that start as one balloon arch and become a full stage.
- **Cake delivery** charges, or a second cake for the office group that turned up.
- **Return gifts** for more children than you planned for.
- **Guest travel.** A venue on the edge of the city can mean cab fares for relatives who don't drive.
- **Late plus-ones**, which the buffer should cover.

Go through this list against each quote before you pick a venue. Our [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/party-planning-checklist/) helps with food quantities per guest.

## When à la carte is simpler for a small party

For a small family birthday, ordering from a menu can be easier than a per-plate deal, because every price is already known. Here is how the arithmetic works on a sample order from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/):

| Dish | Price |
|---|---|
| Paneer Tikka | ₹375 |
| Tandoori Chicken | ₹375 |
| Dal Makhni | ₹275 |
| Kadhai Paneer, full | ₹375 |
| Butter Chicken, full | ₹695 |
| Jeera Rice | ₹230 |
| Butter Naan × 10 | ₹45 each |
| Gulab Jamun × 8 | ₹35 each |
| **Total for this order** | **₹3,055** |

Our prices include GST, so that total is the food bill for that order. How far it stretches depends on the group, so ask us how many people each dish usually serves before you lock the order.

## How do you choose a birthday venue in Ludhiana?

Search results for this lean on directory sites that list banquet halls, cafes and lawns side by side. They are useful for names. They rarely tell you what the evening will feel like. Cut the list down with a few plain checks:

- **Count heads first.** A party for 20 children usually brings parents, siblings and a grandparent or two. Add a few seats for them.
- **Choose lunch or evening.** Young children tend to cope better at lunch, before they get tired. Adult birthdays suit the evening, when lights do much of the decorating on a lawn.
- **Ask where you will actually sit.** A private corner, a shared dining room and an open lawn are very different for a group.
- **Check the drive.** If most guests live in Dugri or Sarabha Nagar, a venue on their side of the city saves arguments.
- **Get the menu in writing.** Prices, veg and non-veg marks, and whether GST is included.

## Birthday party places with price: what to ask

Most venues in the city quote a price per guest, often bundled with decoration, that moves with the date and the guest count. Before you compare quotes, ask each venue what is included: starters, dessert, decoration, the time slot and taxes. Two quotes that look far apart often cover different things.

At Red Wood Farm the party price depends on the menu you pick and how many guests come, so we quote it for your date. ## Biryani at Red Wood Farm

Biryani is rice cooked with spiced meat or vegetables, usually layered and finished with steam so the flavors soak into every grain. It is a meal in itself, which makes it an easy order when you don't want to share a spread of curries.

- **Veg Biryani, ₹325.** Marked veg.
- **Non-Veg Biryani, ₹375.** Marked non-veg. The menu doesn't name the meat, so ask us if you want to know before you order.

Biryani works well for a quick lunch on the lawn, and it travels well for takeaway too. Order by phone or message and collect it from us at the time you choose.

## Every rice dish and its price

| Dish | Mark | Price |
|---|---|---|
| Steamed Rice | Veg | ₹180 |
| Jeera Rice | Veg | ₹230 |
| Matar Pulao | Veg | ₹260 |
| Veg Pulao | Veg | ₹275 |
| Cheese Pulao | Veg | ₹280 |
| Veg Biryani | Veg | ₹325 |
| Chicken Fried Rice | Non-veg | ₹320 |
| Non-Veg Biryani | Non-veg | ₹375 |

None of the rice dishes has a Half size.

## What is the difference between pulao and biryani?

Pulao is usually cooked in one pot with lighter spicing, so the rice stays the main flavor. Biryani is spiced more heavily and is often layered, with the meat or vegetables cooked separately first. In practice, pulao is a side for a curry and biryani is a dish on its own.

Our pulaos are named for what goes in:

- **Matar Pulao:** rice with green peas.
- **Veg Pulao:** rice with mixed vegetables.
- **Cheese Pulao:** rice with cheese.
- **Jeera Rice:** rice tempered with cumin seeds, the simplest flavored rice on the list.

Steamed Rice is plain boiled rice with nothing added. At ₹180 it costs the least, and it suits any dish with plenty of gravy, from Kadhi Pakoda to Manchurian Gravy. If you only need rice to carry a curry, pick this one.

## Which rice goes with which dish?

Matching rice to the main dish makes a better plate. Every dish below is on our menu.

### With dal

Jeera Rice (₹230) is the classic match for Dal Makhni (₹275) and Yellow Dal Tadka (₹245). Read more on our [dal makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/dal-makhani/).

### With rajmah and kadhi

Rajmah with rice is one of Punjab's best-loved home lunches. Order Rajmah (₹230) with Steamed Rice (₹180). Kadhi Pakoda (₹230) also goes best over plain Steamed Rice, which soaks up the yogurt gravy.

### With paneer and kofta

A pulao suits a rich gravy. Try Veg Pulao (₹275) or Matar Pulao (₹260) with Shahi Paneer (Half ₹225, Full ₹375) or Malai Kofta (₹275).

### With Indo-Chinese

Chicken Fried Rice (₹320) goes with Chicken Manchurian (₹355). For a vegetarian version, pour Manchurian Gravy (₹260) over Steamed Rice. Our [Indo-Chinese page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/indo-chinese/) lists the rest of those dishes.

### Biryani on its own

Biryani needs only a raita and perhaps a salad. Laccha Onion Salad (₹125) and Masala Papad (₹75) are the easy extras.

## Raita and curd to order with rice

The Curd & Raita section has seven choices.

| Dish | Price | What the name tells you |
|---|---|---|
| Plain Curd | ₹125 | Plain set yogurt |
| Curd Pudina Jeera | ₹145 | Yogurt with mint and cumin |
| Boondi Raita | ₹165 | Yogurt with small fried gram-flour pearls |
| Cucumber Raita | ₹165 | Yogurt with cucumber |
| Mixed Raita | ₹175 | Yogurt with mixed vegetables |
| Pineapple Raita | ₹195 | Yogurt with pineapple, on the sweet side |
| Mix Fruit Raita | ₹200 | Yogurt with mixed fruit, also sweet |

With a spicy biryani, Cucumber Raita or Curd Pudina Jeera cools each mouthful. Boondi Raita adds a little crunch. The fruit raitas are sweeter, so some people like them against a hot curry and others find them too sweet with biryani. If you can't decide, Mixed Raita is a safe middle choice.

Butter Chicken at Red Wood Farm costs ₹415 for a Half and ₹695 for a Full, GST included. It is one of 15 chicken curries in the non-veg main course at our garden restaurant on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana. Prices start at ₹325 for a Half Chicken Malai Methi and top out at ₹925 for Atta Chicken.

## What is butter chicken?

Butter chicken is a Punjabi dish of chicken in a smooth tomato gravy finished with butter and cream. The chicken is usually cooked in a tandoor first, so it brings a little smoke into the sauce. It tends to be mild and slightly sweet, which is why it often ends up as the dish everyone at the table can agree on.

On our menu, Butter Chicken sits at the same price as Chicken Tikka Butter Masala, Palak Chicken and Farm to Table Special Chicken: Half ₹415, Full ₹695. Chicken Tikka Butter Masala is the closest relative by name, with tikka pieces in a butter masala gravy.

## Our two house chicken dishes

### Farm to Table Special Chicken

The menu calls this "our house signature chicken." It costs Half ₹415 or Full ₹695. The menu doesn't spell out the recipe, so if you want to know what goes into it before you order, send us a message.

### Atta Chicken

Atta Chicken is chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough. The dough case holds the steam and juices in while it cooks. It comes in one size, a Full at ₹925, and it is the highest-priced dish anywhere on our menu. It suits a group that wants one centerpiece dish to share. If you plan your meal around it, message us before you come and we'll tell you how long it takes.

## How the curries differ, going by their names

Most of these names describe the main flavor or the pot. Here is what they usually mean in North Indian cooking.

- **Chicken Curry:** the plain, home-style gravy. A good test of a kitchen.
- **Kadhai Chicken:** cooked in a kadhai, a deep iron wok, usually with onion and capsicum and a thick gravy.
- **Chicken Kali Mirch:** black pepper is the lead spice.
- **Chicken Malai Methi:** cream with fenugreek leaves, which add a slightly bitter, herby note.
- **Palak Chicken:** chicken in a spinach gravy.
- **Lemon Chicken:** lemon gives this one its sharpness.
- **Chicken Handi:** named for the handi, a deep cooking pot.
- **Chicken Tikka Lababdar:** pieces of chicken tikka in a lababdar gravy.

Rara Chicken, Barmi Chicken and Lahori Chicken have names that don't describe the gravy on their own. Ask us and we'll explain each one.

If you like your chicken dry and smoky, skip the curries and look at the Tandoori section. Tandoori Chicken costs ₹375 there. Our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/tandoor-guide/) covers it with the kebabs.

## What to eat with chicken curry

### Breads

Butter Naan (₹45) and Garlic Naan (₹55) are the natural match for Butter Chicken because they soak up the gravy. Roomali Roti (₹30) is thin and soft, good with drier dishes like Kadhai Chicken. Laccha Paratha (₹45) has flaky layers. All 14 breads are in our [Indian breads guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/indian-breads/).

### Rice and sides

- Jeera Rice, ₹230
- Steamed Rice, ₹180
- Non-Veg Biryani, ₹375, if you want rice as a dish of its own
- Boondi Raita, ₹165
- Laccha Onion Salad, ₹125

### Something for the vegetarians at the table

Dal Makhni (₹275) and Paneer Butter Masala (Half ₹225, Full ₹345) work well alongside chicken for a mixed group. Both sit in the vegetarian main course.

If you'd like mutton, the Mutton section starts with Mutton Rogan Josh at Half ₹345 and Full ₹645.

## Should you order a Half or a Full?

We don't publish how many people each portion serves. The price gap is a useful guide: a Full Butter Chicken at ₹695 costs ₹280 more than a Half at ₹415. Two Halves of different curries let a small table try more dishes. For bigger groups, tell us the number of people and we'll suggest a mix. The [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/group-ordering-guide/) explains how to plan Half and Full portions.

## Lunch in the winter sun or dinner under the lights?

December in Ludhiana shapes when you eat outdoors. Afternoons can be pleasant in the sun, though fog is common in Punjab in late December, and evenings turn cold fast.

### Christmas lunch

A lunch from noon gives you daylight and easier photos of the children. In daytime the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating. A family that wants a slow day can stay for two or three hours and finish with dessert as the light fades.

### Christmas dinner

After dark the garden looks most like the season. The walk-through tunnel has warm white fairy lights over a red carpet, the palms along the driveway are wrapped in lights, and the lawn has low seating under string lights. On a December evening, that is the backdrop most families want for a Christmas photo. Bring warm layers, because the lawn is open air.

## What goes on the table without a Christmas menu?

We don't run a special Christmas menu, so plan the meal from the regular one. That has one advantage: you know every price before you arrive, and each one includes GST. A Christmas table from our menu could run like this.

## Dal Makhani in Ludhiana: Dal Makhni at Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/dal-makhani/

In short: Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana serves Dal Makhni at ₹275 for one Full portion, GST included. Pair it with Butter Naan (₹45), Laccha Paratha (₹45) or Jeera Rice (₹230). We are open every day from 10 AM to 11 PM, and you can order it for takeaway at 096467 13555.

Q: How much does dal makhani cost at Red Wood Farm?
A: Dal Makhni is ₹275 for one Full portion, and the price includes GST. The menu does not list a Half size for it.

Q: Is Dal Makhni vegetarian at Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes. Dal Makhni carries the green veg mark on our menu, as do all the other dals: Yellow Dal Tadka, Dal Missi Tadka and Dal Handi.

Q: Can I get dal makhani for takeaway?
A: Yes. Order by phone or message on 096467 13555, tell us the time you will collect it, and pick it up from 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road.

Q: Why is the menu spelling Dal Makhni and not dal makhani?
A: Both spellings mean the same dish. Our printed menu spells it Dal Makhni, so use that name when you order.

Dal Makhni costs ₹275 at Red Wood Farm, our garden family restaurant on Pakhowal Road in Ludhiana. That is the price for one Full portion with GST included; the menu has no Half size for it. Eat it on the lawn with Butter Naan at ₹45, or order it for takeaway by phone or message on 096467 13555.

## What is dal makhani?

Dal makhani is a slow-cooked lentil dish from Punjab. It is usually made with whole black lentils and a smaller share of kidney beans, simmered for a long time and finished with butter and cream. The long cooking makes it thick and dark brown, with a soft, almost silky texture. The name itself refers to the butter.

On our menu the dish is spelled Dal Makhni, so look for that name when you order. If you want to know how our kitchen cooks it, or how spicy it is on a given day, ask us and we'll tell you.

## Which state is famous for dal makhani?

Punjab. Dal makhani grew up in the same North Indian kitchens as the tandoor, and it is often served at Punjabi weddings, family dinners and festival meals. Around Ludhiana it is a regular on restaurant menus, and many families also cook a version of it at home for Sundays and guests.

Because it comes from this region, people here tend to have firm opinions about it. Some like it smoky and heavy on butter. Others want it lighter with more bite left in the lentils. Try ours and tell us what you think.

## How much dal makhani per person?

For a home party where dal is one of several dishes, a common rule of thumb is one small side bowl per adult. Plan for more if dal and rice are the main meal. Plan for less when two or three other gravies share the table.

At Red Wood Farm the menu lists Dal Makhni in one Full size only. We haven't published how many people a Full portion serves, so send us your group size and we'll suggest how many to order. If you are hosting something bigger at home or on our lawn, our [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/party-planning-checklist/) covers food per guest across the whole meal.

## Is dal makhani healthy?

It depends on how much you eat and what goes with it. The lentils and beans give plant protein and fiber. The butter and cream add a lot of fat and calories, which is where the rich taste comes from. Many families keep it for weekends and celebrations and eat plainer dal during the week.

If you want to keep the meal lighter at our place, a few choices help:

- Pair it with Tandoori Roti (₹20) in place of a buttered naan.
- Add a Green Salad (₹125) or Plain Curd (₹125).
- Share one Full portion across the table and add a second, plainer dal such as Yellow Dal Tadka (₹245).

This is general information. If you follow a diet for a health condition, check with your doctor.

## Which other dals are on the menu?

Dal Makhni is one of seven lentil and bean dishes in our vegetarian main course. Each comes in a single Full size.

| Dish | Price | What the name tells you |
|---|---|---|
| Dal Makhni | ₹275 | Black lentils finished with butter and cream |
| Yellow Dal Tadka | ₹245 | Yellow lentils topped with spices tempered in hot fat |
| Dal Missi Tadka | ₹245 | A dal with a tempering; ask us which lentils go in |
| Dal Handi | ₹245 | Named for the handi, a deep cooking pot |
| Rajmah | ₹230 | Kidney beans in gravy, a Punjabi home lunch |
| Chana Masala | ₹275 | Chickpeas in a spiced gravy |
| Kadhi Pakoda | ₹230 | Yogurt and gram-flour curry with fritters |

All seven carry the green veg mark. For the rest of the meat-free menu, see our [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/vegetarian-guide/).

## What goes well with Dal Makhni?

### Breads

A thick dal needs a bread that can scoop. Butter Naan (₹45) and Garlic Naan (₹55) are the usual picks. Laccha Paratha (₹45) is layered and flaky, so it soaks up the gravy well. Missi Roti (₹30) brings its own spice. Our [guide to Indian breads](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/indian-breads/) lists all 14 with prices.

### Rice

Jeera Rice (₹230) is the classic partner, and Steamed Rice (₹180) works if you want the dal to carry all the flavor. More pairings are on our [biryani and rice page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/biryani-and-rice/).

### On the side

- Laccha Onion Salad, ₹125
- Boondi Raita, ₹165
- Masala Papad, ₹75
- Farm to Table Special Herbs Chutney, ₹75, our own herb chutney made in the house

Dal Makhni sits well beside a paneer or chicken gravy. Kadhai Paneer costs Half ₹225 or Full ₹375. Butter Chicken costs Half ₹415 or Full ₹695. One easy order for a small table is one dal, one gravy and a few mixed breads.

## Why couples pick a garden over a mall food court

- palms along the driveway wrapped in fairy lights
- trees wrapped in lights near the tables
- lamp posts along the stone garden paths
- string lights over the low lounge seating
- the green neon RED WOOD FARM sign near the entrance

## What to know before you book

Red Wood Farm is a family restaurant first. Families eat at the next table, and on some evenings a party is booked on part of the lawn. We don't have private cabins, closed rooms or a candle set-up. If a calm evening matters, message us at 096467 13555 and ask whether anything is booked on your date, then pick the night that suits you.

The tables are outdoors. From November to February, Ludhiana evenings on an open lawn turn cold after dark, so bring a jacket or a shawl even if the afternoon was warm. In the summer months, a later booking is cooler.

## A simple plan for the evening

**Arrive just before sunset.** You see the lights come on one string at a time, and the garden paths are easy to walk while there is still some daylight.

**Walk the tunnel first.** The fairy-light tunnel over the red carpet is where most guests take photos. It is less busy early in the evening. Our [tunnel page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/fairy-light-tunnel/) has a few tips for photos on a phone.

**Pick your table.** A round table beside an uplit palm feels a little set apart from the rest of the lawn. The low lounge seating under string lights suits a long, unhurried meal.

**Order in two rounds.** Start with something from the tandoor, then decide on mains once you have settled in. The kitchen cooks to order, so there is no need to order everything at once.

## Dinner for two, with real prices

All prices are from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) and include GST.

### A vegetarian dinner for two (about ₹890)

- Paneer Tikka, ₹375
- Dal Makhni, ₹275
- two Butter Naan at ₹45 each
- two Paneer Jalebi with Rabri at ₹75 each

- Butter Chicken in a Half portion, ₹415
- two Garlic Naan at ₹55 each

If you share well, the Half portions on many main-course dishes keep the bill down without leaving either of you hungry. Our guide to [what to order on a first visit](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/first-visit-what-to-order/) has more pairings.

## A birthday dinner for two

Birthday celebrations for couples are one of the most common reasons people book an evening table with us. Tell us it is a birthday when you message. If you want to bring a cake, ask first so we can tell you what works on that evening. We don't sell decoration packages, and we won't promise a set-up we haven't confirmed for your date.

For a bigger family birthday on the lawn, see our [birthday party guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/birthday-party-venues-ludhiana/) instead.

## Anniversaries and other evenings

If the occasion is an anniversary, our [anniversary dinner guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/anniversary-dinner-ludhiana/) covers table choice and what to expect in more detail. For a regular evening out with no occasion at all, [an evening on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/an-evening-on-the-lawn/) describes what the garden is like after dark.

## Getting here

You will find us on outer Pakhowal Road at VPO Daad, across from Cerajot Tiles. The drive is about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar and about 6.5 km from Dugri. Leave extra time on weekend evenings, when Pakhowal Road is busier. The [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/) has directions and a map. Note that the venue has no wheelchair access.

## Diwali Get-Together Venue in Ludhiana for Families and Offices
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/diwali-get-together/

Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road hosts family and office Diwali get-togethers on a garden lawn lit with fairy lights. The menu has Indian sweets such as Gulab Jamun at ₹35 and Paneer Jalebi with Rabri at ₹75, with GST included. Book at 096467 13555 and confirm timings for the festival days.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm open on Diwali day?
A: Our regular hours are 10 AM to 11 PM every day. For the festival day itself, confirm at 096467 13555 before you plan.

Q: Can we order Diwali sweets as takeaway?
A: Takeaway is available by phone or message. The desserts on the menu include Gulab Jamun, Rasmalai, Raj Bhog and Kesar Kheer; ask us which ones you can take away and in what quantity.

Q: Can an office book a Diwali lunch for its team?
A: Yes. Send the date, time and team size. You order from the regular menu, and every price includes GST.

For a Diwali get-together in Ludhiana, Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road offers a garden lawn strung with fairy lights, a menu of North Indian dishes and Indian sweets, and space for a family or an office group. Gulab Jamun is ₹35 and Paneer Jalebi with Rabri is ₹75, GST included. Book at 096467 13555.

## When do people hold Diwali get-togethers?

Most families spend the festival night itself at home, with prayers, visits to relatives and boxes of sweets going from door to door. The get-togethers happen around it. Offices hold a party in the week before. Friends meet for lunch on the weekend. The extended family sits down to dinner a day or two after, once the visiting is done.

If you can, pick a date other than the festival night. Guests are freer, and you aren't competing with every family's own plans. Our regular hours are 10 AM to 11 PM every day. For the festival days themselves, confirm timings with us.

## Family dinner or office party?

### A family Diwali dinner

Families usually want an evening, and the garden's own lights do much of the decorating. There is a walk-through tunnel of warm white fairy lights, palms along the driveway wrapped in lights, more trees wrapped in lights and lamp posts along the garden paths. Arrive just after dark and the place is already glowing.

Grandparents should know before they come that Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access.

### An office Diwali party

Offices tend to prefer lunch on a working day close to the festival, as a thank-you to the staff. An afternoon on the lawn gets the team out of the building for a few hours, and the long wooden tables set out in daytime let everyone sit together. For more on weekday groups, see [office team lunches](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/office-team-lunch-ludhiana/).

## Which Diwali sweets are on the menu?

Sweets sit at the center of Diwali, and our dessert list has several Indian classics. All prices include GST.

| Dessert | Price |
|---|---|
| Gulab Jamun | ₹35 |
| Rasmalai | ₹45 |
| Raj Bhog | ₹55 |
| Kheer | ₹65 |
| Paneer Jalebi with Rabri | ₹75 |
| Kesar Kheer | ₹75 |

Gajrela (100 g) at ₹75 and Malpua Rabri at ₹65 are marked seasonal, so check whether they are on for your date. To make the dessert course feel festive, order two or three different sweets for each table so everyone gets a taste of each. Our [desserts guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/desserts/) has more on Indian desserts.

## What savory food suits a festive table?

Many Punjabi households keep the festival day vegetarian, while the parties around it often include chicken. For a mixed group, build a vegetarian-heavy spread and add one or two non-veg dishes.

**Vegetarian:** Paneer Tikka (₹375), Mushroom Tikka (₹395), Shahi Paneer (₹225 half, ₹375 full), Dal Makhni (₹275), Veg Biryani (₹325), Garlic Naan (₹55) and Mixed Raita (₹175).

**Non-veg:** Bhatti Da Murg (₹395), Non-Veg Biryani (₹375) and Farm to Table Special Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full), our house signature chicken.

Every dish on the [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) carries a veg or non-veg mark, which helps when part of the family keeps the festival vegetarian.

## How do you run the evening from arrival to dessert?

A Diwali get-together runs more smoothly with a loose order to it. Here is one way to plan a family evening on the lawn.

- **Arrive around dusk.** The lights come into their own as the sky darkens, and guests get photos in their festive clothes while there is still a little light.
- **Photos first.** Walk the family through the fairy-light tunnel before anyone sits down. Once the food arrives, nobody wants to get up.
- **Starters while people trickle in.** Order a Tandoori Veg Platter (₹525) or Paneer Tikka (₹375) so early arrivals have something to share.
- **Mains once the last car is in.** Call for the dal, the curries and the breads when the whole family is seated.
- **Sweets last, and slowly.** Order the desserts as a separate round, so they arrive as the centerpiece of the evening.

Share this plan when you book, and we will tell you what works on the day.

## Can we bring our own sweets, gifts or decorations?

Many offices hand out gift boxes at their Diwali party, and families sometimes bring a box of sweets from a favorite shop. Tell us what you plan to bring, and we will tell you what is possible for your date. The same goes for any decoration beyond what the garden already has.

## Booking a Diwali get-together

Send your preferred date, time and guest count to 096467 13555, or call. Message early in the festival weeks so you still have a choice of dates, and say whether it is a family dinner or an office lunch. For more of the lit garden, see the [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/), and for other events, the [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Dugri to Daad: Driving to Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/from-dugri/

Red Wood Farm is about 6.5 km from Dugri by road. OSRM sends you along Phase 1 Road and Jawadi Road, which meets outer Pakhowal Road for the last 2.8 km to Daad, in about 12 minutes with no traffic. Look for Cerajot Tiles; we are opposite.

Q: Is Dugri the closest Ludhiana neighborhood to Red Wood Farm?
A: Of the starting points we checked with OSRM, Dugri is the shortest by road at 6.5 km. Sarabha Nagar (6.8 km) and Model Town (6.9 km) are close behind.

Q: Does the Dugri route use inner Pakhowal Road?
A: No. OSRM's route goes along Phase 1 Road and Jawadi Road and only joins Pakhowal Road on its outer stretch, which OpenStreetMap labels Jodhan - Ludhiana Road.

Q: What time does Red Wood Farm close?
A: We are open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM every day.

Q: How do I book a table if I am coming from Dugri?
A: Send your date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call the same number. Bookings are made by phone or message only.

Dugri is about 6.5 km from Red Wood Farm by road, the shortest of the city routes we checked. OSRM takes you along Phase 1 Road, then Jawadi Road, which meets the outer stretch of Pakhowal Road for the final 2.8 km to Daad. The estimate is about 12 minutes with no traffic, so leave a little extra.

## How the Dugri route differs from the others

Most routes from central Ludhiana run up inner Pakhowal Road and follow it out of the city. Dugri's route doesn't. According to OSRM, you cut across on Jawadi Road and join Pakhowal Road only on its outer stretch, the part OpenStreetMap labels "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road". That means you skip the inner city section of Pakhowal Road altogether.

There is one surprise in the numbers. Dugri is the shortest trip by distance, yet OSRM gives it 12 minutes, one minute more than Sarabha Nagar or Model Town. OSRM assigns different speeds to different kinds of road, and it expects a slower average on this route: about 6.5 km in 12 minutes, against 6.8 km in 11 from [Sarabha Nagar](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-sarabha-nagar/). In real traffic the gap may go either way.

## Roads in order

Checked with OSRM on 17 Nov 2026, using OpenStreetMap road names:

- **Phase 1 Road, about 1.1 km.** You head out of Dugri on this road.
- **Jawadi Road, about 1.7 km.** The connecting leg. It carries you across to Pakhowal Road without entering the inner city stretch. This is the turn to watch. If you miss it, let your navigation reroute you. You may end up on inner Pakhowal Road instead, which also leads out to Daad, only with a little more distance and more junctions.
- **Jodhan - Ludhiana Road, about 2.8 km.** Outer Pakhowal Road, the last leg before our gate.

The three named roads come to about 5.6 km. OSRM's full figure of 6.5 km also includes the streets inside Dugri and short links at junctions that it doesn't name. OSRM started from the point OpenStreetMap treats as the center of Dugri, so your own street may add or remove a few hundred meters.

## Timing your drive

The 12-minute estimate assumes zero traffic. It is a fair guide early in the day and a poor one at peak hours. If you are meeting family for lunch or arriving before guests at a party, allow extra time so you are not the one running late. We are open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day, so you can plan around the busy hours.

## The last 2.8 km and the gate

When Jawadi Road brings you onto outer Pakhowal Road, you are on the final leg. Keep an eye out for:

1. **Omaxe Flats (Omaxe Royal Residency).** OSRM puts it about 0.8 km from us by road.
2. **Daad village.** It appears as "Dad" on OpenStreetMap and lies under a kilometer from our pin.
3. **Cerajot Tiles.** Red Wood Farm is directly opposite.

Turn in at our garden gate. The green hedge arch with flowers marks the way in, and once inside you will find the "Red Wood Farm" name arch and the paths through the garden.

Please note that Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. If anyone in your group uses a wheelchair, plan ahead.

Coming back after dinner, the same roads in reverse take you home: outer Pakhowal Road, Jawadi Road, then Phase 1 Road into Dugri. Your app may choose otherwise at night, and that is fine too.

## No car: cab or auto from Dugri

A cab or an auto booked on an app is an easy option for a 6.5 km ride. Some drivers may know Pakhowal Road well but not this outer stretch. To avoid a wrong turn, ask us on 096467 13555 to share our location and pass the pin to your driver before you set off.

## Making a trip of it

Because the drive is short, it is easy to treat the trip as an outing rather than a journey. There is open grass on the lawn for children to move about, and the fairy-light tunnel is the spot guests photograph most. For ideas on a half day out with children, read [family outings with kids](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/family-outing-with-kids/). Hungry already: the [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists all 187 dishes with exact prices, and every price includes GST. For a table or a party, send your date, time and guest count to 096467 13555, or call the same number. All other routes are on the [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Farm to table in Ludhiana: what the term means at Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/farm-to-table/

In short: Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant on outer Pakhowal Road, and Farm to Table Special Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full) is the name of our house signature dish. We do not claim to grow our own produce or to buy from named farms, because that is not confirmed. If sourcing matters to you, ask us about the dish you plan to order.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm grow its own vegetables?
A: We have not confirmed that, so we do not claim it. If you want to know where a particular ingredient comes from, ask us at 096467 13555.

Q: What is Farm to Table Special Chicken?
A: It is our house signature chicken, priced at ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full, GST included. For recipe or allergy questions, message us before you order.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm a working farm?
A: Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant and party lawn at VPO Daad on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana. The word farm is part of our name.

Q: Are the prices on the Red Wood Farm menu inclusive of GST?
A: Yes. Every price on our menu includes GST, from ₹20 for a Tandoori Roti to ₹925 for Atta Chicken.

If you are searching for a farm to table restaurant in Ludhiana, here is the honest picture. Red Wood Farm is a garden restaurant on outer Pakhowal Road, and Farm to Table Special Chicken is the name of our house dish (₹415 half, ₹695 full). We do not claim to grow our own produce or source from named farms.

## What does "farm to table" usually mean?

The phrase describes a way of running a kitchen. In its strict sense, a farm to table restaurant buys its main ingredients straight from nearby growers, with few or no middlemen in between. The menu shifts with the harvest. Staff can tell you which farm the vegetables, milk or meat came from, and some restaurants grow part of their produce on their own land.

In everyday use the term is much looser. Around the world, plenty of places use it for a rustic look, a garden setting or a menu with fresh salads. On a sign or a menu, the words alone tell you very little. The useful question is always what a particular restaurant can show you.

## Why the name appears on our menu

Two items on the Red Wood Farm menu carry the label:

- **Farm to Table Special Chicken,** our house signature chicken, ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full.
- **Farm to Table Special Herbs Chutney,** our own herb chutney, made in the house, ₹75.

These are dish names. They point to the house recipe and the garden we serve it in. They are not a sourcing promise, and we would rather say that plainly than let the name do work it has not earned.

The same goes for the word in our own name. Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant and party lawn at VPO Daad, near Daad village. You eat on a lawn, walk a stone path through the grounds and sit under palms wrapped in lights. One guest, gurvinder kaur, wrote in a Google review that it "felt like close to nature". That is the honest appeal of the place.

## What you can expect at Red Wood Farm

- **A garden setting.** An open grass lawn with dining tables, trees, a stone path and, in the evening, fairy lights and string lights.
- **Our own house dishes.** Farm to Table Special Chicken, the herb chutney, and Atta Chicken at ₹925, which is chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough.
- **A clear menu.** 187 dishes with prices that include GST, and every dish marked veg or non-veg.
- **Honest seasonal marks.** Saag, Bhindi, Gajrela, Malpua Rabri and the whole fish section are marked seasonal, so they are not available all year. Ask us before you come for one of them.

## What you should not expect

- **A list of named farms or suppliers.** We have not published one.
- **Vegetables grown on the premises.** We do not say that we grow produce here.
- **Organic claims.** We make none.
- **A working farm visit.** The grounds are a garden restaurant and party lawn.

A few menu names sound farm-fresh too, such as the Garden Fresh Kachumber at ₹125. Read those as the name of a salad, in the same spirit as the chicken.

## How to ask about ingredients

If where your food comes from matters to you, because of an allergy, a diet or a guest with strict rules, message us at 096467 13555 before your visit. Ask about the exact dish you have in mind, and we will tell you what we can confirm.

One example of how we handle unknowns: the Ice Cream with Brownie is marked non-veg on our menu until the egg question is confirmed. When we are unsure, the menu marks it the cautious way. You can read more about how the marks work on our page about [veg and non-veg marks and GST](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/menu-marks-and-gst/).

## What to order if the name brought you here

Start with the dish itself. A half Farm to Table Special Chicken at ₹415 with a Garlic Naan at ₹55 and the herb chutney at ₹75 is a fair first try. For a bigger table, add a full portion at ₹695, or order Atta Chicken at ₹925 as the centrepiece. Ask how long it takes when you order. Our page on [chicken curries](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/chicken-curries/) compares it with Butter Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full) and the rest of the section.

Vegetarians at the same table can share Paneer Lababdar (₹255 half, ₹395 full), Dal Makhni at ₹275 and a Garden Fresh Kachumber. Our [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/vegetarian-guide/) has more ideas, and the [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists every price.

## Visiting and booking

Our address is 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana 142022. Look for us opposite Cerajot Tiles, a short way from Omaxe Flats. We are open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, seven days a week. For a table, send your date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555. More about the lawn and the grounds is on our [garden page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Ferozepur Road to Pakhowal Road: Reaching Red Wood Farm from Bharat Nagar Chowk
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/from-ferozepur-road/

From Bharat Nagar Chowk on Ferozepur Road, Red Wood Farm is about 9.5 km by road, around 14 minutes with no traffic according to OSRM. You follow Ferozepur Road for about 1.5 km, cross to Pakhowal Road, and stay on it out of the city to Daad. We are opposite Cerajot Tiles.

Q: Where does Ferozepur Road meet Pakhowal Road?
A: In OSRM's route from Bharat Nagar Chowk, you leave Ferozepur Road for Pakhowal Road after about 1.5 km (0.6 km on the flyover and 0.9 km on Ferozepur Road).

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from Bharat Nagar Chowk?
A: About 9.5 km by road. OSRM estimates about 14 minutes without traffic, so allow more at peak hours.

Q: I am starting farther out on Ferozepur Road. How do I work out the distance?
A: Add your distance to Bharat Nagar Chowk to our 9.5 km figure, or ask us on 096467 13555 to share our location and let your maps app measure it.

Q: Can Red Wood Farm host an office lunch for a team on Ferozepur Road?
A: Yes, team lunches are booked by message or phone with the date, time and number of guests. Ask us for anything beyond the menu.

From Bharat Nagar Chowk on Ferozepur Road, Red Wood Farm is about 9.5 km by road. You follow Ferozepur Road for roughly 1.5 km, cross over to Pakhowal Road, and stay on it out of the city to Daad. OSRM puts the drive at about 14 minutes with no traffic. Leave extra time for the real thing.

## Why we measure from Bharat Nagar Chowk

Ferozepur Road is long, so "from Ferozepur Road" could mean almost anything. We picked Bharat Nagar Chowk as a fixed junction that OSRM could route from cleanly. If you start somewhere else on Ferozepur Road, the second half of this route stays the same. Only the first part changes.

## Part one: from Ferozepur Road across to Pakhowal Road

Road names below are OpenStreetMap's, from OSRM's route on 17 Nov 2026.

| Road | About |
|---|---|
| Ferozepur Road Flyover | 0.6 km |
| Ferozepur Road | 0.9 km |
| Pakhowal Road | 1.3 km |
| Satpal Mittal Road | 0.3 km |
| Krishna Mandir Road | 0.5 km |

This is the busy part of the trip. You come off the flyover, run along Ferozepur Road for under a kilometer, then switch to Pakhowal Road. OSRM then steps off Pakhowal Road for two short links, Satpal Mittal Road and Krishna Mandir Road, before putting you back on it. Our route data places Hero Bakery Chowk on Satpal Mittal Road, a useful name if you are giving directions to a driver.

Your own navigation app may take a slightly different line through these junctions depending on traffic. Follow it, as long as it brings you back onto Pakhowal Road heading out of the city.

## Part two: Pakhowal Road out to Daad

| Road | About |
|---|---|
| Pakhowal Road | 2.0 km |
| Jodhan - Ludhiana Road (outer Pakhowal Road) | 2.8 km |

The second half is simpler. You stay on Pakhowal Road for about 2 km, and then OpenStreetMap starts calling it "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road". It is still Pakhowal Road to locals and in our address. There are no more changes of road in our route data until you reach us.

The seven named stretches total about 8.4 km. OSRM's 9.5 km also counts short junction links that it doesn't list by name.

## Names to give a driver

If someone else is driving, or you are directing a guest over the phone, a short chain of names does the job. Start with Bharat Nagar Chowk, then Ferozepur Road, then Pakhowal Road. Hero Bakery Chowk and Krishna Mandir Road are the two short links in the middle. After that it is Pakhowal Road all the way out to Daad, where the last names are Omaxe Flats and Cerajot Tiles. Read in that order, they match OSRM's route from start to finish.

## Is 14 minutes realistic?

Only on empty roads. OSRM's estimate leaves out traffic entirely, and part one runs through a string of city junctions. Allow extra time at peak hours. If you are heading out after work on a weekday for a dinner booking, add a generous margin.

## Starting from the railway station instead

The railway station route joins this one early. From Ludhiana Junction, OSRM takes Ferozepur Road for about 0.8 km and then follows the same five roads that come after Ferozepur Road on this page, for 10.7 km in total. ## First Birthday Party Venue in Ludhiana: Planning Your Baby's 1st
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/first-birthday-party/

In short: a first birthday works best as a two-hour daytime party timed after the baby's nap, with comfortable seats for grandparents and a proper meal for the adults. Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road has a garden lawn and a North Indian menu from 10:00 AM daily. Book by message with your date and guest count.

Q: What time of day is best for a first birthday party?
A: Plan around your baby's naps. A late-morning or mid-afternoon slot usually goes better than a late evening, and Red Wood Farm opens at 10:00 AM every day.

Q: How long should a 1st birthday party last?
A: About two hours covers a meal, the cake and the family photos without tiring the baby out.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm easy for elderly relatives?
A: There is no wheelchair access, so let older relatives know in advance. Ask for regular dining chairs for them, since low lounge seats are harder to get up from.

Q: Do you have a first birthday package?
A: We don't publish packages. Send your date, time and number of adults and children on 096467 13555 and we'll reply with what's possible.

A first birthday party goes best as a short daytime gathering of about two hours, timed after your baby's nap, at a place where grandparents can sit comfortably and adults get a proper meal. Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road has a garden lawn and a North Indian menu from 10:00 AM daily.

## Who the party is really for

Your baby won't remember the day. The family will remember the photos, the blessings from the elders and the meal. Most guests at a first birthday are grown-ups, so plan the food, seating and timing for them. Then give your baby a calm 30 to 45 minutes in the middle for the cake and the pictures.

## How to host a 1st birthday party

1. **Fix the time around naps.** Many one-year-olds still nap once in the morning and once in the afternoon. A party that starts soon after a nap catches your baby fresh. A late evening party often ends with the guest of honour asleep before the cake.
2. **Keep it to about two hours.** That is long enough for a meal and cake, and short enough for a cheerful baby.
3. **Write the guest list by household.** Grandparents, aunts and uncles, and a few friends with babies of their own. Count adults and children separately when you message us.
4. **Choose daytime or evening.** By day the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating. After dark the string lights and the fairy-light tunnel take over. The evening looks lovely in photos, though it runs later than most babies like.
5. **Book a table.** Send the date, start time and both head counts to 096467 13555.
6. **Pack a proper baby bag.** A spare outfit (cake happens), a changing mat, wipes, a light blanket, your baby's own food and spoon, and ear muffs if there will be music.

## How to make baby's first birthday special

The moments people talk about later rarely cost much.

- **A handprint card.** Press your baby's hand in paint on a sheet of card, and ask each guest to sign around it.
- **Letters for age 18.** Hand every guest a card and envelope. They write a note for your child to open at eighteen, and you seal the lot in one box.
- **One photo with each grandparent.** Use the same spot every time, such as the flower entrance arch by day or the fairy-light tunnel after sunset. The set of matching pictures becomes a keepsake.
- **A month-by-month photo line.** Peg twelve prints, one from each month, on a string between two chairs.
- **A short cake moment.** Bring a bib and a mat, let your baby touch the cake for a minute, and then take the plate away before it ends up on Grandma.
- **Short video messages.** Ask each elder to record 30 seconds on your phone, speaking to your child.

## Seating and comfort for grandparents

Elders usually stay longest at a first birthday, so look after them first.

- Ask for a table close to where the cake is cut, so they don't need to walk across the lawn.
- Low lounge seating can be hard to get out of. Request regular dining chairs for older guests when you book.
- Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. Tell relatives in advance so nobody is caught out on the day.
- On winter evenings, bring shawls. On warm days, a table under the palm trees is a calmer spot than open grass.
- Share the location pin in the family group. We're at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles. From Model Town it's about 6.9 km, and from Sarabha Nagar about 6.8 km. Leave extra time for traffic. Directions are on our [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/).

## First Lohri celebration for a baby: planning a family evening on the lawn
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/first-lohri-celebration/

In short: a baby's first Lohri works best as an early-evening family gathering in mid-January, kept short enough for the baby, with warm food for elders and simple dishes for children. Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road hosts family gatherings on its garden lawn with food from its regular menu. For anything beyond seating and food, ask us at 096467 13555.

Q: When should we hold a baby's first Lohri?
A: Lohri falls in mid-January, usually on 13 January. Many families gather on the day itself or the weekend nearest to it. Check the exact date for the year.

Q: Is it the same celebration for a baby boy and a baby girl?
A: Yes. More and more Punjabi families celebrate a first Lohri for daughters as well as sons. The planning is the same: family, food, songs and blessings for the baby.

Q: What time is best with a small baby?
A: Start in the late afternoon or early evening and keep it to two or three hours, so the baby is home before the coldest part of the night.

Q: Can we bring our own sweets for guests?
A: Ask us first at 096467 13555. Tell us what you plan to bring and we will tell you what works on your date.

A baby's first Lohri is usually a family gathering in mid-January: grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins come together to bless the baby, sing, share winter sweets and eat a warm meal. Plan it for the late afternoon or early evening, keep it short enough for the baby, and choose food that suits both elders and children.

## Why the first Lohri matters to Punjabi families

Lohri marks the end of the coldest stretch of winter and the start of the harvest season. For a family, the first Lohri after a baby is born, or after a wedding, is a reason to invite everyone. Relatives bring blessings and small gifts, and the evening is about the new member of the family. Many families now celebrate a daughter's first Lohri with the same warmth as a son's.

## When to hold it, and for how long

Lohri usually falls on 13 January, the evening before Maghi. Some families gather on the day itself. Others pick the nearest weekend, so relatives from outside Ludhiana can travel.

With a small baby, timing matters more than anything else:

- start in the late afternoon or early evening, while it is still mild
- plan for two to three hours, not a late night
- have the blessings and songs early, when the baby is fresh
- keep a quiet corner where a parent can feed or settle the baby

## Keeping the baby comfortable on a January evening

Our tables are on an open garden lawn, and Ludhiana evenings in January are cold. Dress the baby in layers with a cap and socks, and bring a blanket for the pram or the lap. Elders feel the cold too, so tell guests in the invitation to bring a shawl or a jacket. If you want a covered area, ask us what seating is available on your date. A covered tent with chandeliers has been used at past events, and whether one suits your date is a question to ask when you book.

## First Lohri ideas that need no special set-up

You don't need a theme to make the evening feel special. A few simple ideas families use:

- **A blessing circle.** Grandparents hold the baby first, then each relative gives a blessing in turn.
- **Lohri songs.** Ask an aunt or a grandmother to lead the traditional songs. Print the words for younger cousins.
- **Winter sweets to share.** Rewri, gajak, peanuts and popcorn are the classic Lohri treats. Ask us before bringing any from outside.
- **A photo walk.** The fairy-light tunnel over a red carpet makes a good backdrop for a family photo with the baby, as long as the baby is wrapped up warm.
- **A note for the baby.** Ask each guest to write one line for the baby to read when they grow up.

## What to serve elders and children

All prices are from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) and include GST.

**For the elders, warm winter dishes.** Saag (seasonal) is ₹275 and Dal Makhni is ₹275, with Tandoori Roti at ₹20 or Missi Roti at ₹30. Ask us whether the seasonal dishes are on the day you book.

**For a mixed family table.** Shahi Paneer and Kadhai Paneer each come in a Half portion at ₹225 or a Full at ₹375. Butter Chicken is ₹415 for a Half and ₹695 for a Full.

**Starters while everyone arrives.** Paneer Tikka is ₹375 and Hariyali Tikka is ₹325. Sweet Corn Soup at ₹155 is a warm start on a cold evening.

**For children.** Butter Naan at ₹45 and Jeera Rice at ₹230 are easy choices.

**Something sweet.** Gajrela (seasonal) is ₹75 for 100 g, Malpua Rabri (seasonal) is ₹65, and Gulab Jamun is ₹35.

There are no set packages. You order from the menu, and Half and Full portions make it easier to feed a big group without waste. Our guide on [Punjabi winter food](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/punjabi-winter-food/) explains the seasonal dishes in more detail.

## How a first Lohri differs from a regular Lohri party

A general [Lohri party](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/lohri-celebration-ludhiana/) can run late with friends and music. A baby's first Lohri is shorter, centred on the family, and planned around one small guest. Fewer people, an earlier start and simpler food usually make it a calmer evening for the parents.

## Getting here

We are at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana. Relatives coming from Ludhiana Railway Station have about 10.7 km to travel. The [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/) has a map and directions. The venue has no wheelchair access, which is worth knowing if elderly relatives are coming.

## Booking a first Lohri

Message or call 096467 13555 with the date, the start time and the number of guests. Mention that it is a baby's first Lohri. We confirm what is possible on the lawn that evening. For a smaller family gathering at another time of year, see our page on [small family functions](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/small-family-functions/).

## How do you keep a meal with children easy?

A few habits help at any family table:

- Order one snack, such as fries or noodles, as soon as you sit down. Hungry children wait better with something on the table.

- Pick one or two shared mains instead of a separate dish for each child.
- Keep dessert as the reward at the end. A ₹50 scoop goes a long way.
- Bring wipes. Tandoor food is eaten with hands.
