## Garden Restaurants in Punjab: What They Offer and How to Choose One
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/garden-restaurants-punjab/

A garden restaurant in Punjab is a place to eat outdoors on a lawn or among trees, usually serving North Indian and tandoor food, often with space for family functions. Choose one by checking the menu prices, evening lighting, drive time, accessibility and how booking works. Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana is one example.

Q: What food do garden restaurants in Punjab usually serve?
A: Most lean on North Indian cooking: tandoor dishes, dal, paneer and chicken curries, and breads. Red Wood Farm also serves Indo-Chinese and a Champ section of soya chaap.

Q: Can I order takeaway from Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes. Order by phone or message on 096467 13555. The kitchen serves dine-in and takeaway from 10 AM to 11 PM every day.

Q: What is Red Wood Farm's Google rating?
A: It showed 4.2 from 72 reviews on Google on 14 Nov 2026.

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from central Ludhiana?
A: About 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar and about 10.7 km from Ludhiana Railway Station by road. Travel times vary with traffic, so leave extra time.

A garden restaurant in Punjab is somewhere you eat outdoors, on a lawn or among trees, usually from a North Indian and tandoor menu, and often with space for family functions. To choose one, check the menu prices, the evening lighting, the drive time, accessibility and how booking works. Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana is one honest example.

## What makes a restaurant a garden restaurant?

The difference is where you sit. At a regular restaurant you're inside four walls. At a garden restaurant most of the tables are outside, on grass or under trees, with plants and open sky around you.

Across Punjab, these places often sit on the edge of a city, where there's land for a lawn. That means a short drive out of town for most people. In return you get space between tables, fresh air and space for children to walk around on the grass.

Most garden restaurants in the state serve North Indian food, with a tandoor at the center of the menu. Many also take bookings for small functions on the lawn, such as birthdays, kitty parties and family get-togethers.

## What should you check before choosing one?

Use this list for any garden restaurant you're considering. It works anywhere in Punjab.

1. **A menu with prices you can see.** Ask for the menu, or look for one online. You should know what a curry and a naan cost before you sit down.
2. **Veg and non-veg marks.** If your group mixes vegetarians and meat eaters, clear marks on the menu make ordering easier.
3. **Whether prices include GST.** Some menus include it and some add it at the bill. Ask.
4. **Opening hours.** Check the closing time if you want to stay after dark.
5. **Evening lighting.** A lawn looks different at night. Ask for night photos, not only daytime ones.
6. **Cover for bad weather.** Ask what happens if it rains or turns cold.
7. **Accessibility.** If someone in your group uses a wheelchair, ask directly about access before you travel.
8. **How booking works.** Find out if you book by phone, message or a website, and what details they need.
9. **Recent reviews with dates.** A rating means more when you know when it was checked.

## How do Punjab's seasons change the experience?

Punjab has hot summers and cold winters, and a garden restaurant feels the change more than an indoor one.

- **Summer.** Afternoons can be very hot. Most people pick an evening table once the sun is down.
- **Monsoon.** Rain can interrupt outdoor plans, so ask about covered seating and keep a backup time.
- **Winter.** Evenings get cold and foggy. Dress warmly. Daytime lunches in the winter sun are pleasant on a lawn.
- **Spring and autumn.** These are the easy months for eating outside at almost any hour.

Seasonal dishes follow the weather too. On our own menu, Saag, Gajrela and the fish dishes are marked seasonal.

Here is how Red Wood Farm answers the checklist above, using only what we can confirm.

- **Marks:** every dish is marked veg or non-veg. 131 dishes are veg.
- **GST:** included in every price.
- **Hours:** 10 AM to 11 PM, every day.
- **Evening lighting:** a walk-through [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/fairy-light-tunnel/) over a red carpet, palms along the driveway wrapped in fairy lights, lit paths with lamp posts and string lights over the lounge seating.
- **Cover:** photos from one event show a covered tent dining area with chandeliers. Ask whether one is part of your booking.
- **Accessibility:** there's no wheelchair access.
- **Booking:** by message or phone, with the date, time and number of guests.
- **Reviews:** Google showed 4.2 from 72 reviews on 14 Nov 2026.

## What does the garden at Red Wood Farm look like?

You arrive through a garden gate and a green hedge arch with flowers. A stone path runs through the grounds, and the open grass lawn is set with dining tables. Some tables sit under palm trees. Low lounge seating sits under string lights. In daytime the lawn has long wooden tables and more lounge seating.

## How Much to Order for a Group: Half and Full Portions Explained
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/group-ordering-guide/

At Red Wood Farm, 24 main-course dishes come in Half and Full; everything else has one price. As general guidance, order one starter or platter and one main for every three or four people, about two breads each, and add rice and raita for larger tables. Takeaway group orders go by phone or message.

Q: Is a Full portion double a Half?
A: The menu doesn't print portion weights, so we can't promise an exact ratio. On price, a Full costs less than two Halves for every dish except Shahi Mutton. Ask us how much a Full serves before a big order.

Q: Does Dal Makhni come in a Half portion?
A: No. Dal Makhni has one price, ₹275. So do the other dals: Yellow Dal Tadka, Dal Missi Tadka and Dal Handi are ₹245 each.

Q: Can I place a group takeaway order?
A: Yes. Send the dish names, Half or Full where it applies, and your pickup time to 096467 13555, or call the same number.

Q: Do the sample totals include GST?
A: Yes. Every menu price already includes GST, so the totals on this page are the sum of menu prices with nothing added for tax.

On the Red Wood Farm menu, only 24 main-course dishes have separate Half and Full prices: the paneer curries, the chicken curries and four mutton dishes. Every other dish, including all the dals, has one price. As general guidance, plan one starter and one main for every three or four people, plus about two breads per person.

## Which dishes come in Half and Full?

Half and Full only appear inside Main Course. On the [menu page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) those groups show two price columns, Half on the left and Full on the right.

Paneer dishes with both sizes include:

- Shahi Paneer: Half ₹225, Full ₹375
- Kadhai Paneer: Half ₹225, Full ₹375
- Paneer Butter Masala: Half ₹225, Full ₹345
- Palak Paneer: Half ₹225, Full ₹295
- Paneer Lababdar: Half ₹255, Full ₹395

Chicken and mutton dishes with both sizes include:

- Butter Chicken: Half ₹415, Full ₹695
- Farm to Table Special Chicken, our house signature: Half ₹415, Full ₹695
- Kadhai Chicken: Half ₹350, Full ₹600
- Chicken Curry: Half ₹395, Full ₹665
- Mutton Rogan Josh: Half ₹345, Full ₹645

Some mains are Full only. Atta Chicken is ₹925, Chicken Handi ₹645, Mutton Handi ₹665, and Malai Kofta ₹275.

## When should you pick Half over Full?

Look at the prices side by side. Two Half Shahi Paneer cost ₹450, while one Full costs ₹375. Two Half Butter Chicken cost ₹830, while one Full costs ₹695. For 23 of the 24 dishes, one Full costs less than two Halves. The exception is Shahi Mutton: two Halves at ₹325 come to ₹650, and a Full is ₹695.

So the rule is simple:

- **Order Half** when a small table wants to try two or three different curries.
- **Order Full** when several people want the same curry.

The menu doesn't print portion weights. If you need to know how many people a Full serves, ask us before you order.

## How much dal makhani per person?

Dal Makhni comes in one size at ₹275. As a rough guide, one order goes round three or four people when there's also a curry, bread and rice on the table. If dal is the main event at your table, order one for every two or three people. Our [Dal Makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/dal-makhani/) covers the dish itself.

This example uses menu prices only. It's general guidance, not a set meal.

| Dish | Price |
|---|---|
| Paneer Tikka | ₹375 |

## How to choose a party venue in Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/how-to-choose-a-party-venue-ludhiana/

In short: fix your guest count and budget first, then compare Ludhiana party venues on indoor or outdoor space, who cooks the food, the time slot, travel time for guests and access for older or disabled relatives. Get the menu, prices and slot in writing before you pay an advance. Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road is used here as an honest example, including that it has no wheelchair access.

Q: How early should I book a party venue in Ludhiana?
A: Message venues as soon as your date is fixed, since weekend and festival dates fill first. For Red Wood Farm, send the date, time and guest count to 096467 13555 and we'll tell you what's open.

Q: Do party venues in Ludhiana publish prices?
A: Many venues quote per head only after you share a date and guest count. Red Wood Farm publishes its full restaurant menu with GST-inclusive prices, and party pricing depends on the menu and numbers, so ask us.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm suitable for guests in wheelchairs?
A: No. Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. If a guest uses a wheelchair, choose a venue with step-free access from the gate to the seating.

Q: Can I see a venue before I book?
A: You should, and any venue that refuses is a warning sign. Red Wood Farm is a restaurant open daily from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, so you can come for a meal and see the lawn before you book.

To choose a party venue in Ludhiana, fix your guest count and budget first, then compare venues on five points: indoor or outdoor space, whether food is cooked in-house, the time slot, travel time for your guests, and access for older relatives. Get every answer in writing before you pay an advance.

The rest of this guide takes those points one at a time. We run a garden restaurant and party lawn on Pakhowal Road, so we use Red Wood Farm as a worked example throughout, including the places where we're the wrong fit.

## Start with two numbers: guests and budget

Write down the guest list before you call anyone. Then estimate how many will really come. Some people drop out, and some bring an extra family member or two. A range such as "40 to 50" is more useful to a venue than a single hopeful number.

Next, set a budget per head. Food is usually the largest cost at an Indian party, so most venues price around the menu and the headcount. Decoration, cake and return gifts sit on top of that.

With those two numbers, you can rule out half the venues on your list in one evening of messages.

**At Red Wood Farm:** we don't publish a capacity figure. Tell us your headcount and we'll say honestly whether the lawn works for it. Our restaurant menu is public, with every price including GST, so you can see what the food costs before you ask.

## Indoor or outdoor

This choice shapes everything else, from the decoration to the weather plan. We've written a full comparison in [outdoor vs indoor party venues](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/outdoor-vs-indoor-party-venues/), so here is only the short version.

An outdoor lawn gives space, open sky and lights that do part of the decorating after dark. An indoor hall gives you control over heat, cold and rain. If you pick outdoors, ask every venue where your party will go if the weather turns on the day.

**At Red Wood Farm:** parties happen on an open grass lawn with string lights, palms wrapped in fairy lights and a walk-through light tunnel. A covered tent dining area with chandeliers has been set up at an event. Ask us what cover is possible for your date before you commit.

## Food: the venue's kitchen or an outside caterer

Some venues cook everything themselves. Others rent the space and let you bring a caterer. Each has trade-offs.

An in-house kitchen means one bill, one point of contact and a menu you can taste beforehand by eating there. An outside caterer gives you more choice of dishes, but you then coordinate two businesses, and some venues add a charge for it.

Whichever you choose, ask for the menu in writing with prices, and check that veg and non-veg dishes are clearly separated. For quantities, such as how much dal or how many breads per guest, use our [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/party-planning-checklist/).

**At Red Wood Farm:** food comes from our own kitchen, which serves North Indian, tandoor and Indo-Chinese dishes. The [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists 187 dishes, each marked veg or non-veg, and many mains come in half and full portions. If you want to bring an outside caterer, ask us first.

## Timing: lunch, evening and the length of the slot

Lunch suits small children and elderly guests. Evenings suit adult birthdays, anniversaries and anything that benefits from lights. Weekends and festival weeks book up first, so have a second date in mind.

Ask what time your slot starts and ends, if you can arrive early to set up, and what happens if the party runs past the end time.

**At Red Wood Farm:** we're open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, so both lunch and evening parties are possible. Confirm your exact slot and set-up time when you book.

## Location and travel for your guests

Look at where most of your guests live, not just where you live. A venue that's ten minutes from your house can be forty minutes for your relatives across town. Share the location pin in the family group before you book and see who objects.

**At Red Wood Farm:** we're on outer Pakhowal Road at VPO Daad, opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats. By road that's about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar, 10.7 km from Ludhiana Railway Station and 8.2 km from the ISBT bus stand. Those figures don't include traffic, so guests should leave extra time in the evening. Route details are on the [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/).

## Accessibility

Ask about steps, uneven ground and the walk from the gate to the seating. If an older relative or a guest who uses a wheelchair is coming, this matters more than the decoration.

**At Red Wood Farm:** we have no wheelchair access. If someone in your group needs it, please choose a venue that has step-free access throughout. We'd rather say so now than have a guest stuck at the gate.

## Questions to ask every venue

Send these in one message so the answers come back in writing:

1. Is the space private for our group, or shared with other diners?
2. What exactly is included in the price, and is GST included?
3. Which time slot do we get, and when can we set up?
4. What is the plan if it rains or gets cold?
5. Can we bring our own cake, decoration and music?
6. How much advance do you need, and what happens if we change the date?
7. Can we see the actual area we'll use before booking?
8. Who is our single contact on the day?

## Red flags to watch for

- **No written menu or prices.** If a venue won't put numbers, the bill can grow later.
- **Photos that aren't of the venue.** Ask for pictures of the exact area you'll use. Our [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/) shows only photos taken at Red Wood Farm.
- **A vague weather answer** for an outdoor space.
- **Pressure to pay a large advance today**, with no written terms.
- **Capacity claims that sound padded.** Ask how the space is laid out for your number.
- **No visit allowed** before you book.

## Is Red Wood Farm the right fit for you?

Real photos from past events show birthday balloon arches, a kite-theme daytime backdrop, a mehndi stage, decorated entry gates, buffet counters on the lawn and function set-ups with drapes. One Google reviewer, Inderpreet Singh, called it a "Good space for small function parties.." and another, Kala Chahal, wrote "Great place for family party and social events." On 14 Nov 2026 we had a Google rating of 4.2 from 72 reviews.

We're likely a good fit for a family-sized gathering that wants a garden setting and food from a restaurant kitchen. We're the wrong fit if any guest needs wheelchair access, or if you need a guaranteed fully indoor hall.

## Send an enquiry

Message or call 096467 13555 with three things: the date, the time and the number of guests. We'll reply with what's possible that day. You can also come for a meal any day between 10:00 AM and 11:00 PM and see the lawn for yourself. More planning guides are on the [guides hub](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## How to Host a Kitty Party: The Host's Job, Step by Step
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/kitty-party-hosting-guide/

To host a kitty party, book the venue for your turn, send the invitation on the group's chat with a reply-by date, collect every member's contribution and record it, hand the month's kitty to the member whose turn it is, and keep the food and the games on a simple timetable. The host manages two things: the money and the clock.

Q: How many members does a kitty party usually have?
A: It varies by group. The member count also sets the cycle length, because each member hosts once and receives the kitty once before the cycle starts again.

Q: Who pays for the food at a kitty party?
A: Groups decide this at the start. Common rules are that the host pays, that the bill comes out of the month's collection, or that members split it equally. Pick one and write it down.

Q: What happens if a member misses her month?
A: Most groups agree she still pays her share on time, even if she can't attend. Settle this rule at the first meeting so nobody argues later.

Q: Can we book a kitty party table at Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes. Send your date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call the same number. We're open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM every day.

Hosting a kitty party comes down to five jobs: book the venue for your month, send the invitation on the group's chat with a reply-by date, collect every member's contribution and write it down, hand the kitty to the right member, and keep lunch and games on time. Get the money and the timetable right and the rest follows.

This page covers the host's side of it. For picking a place, see our page on [kitty party venues in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/kitty-party-venues-ludhiana/). For ideas to fill the afternoon, see [kitty party themes and games](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/kitty-party-themes-and-games/).

## What does the kitty host actually do?

The host for the month takes on a short list of tasks:

1. Choose the date and book the venue.
2. Send the invitation and chase replies.
3. Pick the theme or dress code, if the group uses one.
4. Collect contributions and keep the record.
5. Run the draw or hand over the kitty to the member whose turn it is.
6. Order the food, or agree the menu with the venue.
7. Keep time, so the group finishes when people need to leave.

None of it is hard. It just has to happen in the right order, and the host is the one who makes sure it does.

## How does a kitty rotation work?

A kitty group has a fixed set of members. Every month, each member puts in the same agreed amount. The full collection, the kitty, goes to one member that month. Over one full cycle, every member receives it once.

Groups decide who receives it in one of two ways:

- **A fixed order**, written down at the first meeting.
- **A draw**, where the names of members who haven't received the kitty yet go into a bowl and one is picked each month.

Hosting usually rotates too, but it doesn't have to match the receiving order. Some groups let the member receiving the kitty host. Others keep a separate hosting list. Whichever you choose, write both lists in the group's record so nobody has to remember.

## How should the host collect and record the money?

This is where groups fall out, so keep it clean.

Use one register or one shared spreadsheet for the whole cycle. For every meeting, record:

- the date and venue
- each member's name and the amount she paid
- who collected it
- who received the kitty that month
- anything still owed

At the end of the meeting, take a photo of the page and post it in the group. That one photo settles most questions before they start. Agree up front what happens if someone pays late or leaves the group mid-cycle, and put that rule at the top of the register.

## How to send the kitty invitation

Send it one to two weeks before the date, and pin it in the group. Keep it to the facts members need. A simple format:

> **December kitty at Red Wood Farm**\
> Date: [day and date]\
> Time: 1:00 PM\
> Place: Red Wood Farm, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles (map pin below)\
> Theme: [theme or dress code]\
> Please reply by [date] so I can confirm the table.\
> Contribution is due on the day.

Drop the venue's map pin right under the message. Two days before, send a short reminder to anyone who hasn't replied. Your final count goes to the venue after that.

## How do you plan the menu for a kitty party?

Kitty lunches work best with sharing plates: a few starters in the middle of the table, then one round of mains or a light dessert. Check how many members are vegetarian before you order. Our menu marks every dish veg or non-veg, which makes this quick, and our [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/vegetarian-guide/) has more on the veg side of the menu.

Starters that suit a shared table, from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/):

- Tandoori Veg Platter: ₹525
- Chinese Veg Platter: ₹575
- Paneer Tikka: ₹375
- Malai Champ: ₹275
- Cheese Fingers: ₹315
- Honey Chilli Potato: ₹255
- Masala Papad: ₹75

For a lighter main, Hakka Noodles are ₹255, and soups start at ₹145 for Tomato Shorba or Lemon Coriander. For dessert, Paneer Jalebi with Rabri is ₹75, Rasmalai is ₹45, and ice cream is ₹50 a scoop for Vanilla or Strawberry and ₹55 for Chocolate or Tutti Frutti. All our prices include GST, which makes splitting the bill simple.

Decide before the day who pays: the host, the month's collection or an equal split. Then order to match.

## What is a good timetable for the afternoon?

Most kitty parties run in the early afternoon. A timetable that works:

- **1:00 PM:** Members arrive. Starters go on the table.
- **1:30 PM:** Collect contributions and fill in the register.
- **2:00 PM:** Games.
- **2:45 PM:** The draw or the handover, then dessert.
- **3:15 PM:** Group photos. Post the register photo in the group.
- **3:30 PM:** Wrap up.

Keep the draw near the end. Members who arrive late still get to see it, and it gives the afternoon a clear finish. If many members collect children from school, move everything earlier.

## Hosting your month at Red Wood Farm

Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant and party lawn at 676, VPO Daad, on Pakhowal Road near Omaxe Flats. In daytime the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating, and our photos show a kite-theme backdrop set up for a daytime party. We're open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

To book your turn, send the date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call. Directions from Sarabha Nagar, Dugri and Model Town are on our [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/). More guides for hosts are in our [guides section](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## How to Read Our Menu: Veg Marks, GST, Half and Full
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/menu-marks-and-gst/

On the Red Wood Farm menu, a green square with a dot marks veg and a reddish-brown square with a triangle marks non-veg. Every price is in rupees and already includes GST. Half and Full columns appear only on some main courses, and ice creams are priced per scoop.

Q: Will GST be added on top of the menu price?
A: No. Every price on our menu already includes GST, so tax isn't added on top of the listed price.

Q: Are egg dishes marked veg or non-veg?
A: Non-veg. The three omelettes in the Sides section carry the non-veg mark, from ₹70 to ₹85.

Q: Why doesn't the search find dal makhani?
A: The menu spells it Dal Makhni. Type "makh" or "dal" and it will show up.

Q: What are the lowest and highest prices on the menu?
A: Tandoori Roti and Tawa Roti are ₹20 each. Atta Chicken is the highest at ₹925.

Q: How many vegetarian dishes are there?
A: 131 of the 187 dishes carry the veg mark. The other 56 are marked non-veg.

Every dish on the Red Wood Farm menu carries one of two marks. A green square with a dot means veg. A reddish-brown square with a triangle means non-veg. All prices are in rupees and already include GST, so no tax is added on top. Some mains also show separate Half and Full prices.

## What do the veg and non-veg marks mean?

The marks follow the green-and-brown idea most Indian diners already know from food packets:

- **Veg:** a green square outline with a green dot in the middle.
- **Non-veg:** a reddish-brown square outline with a triangle inside.

Of our 187 dishes, 131 carry the veg mark and 56 carry the non-veg mark. On the [menu page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) the mark sits just to the left of each dish name. Screen readers announce it as "Veg" or "Non-veg".

Egg counts as non-veg on our menu. The Plain Omelette with 2 Slices (₹70), the Masala Omelette with 2 Slices (₹75) and the Cheese Omelette with 2 Slices (₹85) all carry the non-veg mark. If your family is strictly vegetarian, our [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/vegetarian-guide/) picks out what to order.

## Why is Ice Cream with Brownie marked non-veg?

Brownies are often made with egg. Until we've confirmed that the brownie we serve is eggless, Ice Cream with Brownie (₹95) stays marked non-veg. We'd rather mark one dish too cautiously than let an egg-free family order it by mistake. The four plain ice creams are all marked veg.

## Do the prices include GST?

Yes. Every price on the menu includes GST. A Butter Naan listed at ₹45 is ₹45, and a Dal Makhni listed at ₹275 is ₹275. When you add up an order from the menu, the sum is the total for those dishes with GST already inside.

The full range runs from ₹20 for a Tandoori Roti or a Tawa Roti up to ₹925 for Atta Chicken, our chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough.

If you have a question about anything else on a bill, ask us at the table or.

## How do the Half and Full columns work?

Only 24 dishes have two sizes, all in Main Course. On the menu page, any group that contains them shows a small "Half / Full" heading on the right. Each dish in that group then has two prices:

- Shahi Paneer: Half ₹225, Full ₹375
- Chicken Curry: Half ₹395, Full ₹665
- Mutton Rogan Josh: Half ₹345, Full ₹645

When a dish in the same group has only one size, the Half column is blank and the single price sits under Full. Malai Kofta (₹275) and Chicken Handi (₹645) are examples. Every dish outside Main Course has one price. Dal Makhni, for instance, is just ₹275.

To plan how many Halves or Fulls a table needs, read our [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/group-ordering-guide/).

## What does "seasonal" mean on the menu?

A dish marked seasonal isn't on every day of the year. These are the seasonal items:

- Saag (seasonal): ₹275
- Bhindi (seasonal): ₹275
- Gajrela, 100 g (seasonal): ₹75
- Malpua Rabri (seasonal): ₹65
- The whole Fish (seasonal) group of eight dishes, from Fish Manchurian at ₹555 to Fish Curry at ₹595

If you're coming for one of these, send us a message on the day to check.

## Why are ice creams priced per scoop?

The Ice Creams section has a note that says "Per scoop". Vanilla and Strawberry are ₹50 a scoop. Chocolate and Tutti Frutti are ₹55. Order three scoops of Vanilla and the line on your order is ₹150. Our [desserts page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/desserts/) has the rest of the sweet side.

## How do you use the search and filter on the menu page?

The menu page has a strip of tools that stays at the top of the screen as you scroll:

1. **Search box.** Type part of a dish name, such as "paneer", "tikka" or "naan". The list narrows as you type.
2. **Diet buttons.** Tap All, Veg or Non-veg. The buttons work together with the search, so "Veg" plus "tikka" shows only veg tikkas.
3. **Category links.** Tap a section, such as Champ or Breads, to jump straight to it.

A line above the dishes shows how many match, for example "12 of 187 dishes". If nothing matches, you'll see a note suggesting another word.

A few search tips:

- Search uses the spellings on our menu. Dal makhani is spelled "Dal Makhni", and soya chaap is listed under "Champ".
- Search matches dish names only, not the short notes under some dishes.
- Short fragments work well. "makh" finds Dal Makhni, and "chick" finds every chicken dish.

## Ask about anything you can't find

## Indo-Chinese Food in Ludhiana at Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/indo-chinese/

In short: Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana serves Indo-Chinese dishes beside its North Indian menu. Hakka Noodles cost ₹255, Manchurian Dry ₹275, Manchow Soup ₹155 and Chilli Paneer ₹375, and chicken versions such as Chicken Manchurian start at ₹355. All prices include GST.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm have veg fried rice?
A: No. The only fried rice on our menu is Chicken Fried Rice at ₹320. For a vegetarian Indo-Chinese meal, pair Manchurian Gravy (₹260) with Hakka Noodles (₹255) or Steamed Rice (₹180).

Q: What is the cheapest Indo-Chinese dish on the menu?
A: Hot & Sour soup at ₹145. Among the starters, Spring Roll is the lowest at ₹240.

Q: Are the Indo-Chinese dishes vegetarian?
A: Most are. Every dish carries a veg or non-veg mark on the menu, and the chicken and fish versions are marked non-veg.

Q: Can I order Indo-Chinese food for takeaway?
A: Yes. Call or message 096467 13555 with your order and pickup time, and collect it from 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road.

Red Wood Farm serves Indo-Chinese food next to its tandoor and curry menu on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana. Hakka Noodles cost ₹255, Manchurian Dry ₹275, Manchow Soup ₹155 and Chilli Paneer ₹375. The chicken side starts with Chicken Manchurian at ₹355. Every price includes GST, and each dish comes in one size.

## What does Indo-Chinese mean?

Indo-Chinese is Chinese cooking that has been changed to suit Indian tastes. It is commonly traced to the Chinese community in Kolkata, and from there it spread to restaurants and street stalls across India. The cooking uses Chinese methods such as stir-frying and deep-frying, with soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, ginger and green chilli. Indian cooks then add more heat and a thicker, glossier sauce.

Many dishes in this style were invented in India and are rarely found in China. Manchurian is the best-known example. In Punjab, Indo-Chinese plates are a regular part of family dinners and parties, often eaten as starters before a North Indian main course.

The words in a dish name tell you how it is cooked. "Dry" means the sauce clings to the pieces, so the dish works as a starter. "Gravy" means more sauce, meant to go over noodles or rice. "Chilli" usually signals a soy and green chilli sauce with onion and capsicum. "Crispy" means the main ingredient is fried before it is tossed in sauce.

## Soups

Four of our soups belong to this style:

- **Manchow Soup, ₹155.** Usually a dark, spicy soup with chopped vegetables, often topped with crisp fried noodles.
- **Sweet Corn Soup, ₹155.** Usually a thick, mild corn soup.
- **Hot & Sour, ₹145.** Sharp with vinegar and hot with pepper, as the name says.
- **Chicken Hot & Sour, ₹245.** The non-veg version.

A soup is a good way to start a winter evening on the lawn while the rest of the order is cooked.

## Manchurian, dry or in gravy

Manchurian is usually made from deep-fried balls of minced vegetables or pieces of chicken, tossed in a garlic, soy and chilli sauce. We serve it two ways.

| Dish | Price |
|---|---|
| Manchurian Dry | ₹275 |
| Manchurian Gravy | ₹260 |
| Chicken Manchurian | ₹355 |
| Chicken Manchurian Dry | ₹375 |
| Fish Manchurian (seasonal) | ₹555 |

Order the dry version as a starter to share. The gravy version is meant to go with noodles or rice. Fish Manchurian sits in our seasonal fish section, so ask us whether it is available on your date.

## Chilli dishes and crispy starters

These work well as shared starters before the mains.

- **Chilli Paneer, ₹375.** Paneer in a chilli sauce, listed in our vegetarian main course. More paneer options are on our [paneer dishes page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/paneer-dishes/).
- **Cheese Chilli, ₹325.**
- **Mushroom Chilli, ₹325.**
- **Baby Corn Chilli, ₹265.**
- **Honey Chilli Potato, ₹255.** Usually crisp potato strips in a sweet and spicy glaze.

## Kids Birthday Party Ideas for Ludhiana: At Home or on a Garden Lawn
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/kids-birthday-party-ideas/

In short: keep a kids birthday party to two or three hours, plan running games that need open space, and order food children already eat. At Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road the lawn gives space for games and the menu has kid favourites such as French Fries at ₹195. There is no play area, so adults supervise.

Q: What age is a lawn birthday party best for?
A: Children from about three to ten get the most out of open grass and running games. For toddlers, keep the party short and set up quiet corners such as bubbles and drawing.

Q: Is there a play area for children at Red Wood Farm?
A: No. The lawn is open grass with no play area, rides or kids' zone, so plan supervised games and bring a few simple props from home.

Q: Can we bring our own cake and decorations?
A: Tell us what you plan to bring when you book with a message (096467 13555), and we'll confirm what works for your date. Birthday set-ups with balloon arches have been done on our lawn before.

Q: What is a good time of day for a kids birthday party?
A: Late morning or mid-afternoon suits most children because it avoids a late bedtime. Red Wood Farm is open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM every day.

The kids birthday party ideas that work in Ludhiana are simple. Keep the party to two or three hours, plan games that need running space, order food children already eat, and have enough adults watching. An open lawn handles the running games a flat can't. These ideas work at home or at Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road.

## Home party or venue: which suits your child?

A party at home makes sense when the list is short and mostly cousins. You know where everything is, toddlers can nap in their own beds, and nobody needs directions. The cost is your time. Someone cooks, someone cleans up, and a dozen children end up racing between the sofa and the dining table.

A venue starts to make sense once school friends join, because most of their parents stay too. The food comes out cooked, staff clear the plates, and the mess stays behind when you drive home. At a garden venue the children also get real grass under their feet.

A rough guide:

- **Ten or fewer children, mostly family:** home is easy.
- **A whole class plus parents:** look for a place with open outdoor space.
- **A winter evening party:** ask the venue where guests sit once the night turns cold.
- **Grandparents who use a wheelchair:** Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access, so a home party or a step-free venue may suit your family better.

For the venue side of the choice, our page on [birthday party venues in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/birthday-party-venues-ludhiana/) covers what to check before you book.

## Games that work on an open lawn

Indoor games run out of space fast. On grass the children can spread out. Most of these need little more than a phone and a few things from home:

- **Picture-clue treasure hunt.** Draw 8 to 10 clues for children who can't read yet, and write words for older ones. Hide them near your own tables, within sight of the adults. Check with us before the day about where clues can go.
- **Musical statues.** One phone and a small speaker. Everyone freezes when the music stops. It works from about age three up to ten.
- **Relay races.** Spoon and lemon, a sack race in old pillow covers, or a plain run to the far chair and back. Swap the lemon for a small soft ball with the little ones.
- **Bedsheet bounce.** Four parents hold an old bedsheet by the corners and bounce a soft ball while the children try to catch it.
- **Bubble corner.** Two bottles of bubble mix keep toddlers busy while the older kids race.
- **Card-making table.** Put crayons and paper on one table. Each guest draws a card for the birthday child, and you take home a stack of keepsakes.

For a theme, pick one color and one character, then carry them through the cake, the balloons and the return gifts. Birthday set-ups with balloon arches have been done on our lawn. Tell us what decoration you plan to bring when you book, and we'll confirm what works.

## Planning a party for about 20 children

Twenty children rarely means twenty guests. Count the parents who will stay, the siblings and the grandparents. Send us both numbers, children and adults,, and we'll tell you which part of the lawn suits your group on that date. There is no fixed number we quote, because it depends on the set-up.

A simple three-hour afternoon plan:

1. **First 30 minutes:** arrivals, name stickers and the card-making table.
2. **Next 45 minutes:** two or three running games while energy is high.
3. **Then food:** starters for the children, mains for the adults alongside.
4. **Cake:** after the food, once the children have calmed down a little.
5. **Last half hour:** one quiet game, return gifts and goodbyes.

We open at 10:00 AM every day, so a late-morning party works too. For quantities, use our [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party-planning-checklist/).

Our guide to [kid-friendly food](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/kids-favourites/) goes into more detail. A practical tip: order starters in two rounds. Children eat a few fries and run off, so a second plate 40 minutes later arrives hot.

## Safety notes for an outdoor kids' party

- Red Wood Farm has no play area, rides or kids' zone. The lawn is open grass, so plan supervised games and give each small group one adult.
- Pick up burst balloon pieces from the grass. They are a choking risk for children under three.
- Ask children to keep their shoes on during races.
- Write a parent's phone number on each name sticker.
- Ask parents about food allergies before you order, and share the menu link ahead of the day.
- On warm days, bring water bottles and caps. After dark the paths are lit by lamp posts and string lights, but keep the little ones close to your tables.
- Keep games away from the walkways where food is carried out.

## Kitty Party Games and Themes: Quick and Funny Ideas for Your Group
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/kitty-party-themes-and-games/

In short: the best kitty party games are quick, need few props and get the whole table laughing, such as one-minute challenges, baby photo guessing, film charades and housie. Pick four to six games and one simple theme. Red Wood Farm hosts daytime groups on its garden lawn on Pakhowal Road.

Q: How many games should a kitty party have?
A: Four to six is plenty for a three-hour afternoon. Mix two or three one-minute games with one team game, and finish with housie or a prize round.

Q: What prizes work for kitty party games?
A: Small things wrapped before the party, such as a scented candle, a small plant or a box of sweets. Keep every prize close to the same value so nobody feels short-changed.

Q: Can we put up our own theme backdrop at Red Wood Farm?
A: Tell us your theme when you book with a message (096467 13555) and we'll confirm what can be set up. A daytime party here has used a kite-theme backdrop on the lawn.

Q: What time should a kitty party start?
A: Most groups meet in the late morning or early afternoon. Red Wood Farm opens at 10:00 AM every day.

The kitty party games that work best are quick, need almost no props and get the whole group laughing: one-minute challenges, guessing games and team games across two halves of the table. Choose four to six, add one easy theme, and a three-hour afternoon plans itself. Every idea below works at home or at a daytime booking on our lawn.

## One-minute games for a kitty party

Set a 60-second timer on a phone. Each player gets one turn, and the best score wins a small wrapped prize.

- **Cup pyramid.** Build a pyramid from ten paper cups, then stack them back into a single tower, all inside a minute.
- **Name ten.** The host calls a category, such as things in a handbag, Ludhiana markets or film titles with the word love. Players race to name ten before time runs out.
- **Peanut shift.** Move peanuts from one bowl to another using only chopsticks. Count the peanuts at the buzzer.
- **Balloon keep-up.** Keep two balloons in the air for 60 seconds using one hand. Touch the ground and you're out.
- **Card tower.** Build three levels with a deck of playing cards. A slight breeze on the lawn makes this one funnier.
- **Lipstick without a mirror.** Apply lipstick in a minute with no mirror, and the group votes on the neatest result.
- **Spoon and lemon dash.** Walk a lemon on a spoon to the far chair and back. Drop it and you restart from the line.

These games fill the gaps between starters arriving, so keep the props in one tote bag and hand it to whoever is hosting the round.

## Funny group games for ladies

Team games take longer and get louder. Save two of them for after the main course.

- **Guess the bag.** Everyone drops one item from her handbag into a basket. The host pulls them out one by one and the group guesses who each item belongs to.
- **Baby photo match.** Each member sends a childhood photo to the host a day before. The host prints and numbers them, and players match faces to names on a slip of paper.
- **Film charades.** Split into two teams, one on each side of the table. Act out film titles with no words. Whichever team guesses more inside two minutes per round wins.
- **Song chain.** One team sings a line from any film song. The other team has ten seconds to start a new song with the last letter of that line. Miss it and the point goes across.
- **Two truths and a lie.** Each person says three things about herself. The table votes on which one is made up. Long-time members usually learn something new.
- **Pass the parcel with forfeits.** Wrap a small prize in many layers, with a dare slip inside each layer, such as mimicking a teacher or singing two lines.
- **Housie.** The old favourite for the end of the afternoon. Bring printed tickets and use a number-calling app.

## Simple kitty party themes

A theme gives the group something to plan for and makes the photos match.

- **Kite theme.** A daytime party on our lawn used a backdrop of paper kites on a green curtain, with flower stands in front. Kites suit a winter afternoon.
- **One-color dress code.** Everyone wears yellow, pink or white. Daytime light on the lawn makes single-color group photos easy.
- **Festival month.** Plan around Lohri in January, Teej in the monsoon months or the Diwali season, and match the food and the outfits.
- **Retro film day.** Each member dresses as an old film star. The song chain game fits this theme well.
- **Garden picnic.** Sun hats, sunglasses and a basket of fruit as the table centerpiece.
- **Shawl and scarf afternoon.** A cozy winter theme for November to February, with everyone in her favourite shawl.

## Running games at a daytime lawn booking

The long wooden tables on the lawn by day suit games, because the host can see everyone and be heard. The lounge seating nearby works for chatting between rounds.

A running order that keeps energy up:

1. **Late morning:** arrivals, photos at the backdrop and the first one-minute games while starters come out.
2. **Middle:** mains, then two team games.
3. **End:** dessert, housie and the prize handover.

Order finger food that doesn't stop play. Masala Papad (₹75), Aloo Chana Chaat (₹125), Spring Roll (₹240) and Honey Chilli Potato (₹255) work well between rounds. For a group, a Chinese Veg Platter (₹575) or a Tandoori Veg Platter (₹525) covers several tastes on one plate. Paneer Jalebi with Rabri (₹75) is a good last plate with housie. Every price includes GST, and the full list is on our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/).

Wrap prizes before you leave home and keep them in one bag. Hand them all out at the end so nobody leaves early with a prize still owed.

## Choosing where to hold it

This page is about what to play. For what to ask a venue about the time slot, seating and menu, read our [kitty party venue guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/kitty-party-venues-ludhiana/). Many of these games also work at a [baby shower](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/baby-shower-venue-ludhiana/) with a few changes.

Send your date, start time, group size and theme to 096467 13555. We're open from 10:00 AM every day at VPO Daad on Pakhowal Road, near Omaxe Flats. More photos of the lawn are on our [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## How to host a kitty party at a restaurant

Hosting at a venue saves the host a day of cooking and cleaning up. The steps are short:

1. **Fix the date and the host for the month.** Most groups rotate.
2. **Get a firm headcount.** Kitty groups are usually steady, but one or two members bring a guest or drop out.
3. **Book the slot.** Say what time you arrive and roughly how long you plan to stay.
4. **Choose the food.** Either order on the day from the menu, or agree a short list in advance.
5. **Plan the games and the theme.** Our page on [kitty party themes and games](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/kitty-party-themes-and-games/) has ideas that work at a table.
6. **Settle the kitty and the bill** before the group starts leaving.

The finer points, such as who invites, how the kitty draw runs and how the host keeps things fair, are in our [kitty party hosting guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/kitty-party-hosting-guide/).

## Kitty party halls with price, and how a restaurant compares

Banquet halls in the city usually quote a fixed price per guest with a set menu, and some ask for a minimum number of guests. That suits a large group that wants one bill and no choices. A restaurant lets a smaller group order what it likes and pay for what it eats.

We quote party prices because they depend on your menu and group size. Our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) shows every dish price up front, GST included, which lets the host work out a rough spend before booking. When you compare a hall quote with a restaurant, check what the hall price covers: starters, dessert and taxes are the usual gaps.

## Kitty party restaurants: what makes one work

A restaurant table works for a kitty group when a few practical things line up. Run through these before you book anywhere:

- **Room to sit as one group.** Twelve to twenty ladies split across three small tables turns into three separate parties. Ask for long tables or a joined set.
- **Time to linger.** A kitty lunch often runs three hours with the games. Check that nobody will need your table back halfway through.
- **A corner where you can hear each other.** Housie and quiz games need people to hear the caller.
- **A menu that suits mixed diets.** Clear veg and non-veg marks save the host a lot of questions.
- **One person to deal with on the day.** Save that number in the group before the date.

## Lohri Party Venue in Ludhiana on a Garden Lawn
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/lohri-celebration-ludhiana/

Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road hosts Lohri get-togethers on its garden lawn in mid-January, with food from the regular menu, including seasonal winter dishes such as Saag and Gajrela when available. Prices are listed per dish and include GST. For anything on the lawn beyond seating and food, ask us at 096467 13555.

Q: When is Lohri celebrated?
A: Lohri falls in mid-January, usually on 13 January, the evening before Maghi. Check the exact date for the year when you plan.

Q: Are there Lohri party venues in Ludhiana with prices?
A: Red Wood Farm publishes every dish price on its menu page, with GST included. There are no set packages. You order from the menu, and we confirm what is possible for your date.

Q: Is Saag on the menu all year?
A: No. Saag is marked seasonal on the menu, at ₹275. Ask us whether it is available on your date.

Q: Can we celebrate a baby's or a newly married couple's first Lohri here?
A: Yes, family gatherings are what the lawn is for. Send the date, time and guest count, and ask us what is possible on the lawn for anything you plan beyond food and seating.

Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road is a Lohri party venue in Ludhiana with an open garden lawn, fairy lights after dark and winter dishes like Saag and Gajrela when in season. You order by the dish, at prices that include GST. Book at 096467 13555 and ask us what is possible on the lawn.

## What is Lohri, and why do families gather for it?

Lohri is Punjab's winter festival, held in mid-January, usually on 13 January. It marks the end of the coldest stretch of the year and has long been linked with the farming calendar in Punjab. Traditionally, families and neighbors gather in the evening around a fire, sing folk songs, dance, and share sesame and jaggery sweets, peanuts and popcorn.

A family's first Lohri after a wedding or the birth of a child is often the biggest of all. Relatives come from across the city and from further away, gifts change hands, and the evening runs late. That is usually when people look for a venue, because the guest list outgrows the house.

## Can we hold our Lohri customs on the lawn?

We host family gatherings and parties on the lawn, with dining tables, low lounge seating under string lights and food from our own kitchen. This page can't confirm any particular ritual set-up for Lohri. If your family plans anything beyond seating, food and decoration, ask us what is possible on the lawn when you message, and we will answer for your specific date.

## What should guests expect on a January evening?

January nights in Ludhiana are cold, and the lawn is open air. Tell guests to bring shawls and warm jackets, especially the elders. Red Wood Farm's own photos show a covered tent dining area with chandeliers set up at one event, so ask whether a covered set-up is possible for your Lohri.

After sunset the garden is lit. A walk-through tunnel of warm white fairy lights runs over a red carpet, the palms along the driveway are wrapped in lights, and lamp posts line the garden paths. Guests photograph the tunnel more than anything else, which makes it a natural spot for the family picture in your Lohri outfits.

## What winter food is on the menu for Lohri?

Lohri food is winter food: greens, butter, jaggery and milk sweets. Our menu has several dishes that suit a January table. Anything marked seasonal depends on availability, so confirm it a few days ahead.

**Seasonal dishes**

- **Saag (seasonal)** at ₹275, a winter staple in Punjab
- **Gajrela (100 g, seasonal)** at ₹75, the carrot and milk pudding many families make every winter
- **Malpua Rabri (seasonal)** at ₹65

The menu has no corn roti. Missi Roti (₹30), Tandoori Roti (₹20) and Butter Naan (₹45) are the breads to pair with Saag.

**Year-round dishes for the rest of the table**

- Dal Makhni (₹275) and Kadhi Pakoda (₹230)
- Paneer Tikka (₹375) and Tandoori Chicken (₹375) from the tandoor
- Butter Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full) and Mutton Rogan Josh (₹345 half, ₹645 full)
- Gulab Jamun (₹35) and Kheer (₹65)

Sesame sweets, peanuts and popcorn are not on our menu. If you want to bring your own to hand out, ask us first. The [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists every dish with its price, and our guide to [Punjabi winter food](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/punjabi-winter-food/) covers more of the season's dishes.

## How do you plan a Lohri party for a big family?

- **Fix the date early.** Lohri is one evening, and many families want that same evening.
- **Choose the hour.** It is an evening festival. Starting around sunset gives you the lights, and we close at 11 PM.
- **Count heads twice.** Give a rough number when you book and a firm one closer to the day.
- **Plan for the elders.** There is no wheelchair access at Red Wood Farm, so think ahead for any grandparent who uses a wheelchair.
- **Gifts and decorations.** Tell us if you are bringing a cake, decorations or gifts to hand out.

Our page on [small family functions](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/small-family-functions/) covers roka and engagement gatherings, which need much the same planning.

If the party is for a first Lohri, put the couple or the baby's parents at the center table and keep the singing and the gift-giving close to them. Order the starters to arrive as guests settle, so the food is not competing with the singing later in the evening.

## Booking Lohri at Red Wood Farm

Message 096467 13555, or call, with your date, start time and number of guests. Mention whether it is a first Lohri, and ask us what is possible on the lawn for anything beyond food and seating. See other events on the [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/), or read about [winter evenings on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/winter-evenings-on-the-lawn/).

## Ludhiana Railway Station to Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/from-railway-station/

Red Wood Farm is about 10.7 km from Ludhiana Railway Station by road. The route follows Ferozepur Road, then Pakhowal Road out of the city towards Daad, and OSRM estimates about 16 minutes with no traffic. Take a cab or auto booked on an app, or drive, and allow extra time at peak hours.

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from Ludhiana Railway Station?
A: About 10.7 km by road, according to OSRM route data checked on 17 Nov 2026. OSRM's estimate of about 16 minutes assumes empty roads.

Q: Can I take an auto from the station to Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes. Book an auto or a cab on a ride-hailing app and set Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road as the drop point. Ask us on 096467 13555 to share our location so you can forward the pin to the driver.

Q: Is the ISBT bus stand closer to Red Wood Farm than the railway station?
A: Yes. OSRM puts ISBT Ludhiana about 8.2 km away by road, roughly 13 minutes with no traffic, against 10.7 km from the railway station.

Q: Which building is Red Wood Farm opposite?
A: Cerajot Tiles. We are on Pakhowal Road near Daad village and Omaxe Flats, and you turn in at our garden gate.

Ludhiana Railway Station is about 10.7 km from Red Wood Farm by road. You leave on Ferozepur Road, switch to Pakhowal Road, and stay with it as it runs out of the city towards Daad. OSRM, an open routing engine built on OpenStreetMap data, puts the drive at about 16 minutes on empty roads. Real traffic adds to that.

## Which roads does the route use, in order?

This route comes from OSRM, checked on 17 Nov 2026. The road names are the ones OpenStreetMap uses, so a signboard may spell a few of them differently.

1. **Ferozepur Road, about 0.8 km.** You leave the station area and join Ferozepur Road.
2. **Pakhowal Road, about 1.3 km.** The route turns off Ferozepur Road onto Pakhowal Road.
3. **Satpal Mittal Road, about 0.3 km.** A short link. Our route data places Hero Bakery Chowk on this road, which is a handy name to give a driver.
4. **Krishna Mandir Road, about 0.5 km.** Another short connector that brings you back onto Pakhowal Road.
5. **Pakhowal Road, about 2.0 km.** The main run out of the built-up part of the city.
6. **Jodhan - Ludhiana Road, about 2.8 km.** This is the outer stretch of Pakhowal Road. OpenStreetMap labels it with this name. Our address, and most people you ask, still call it Pakhowal Road.

Those six named stretches add up to about 7.7 km. The other 3 km or so is made of short turns and junction links that OSRM counts in the total without giving each one a name. Steps 3 and 4 come close together, so set your navigation before you pull away from the station.

## How long should you allow?

Read OSRM's 16 minutes as the best case. It assumes no traffic at all, which you will rarely get near a busy railway station. Signals, crowds outside the station after a train arrives and slow traffic on the inner roads all stretch the trip. Allow extra time at peak hours and on festival evenings. If you are heading back for a train after your meal, leave Red Wood Farm earlier than the map suggests.

## Getting here by cab or auto

Most people arriving by train will book a cab or an auto on a ride-hailing app. Type "Red Wood Farm, Pakhowal Road" as the drop point and look at the pin on the map before you confirm the ride. Many drivers will know Pakhowal Road by name. Fewer will know exactly where it reaches Daad, so keep three landmarks ready: Daad village, Cerajot Tiles and Omaxe Flats.

We can't quote a fare. It depends on the app, the vehicle and the time of day.

### Send "share location" first

Before you leave the platform, message us at 096467 13555 and ask us to share our location. Open the pin in your maps app, or forward it straight to your driver. It saves a roadside phone call and points the car at the right gate.

## Driving your own car

Once you are on Pakhowal Road the drive is simple: you keep going until the city thins out near Daad. The early part, up to the point where you rejoin Pakhowal Road, takes the most attention, because the route switches roads four times in under 3 km of named road. After that, the last 4.8 km is two long stretches with no change of road in our route data.

## Finding the gate at the end

The final 2.8 km is the stretch OpenStreetMap labels Jodhan - Ludhiana Road. As you get close, Daad village sits under a kilometer from our pin and Omaxe Flats, also known as Omaxe Royal Residency, is just off the road. Red Wood Farm stands opposite Cerajot Tiles. Turn in at the garden gate and walk through the green hedge arch with its flowers. After dark the palms along our driveway are wrapped in fairy lights, which tells you that you have the right place.

A note for families travelling with an older relative or a wheelchair user: Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. Please plan for that before you set out.

## Before you head out from the station

- We are open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day.
- For a table or a party, send your date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call the same number.
- Hungry after a long journey: our [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists every dish with its price, GST included.
- Coming in from the Ferozepur Road side instead: the [Bharat Nagar Chowk route](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-ferozepur-road/) shares most of these roads.
- For the bigger picture of the road we sit on, read the [Pakhowal Road guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/pakhowal-road-guide/).

Once you are inside, walk through the [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/) on your way to the lawn. Every other route to us is on the [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Model Town to Pakhowal Road: Directions to Red Wood Farm
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/from-model-town/

Red Wood Farm is about 6.9 km from Model Town by road. The OSRM route takes Model Town Road and Krishna Mandir Road onto Pakhowal Road, then follows it out of the city to Daad, in about 11 minutes with no traffic. We are opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats.

Q: How do I get from Model Town to Pakhowal Road?
A: Take Model Town Road for about 0.6 km and Krishna Mandir Road for about 0.5 km. That brings you onto Pakhowal Road, according to OSRM route data from 17 Nov 2026.

Q: Is the route from the ISBT bus stand similar?
A: Yes. From ISBT Ludhiana, OSRM uses the same Krishna Mandir Road, Pakhowal Road and outer Pakhowal Road sequence, for about 8.2 km and roughly 13 minutes with no traffic.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm do takeaway for Model Town?
A: We do takeaway. Order by phone or message on 096467 13555 and collect it from us on Pakhowal Road. Ask us about anything beyond that.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm open on weekdays?
A: Yes, we are open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

Model Town is about 6.9 km from Red Wood Farm by road. Take Model Town Road and Krishna Mandir Road onto Pakhowal Road, then stay on Pakhowal Road as it heads out of the city to Daad. OSRM estimates about 11 minutes on clear roads. Expect the real drive to take longer at busy times.

## Step by step from Model Town

This is the route OSRM produced on 17 Nov 2026, with road names as OpenStreetMap shows them.

**Step 1. Model Town Road, about 0.6 km.** OSRM's starting point sits on Model Town Road, in the Gurudev Nagar part of the map. Head along it to the first turn.

**Step 2. Krishna Mandir Road, about 0.5 km.** A short connector. It is the same link used by the routes from the railway station, the ISBT bus stand and Ferozepur Road, so you will see it on several of our route pages.

**Step 3. Pakhowal Road, about 2.0 km.** You are now on Pakhowal Road proper. Keep going away from the city center.

**Step 4. Jodhan - Ludhiana Road, about 2.8 km.** OpenStreetMap changes the label here, but it is the same road you were on. Locals and our address call it Pakhowal Road. This is the final leg.

Add up the named roads and you get about 5.9 km. The remaining 1.0 km or so is streets in Model Town and short pieces at junctions, which OSRM counts in its 6.9 km total without naming. Your own house may sit a little closer or farther than OSRM's start point.

## How long it really takes

OSRM's 11 minutes is a no-traffic figure. It doesn't account for signals, queues or a festival evening. Treat it as the shortest the trip could be. On a weekday at peak hours, allow extra time, and more again if you have guests arriving for a party and want to be there first.

For a sense of scale, Model Town is roughly level with Sarabha Nagar in our route data: 6.9 km and 6.8 km, both about 11 minutes. [Dugri](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-dugri/) is a little shorter at 6.5 km.

## Coming from the ISBT bus stand instead

Friends arriving by bus can follow almost the same route. ISBT Ludhiana is also listed in Gurudev Nagar, and OSRM routes it along Krishna Mandir Road (about 0.5 km), Pakhowal Road (about 2.0 km) and Jodhan - Ludhiana Road (about 2.8 km). The total is about 8.2 km, roughly 13 minutes with no traffic. If you are collecting someone off a bus, pick them up first and the rest of the drive is shared.

## What you'll see near the end

On the last 2.8 km you reach the area around Daad. These are the landmarks in our address:

- **Daad village**, spelled "Dad" on OpenStreetMap, under a kilometer from our pin.
- **Omaxe Flats**, the Omaxe Royal Residency development, about 0.8 km from us by road.
- **Cerajot Tiles**, across the road from Red Wood Farm.

Pull in at the garden gate opposite Cerajot Tiles. The green hedge arch with flowers is the entrance, and at night the palms along the driveway carry fairy lights.

One thing to know in advance: there is no wheelchair access at Red Wood Farm. Families with a wheelchair user should plan for that.

## Without a car

From Model Town, a cab or an auto booked through an app is the simplest choice. Set the drop point to Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road. To be sure the driver stops at the right gate, ask us on 096467 13555 to share our location and forward it to them. That works better than reading out directions over the phone.

## Why people from Model Town make the drive

The drive out to Daad brings you to open lawn, tables under palm trees and string lights in the evening. Guests have described it as feeling "close to nature" (gurvinder kaur, Google review). The food is North Indian, tandoor and Indo-Chinese, and our house dishes include the Atta Chicken (₹925), chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough.

A few practical points:

- Open 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day.
- Browse every dish and price on the [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/). Prices include GST.
- Planning a birthday or a family function: see how [parties on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/) work.
- Want the wider context of the road: the [Pakhowal Road guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/pakhowal-road-guide/) covers where it runs and how far common starting points are.

Book a table or a party by message or phone at 096467 13555 with your date, time and number of guests. Directions from other parts of the city are on the [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Naan, Roti and Paratha: Every Bread at Red Wood Farm, Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/indian-breads/

In short: Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana lists 14 breads, from Tandoori Roti and Tawa Roti at ₹20 to Cheese Naan at ₹80, with Butter Naan at ₹45 and Garlic Naan at ₹55. Four stuffed parathas with butter, from ₹50 to ₹60, sit in the Sides section. All prices include GST.

Q: What is the cheapest bread at Red Wood Farm?
A: Tandoori Roti and Tawa Roti, both at ₹20. They are also the lowest prices anywhere on our menu.

Q: Do you have aloo paratha?
A: Yes. Aloo Paratha with Butter is ₹50 and sits in the Sides section with Gobi, Mix and Cheese parathas. We open at 10 AM, so it works for a late breakfast.

Q: Are the breads vegetarian?
A: Yes. Every bread on the menu carries the green veg mark, including the stuffed parathas.

Q: Is there a maize-flour roti to go with saag?
A: The menu has no maize-flour bread. When Saag (seasonal) is on, at ₹275, Missi Roti (₹30) or Tandoori Roti (₹20) are the heartier choices to go with it.

Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road lists 14 breads, from Tandoori Roti and Tawa Roti at ₹20 to Cheese Naan at ₹80. Butter Naan costs ₹45 and Garlic Naan ₹55. Four stuffed parathas with butter sit in the Sides section at ₹50 to ₹60. Every bread is marked veg, and every price includes GST.

## Tandoor or tawa: what the names tell you

Two of our breads say how they are cooked right in the name.

**Tandoori Roti (₹20)** comes from the tandoor, a clay oven heated very hot. The dough is pressed onto the inside wall, where it puffs and chars in spots. The result is firm at the edges with a slight chew and a smoky taste.

**Tawa Roti (₹20)** is cooked on a tawa, a flat iron griddle. It is closer to the soft roti most Punjabi families make at home every day, with no char from the oven wall.

The menu doesn't say how the other breads are cooked, so here is what usually happens in North Indian kitchens:

- **Naan** is traditionally a tandoor bread made with refined flour, which makes it softer and puffier than roti.
- **Parathas** are usually cooked on a griddle with butter or oil. "Laccha" refers to the many flaky layers of the Laccha Paratha.
- **Roomali Roti** is a very thin roti. The name compares it to a handkerchief, a reference to how thin and soft it is.
- **Missi Roti** is usually made with gram flour mixed into the dough with spices, which gives it a yellow color and more flavor.

If you want to know exactly how a bread is cooked in our kitchen, ask us. For more on the clay oven, read our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/tandoor-guide/).

## Which bread goes with which dish?

Pick the bread by how thick the gravy is and how rich the dish already tastes.

### Thick, rich dals and gravies

Dal Makhni (₹275) is heavy with butter, so a bread that scoops well suits it. Butter Naan (₹45) or Laccha Paratha (₹45) are the usual picks. Missi Roti (₹30) gives it a spiced edge. More on that pairing is on our [dal makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/dal-makhani/).

### Butter Chicken and creamy curries

Garlic Naan (₹55) stands up to Butter Chicken (Half ₹415, Full ₹695) and Shahi Paneer (Half ₹225, Full ₹375). Plain Naan (₹25) is the choice if you want the gravy to do the talking. See every chicken gravy on our [chicken curries page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/chicken-curries/).

### Drier dishes

Kadhai Paneer (Half ₹225, Full ₹375) and Kadhai Chicken (Half ₹350, Full ₹600) have a thick, clinging masala. Roomali Roti (₹30) folds around them neatly, and Tandoori Roti (₹20) gives more bite.

### Chickpeas and seasonal greens

Chana Masala (₹275) goes well with Laccha Paratha or Onion Naan (₹55). When Saag (seasonal) is on, at ₹275, Missi Roti or Tandoori Roti are the heartier partners.

### When rice is better

Rajmah (₹230) and Kadhi Pakoda (₹230) are usually eaten with rice in Punjab. Our [biryani and rice page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/biryani-and-rice/) covers those pairings.

## Stuffed parathas as a meal

The parathas in the Sides section are filling enough to eat on their own. Since we open at 10 AM, they make a good late breakfast on the lawn. Order an Aloo Paratha with Butter (₹50) or a Gobi Paratha with Butter (₹55) with:

- Plain Curd, ₹125
- Mango Chutney, ₹55
- Rajasthani Hari Mirch Masala Pickles, ₹65
- Farm to Table Special Herbs Chutney, ₹75, our own herb chutney

The Paneer Paratha (₹55) and Mirchi Paratha (₹55) from the Breads section work the same way.

## How many breads should you order?

As a rough guide, most adults eat two or three pieces of bread with a curry meal, and children eat fewer. Breads are cheap next to the mains, so it is easy to order a first round and add more once you see how the table is eating. Mixing a few kinds, say Butter Naan, Garlic Naan and Tandoori Roti, lets everyone try something.

## Coming in or ordering bread with your takeaway

Red Wood Farm is at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, across from Cerajot Tiles and close to Omaxe Flats. We're open from 10 AM to 11 PM, all week. To book a table or add breads to a takeaway order, message 096467 13555. Every bread and dish is listed on the [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/).

## New Year's Eve Family Dinner in Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/new-years-eve-family-dinner/

Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road suits a New Year's Eve family dinner on its fairy-lit garden lawn. Regular hours are 10 AM to 11 PM, so plan an evening meal and see in midnight at home, and ask us at 096467 13555 about New Year's Eve itself. You order from the regular menu, with GST included.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm stay open past midnight on New Year's Eve?
A: Our regular hours are 10 AM to 11 PM. Ask us at 096467 13555 about New Year's Eve before you plan around a later time.

Q: Is there a New Year's Eve package or entry fee?
A: We don't publish any package. You order from the regular menu, where every price includes GST. Ask us about anything specific to the night.

Q: Is the lawn comfortable for grandparents on 31 December?
A: Older guests should know there is no wheelchair access and that the lawn is open air, so warm clothes help on a December night.

Q: How far ahead should we book for New Year's Eve?
A: Message us as soon as your family fixes the plan, and ask about New Year's Eve in the same message. We reply with what is possible that night.

For a New Year's Eve family dinner in Ludhiana, Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road offers tables on a garden lawn lit with fairy lights and a full menu with GST-inclusive prices. Regular hours run from 10 AM to 11 PM, so treat it as an evening meal and ask us at 096467 13555 about the night.

## What can we do on New Year's Eve with family?

Plenty of families skip the loud ticketed party and want a good dinner together, a few photos and a safe drive home before the roads fill up. Here is a simple plan that suits small children and grandparents alike.

1. **Eat early.** Book a table for the early evening. The children are still awake and cheerful, and the elders are not out late in the cold.
2. **Walk the tunnel.** After dinner, walk through the fairy-light tunnel, the spot our guests photograph most. Warm white lights over a red carpet make a fine last family photo of the year.
3. **Stop at the name arch.** The "Red Wood Farm" name arch and the green neon sign give you two more backdrops.
4. **See in midnight at home.** Our regular hours end at 11 PM, which leaves time to drive home and watch the countdown together on TV or from the roof.

For the night itself, ask us what we have planned for New Year's Eve. This page doesn't promise a countdown or late opening.

## What should three generations order?

A table with a seven-year-old and a seventy-year-old needs range. Order a lighter base, a few rich dishes and something the kids will finish.

- **Lighter dishes:** Tomato Shorba (₹145), Yellow Dal Tadka (₹245), Palak Paneer (₹225 half, ₹295 full) and Steamed Rice (₹180).
- **The rich dishes for the night:** Dal Makhni (₹275), Paneer Butter Masala (₹225 half, ₹345 full), Mutton Rogan Josh (₹345 half, ₹645 full) and Farm to Table Special Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full), our house signature chicken.
- **For the children:** Cheese Naan (₹80), French Fries (₹195), Veg Cutlet (₹245) and Chicken Popcorn (₹385).
- **To end the year on something sweet:** Paneer Jalebi with Rabri (₹75), Rasmalai (₹45) or Chocolate ice cream (₹55 a scoop).

Half portions on many curries let a family try more without over-ordering. The [full menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) has the rest, and the [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/group-ordering-guide/) explains half and full sizes.

## How do we get there and back on a busy night?

The last night of the year brings extra traffic to the city. The times below come from route data without traffic, so leave well before your booking.

- Pakhowal Road at Hero Bakery Chowk: 6.1 km, about 10 minutes
- Dugri: 6.5 km, about 12 minutes
- Sarabha Nagar: 6.8 km, about 11 minutes
- Model Town: 6.9 km, about 11 minutes

The address for your map is 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana. Directions and the pin are on the [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/).

## What if we would rather eat at home?

Takeaway works for New Year's Eve too. Order by phone or message on 096467 13555, collect the food on your way home and serve it as midnight gets close. A Veg Biryani (₹325) or Non-Veg Biryani (₹375) is an easy one-pot order for a home table, with Boondi Raita (₹165) on the side. Place the order early in the evening, since our regular hours end at 11 PM.

## Could New Year's Day lunch work better?

Some families find the evening of 31 December too crowded, with relatives at other parties and children who won't last until late. A lunch on 1 January is a calmer way to start the year together. We open at 10 AM, so a late-morning table gives you the whole afternoon on the lawn. In daylight the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating, and on a clear day the winter sun makes a long lunch easy. Start with Sweet Corn Soup (₹155), move on to Paneer Tikka (₹375) and Tandoori Chicken (₹375), and finish with Kesar Kheer (₹75).

## What should we wear and bring?

The lawn is open air and the last night of December is cold in Punjab. Dress the children in layers and bring a shawl or blanket for the grandparents. If you want to bring a cake to cut for the new year, tell us and we will tell you what is possible at your table. The same applies to balloons or any small decoration you have in mind.

## Booking the last dinner of the year

Message or call 096467 13555 with the date, your preferred time and the number of guests, and ask what is on for New Year's Eve. If the family is still choosing between Christmas and New Year's Eve for the big meal, our [Christmas lunch page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/christmas-lunch-ludhiana/) has ideas for 25 December.
