## Open-air dining in Ludhiana: a garden lawn on Pakhowal Road
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/open-air-dining-ludhiana/

In short: Red Wood Farm is an open-air garden restaurant on outer Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana, open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM. Tables sit on a grass lawn, under palm trees and on low lounge seating beneath string lights, and you walk in through a fairy-light tunnel. Menu prices run from ₹20 to ₹925 with GST included.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm open for lunch or only in the evening?
A: Both. We are open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, so you can eat on the lawn in daylight or after the lights come on.

Q: Is there covered seating if it rains?
A: Our seating is mainly outdoors on the lawn. A covered tent dining area has been set up at an event, but we can't promise cover for a regular table, so message us on 096467 13555 before you set out on a wet day.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm good for a couple's dinner?
A: For two people, the tables under the palm trees or the low lounge seating under string lights work well. Send your date and time and ask which tables are free.

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from Sarabha Nagar?
A: About 6.8 km by road, around 11 minutes without traffic, via Pakhowal Road. Leave extra time in the evening rush.

Red Wood Farm is an open-air garden restaurant on outer Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana, open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM. You eat at tables on a grass lawn, under palm trees or on low lounge seating beneath string lights. Guests arrive through a walk-through tunnel of fairy lights.

## What the open-air space looks like

What follows is drawn from our own photos of the place.

You come in through a garden gate and a green hedge arch with flowers, and past a "Red Wood Farm" name arch. A green neon sign with our name sits on the grounds.

The part guests photograph most is the fairy-light tunnel. It's a walk-through arch of warm white lights over a red carpet, with green uplights in the trees on either side. A stone garden path runs through the grounds by day. At night, lamp posts light the paths, and the palms along the driveway are wrapped in fairy lights. Trees around the grounds are wrapped in lights too.

The lawn itself has three kinds of seating:

- **Dining tables on the open grass**, with the sky overhead
- **Tables under the palm trees**
- **Low lounge seating under string lights**, with cushions on the ground

In daytime we also set out long wooden tables and lounge seating on the lawn.

One Google reviewer, gurvinder kaur, said the place "felt like close to nature." On 14 Nov 2026 we had a Google rating of 4.2 from 72 reviews.

## When to come: daytime or evening

Both work, and they feel quite different.

**Daytime** suits a family lunch or a slow weekend meal. You get the green of the lawn and trees, and the long tables make it easy to seat a bigger family together.

**Evening** is when the lights do the work. In Ludhiana the sun sets before 6 PM through the winter months and after 7 PM in summer. Arrive a little before sunset and you'll see the tunnel and the palms switch from daylight to fairy lights while you order. We stay open until 11 PM.

A few honest notes on weather. This is an open-air restaurant, so the sky decides a lot. A covered tent dining area with chandeliers has been set up at an event, but we can't promise cover for an ordinary table. On a day with rain in the forecast, message us on 096467 13555 before you leave home. Punjab winter evenings get cold, so bring a warm layer if you plan to sit out late.

## Open-air dining for couples

For two people, the tables under the palms and the lounge seating under the string lights are the coziest spots on the lawn. The lawn is shared with other diners. If you want a particular spot, send the date and time and ask which tables are free.

A simple dinner for two from the [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/):

- **Tandoori Chicken** ₹375
- **Kadhai Paneer** ₹225 half
- Two **Garlic Naan** at ₹55 each
- Two **Rasmalai** at ₹45 each

That comes to ₹800, with GST already in the price.

If you both eat veg, try **Paneer Tikka** ₹375 and **Dal Makhni** ₹275, with two **Butter Naan** at ₹45 each and two **Gulab Jamun** at ₹35 each. That order totals ₹810. For more starters, see our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/tandoor-guide/).

The fairy-light tunnel makes a good first stop for a photo of the two of you. Walk through it on the way in, before you sit down to order.

## What open-air dining here costs

Our menu prices are published and include GST. They run from ₹20 for a Tandoori Roti up to ₹925 for **Atta Chicken**, our chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough. Some everyday reference points:

- **Dal Makhni** ₹275

Many mains come in half and full portions, which keeps the bill sensible for two or three people.

## A garden lawn or a rooftop?

Red Wood Farm is at ground level. We have no rooftop. If you're comparing open-air places in Ludhiana, the choice is mostly about setting. Rooftop restaurants in the city give you height and a view over the streets. A garden gives you grass underfoot, trees and room to move around. Children have space on the grass, though we don't have a play area, so keep an eye on them near the paths.

The other difference is distance. We're on outer Pakhowal Road, near Daad village. By road we're about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar, 6.5 km from Dugri and 6.9 km from Model Town. Without traffic that's roughly 11 or 12 minutes from each. Evenings are busier, so leave extra time.

## Outdoor vs Indoor Party Venues: An Honest Comparison for Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/outdoor-vs-indoor-party-venues/

An outdoor lawn gives you space, fresh air and lit-up photos after dark, while an indoor hall protects you from heat, rain and cold and is easier for elders. In Ludhiana the month decides most of it: October to March suits a lawn, and May, June and the monsoon push many parties indoors.

Q: Is an outdoor party a good idea in Ludhiana in December?
A: Yes, if you plan for the cold. A lunch or an early evening start works well. Ask guests to bring warm layers, and expect fog late at night in December and January.

Q: What happens if it rains on the day of an outdoor party?
A: Ask the venue for its rain plan before you book. At Red Wood Farm, our photos show a covered tent dining area with chandeliers set up at one event, so ask us on 096467 13555 whether a tent is possible for your date.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm have wheelchair access?
A: No. Red Wood Farm does not have wheelchair access. Please plan for that if a guest uses a wheelchair.

Q: Are outdoor venues cheaper than indoor halls?
A: Not as a rule. The cost depends on the per-plate quote, decor and time slot at each place, so compare written quotes for the same guest count.

Pick an outdoor venue when the weather is mild and you want space, fresh air and lit-up photos after dark. Pick an indoor hall for peak heat, the monsoon, guests in wheelchairs, or music that runs loud and late. In Ludhiana, the calendar settles most of this decision.

## What does an outdoor lawn do well?

- **Room to move.** Guests spread out into small groups and can talk without raising their voices. Children have grass to run on.
- **Air.** No stale room smell, no heavy air conditioning, and the tandoor smoke drifts away.
- **Photos after dark.** Lights in trees and over paths look far better on a phone camera than a ceiling of tube lights.
- **A softer mood.** People stay longer when they can sit back under the sky.

## Where does an outdoor lawn fall short?

- **Weather.** Heat, rain, wind and cold all reach you. A plan B is part of the booking.
- **Insects.** Mosquitoes come out in the monsoon and after sunset in warm months.
- **Uneven ground.** Grass and garden paths are harder for elders and for anyone in heels.
- **Sound spreads.** Speeches get lost unless someone uses a mic, and music travels further.
- **Light fades.** A daytime party needs shade, and an evening party depends on how well the grounds are lit.

## When is an indoor hall the better choice?

People searching for indoor birthday party places in Ludhiana usually have one of these reasons, and they're good ones:

- The date falls in May or June, when afternoons are very hot.
- The date falls in the monsoon, roughly July to September.
- Several guests are elderly, unsteady on grass or use a wheelchair.
- You want a DJ and dancing until late.
- The group is small and you want a private room.

When you visit an indoor hall, check a few things in person: whether the air conditioning keeps up with a full room, whether there's power backup, whether a lift or ramp exists if the hall is upstairs, and how high the ceiling is if you plan balloon decor.

## How do Punjab's seasons change party timing?

| Months | Outdoor party | Best time of day |
|---|---|---|
| October to November | Good | Evening |
| December to January | Good with warm clothes | Lunch or early evening; fog late at night |
| February to March | Good | Lunch or evening |
| April | Fair | After sunset |
| May to June | Hard | Only late evening, and still warm |
| July to September | Risky | Plan a covered backup for rain |

If you're set on a lawn in summer, start the party after sunset and keep it short. In winter, a lunch party gives you the warm part of the day. Our [winter evenings on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/winter-evenings-on-the-lawn/) page has more on cold-weather dinners outdoors.

## How much does lighting matter?

More than most hosts expect. An indoor hall gives even light everywhere, so photos are predictable but rarely special. Outdoors, the lighting is the decor.

At Red Wood Farm, guests arrive through a walk-through tunnel of warm white fairy lights over a red carpet, with green uplights in the trees. It's the spot guests photograph most, and our [fairy-light tunnel page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/) has more on it. Past it, there are lit garden paths with lamp posts, palms along the driveway wrapped in fairy lights, string lights over low lounge seating, and a green neon "RED WOOD FARM" sign.

For a daytime party, look for shade. Our lawn has tables under palm trees and long wooden tables with lounge seating in daytime.

## Will elders be comfortable at an outdoor venue?

It depends on the venue and the planning. Grass, stone paths and steps are the main problems. We'll say it plainly: Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access. If a guest uses a wheelchair, an indoor venue with step-free entry is the better pick.

For elders who can walk short distances, a few steps help at any lawn:

- Seat them at a table near where food is served, so they don't cross the lawn with a plate.
- Keep their table away from the speakers.
- In winter, bring shawls and start earlier.
- In summer, start late and keep water within reach.

## Which is louder, outdoor or indoor?

Indoors, sound bounces. A small hall with a DJ gets loud fast, which is fun for dancing and hard on conversation. Outdoors, sound drifts off, so you need less volume for the same mood, though music carries further beyond the venue.

Every venue has its own rules on music and closing time. Ask before you book. For Red Wood Farm, ask us about music for your event.

## Red Wood Farm as an outdoor example

Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant and party lawn on outer Pakhowal Road. Our own photos show an open grass lawn with dining tables, buffet counters set up on the lawn, birthday balloon arches and a mehndi stage. At one event, a covered tent dining area with chandeliers was set up. We don't describe any indoor hall on this site, so if you need indoor space, ask us what's possible.

One guest, Inderpreet Singh, described it on Google as a "Good space for small function parties.."

If you're still weighing options, our guide on [how to choose a party venue in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/how-to-choose-a-party-venue-ludhiana/) lists the questions to ask any venue. For birthdays, see [birthday party venues in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/birthday-party-venues-ludhiana/). To see the lawn before deciding, find directions on our [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/). We're open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, and you can book by message or phone at 096467 13555.

## Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana: Where It Runs and How Far Things Are
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/pakhowal-road-guide/

Pakhowal Road is a Ludhiana road that runs from the city out towards Daad village. Routes from Ferozepur Road, Model Town, Sarabha Nagar and the railway station all join it, and OpenStreetMap labels its outer stretch Jodhan - Ludhiana Road. Red Wood Farm sits on that outer stretch, opposite Cerajot Tiles.

Q: Is Jodhan - Ludhiana Road the same as Pakhowal Road?
A: On the stretch near Daad, yes in practice. OpenStreetMap labels the outer part of the road Jodhan - Ludhiana Road, while local usage and our address call it Pakhowal Road.

Q: How far is Pakhowal Road from Ludhiana Railway Station?
A: OSRM's route from the station reaches Pakhowal Road after about 0.8 km on Ferozepur Road and continues to Red Wood Farm, 10.7 km from the station in total.

Q: Which villages are near outer Pakhowal Road around Red Wood Farm?
A: OpenStreetMap lists Daad (spelled Dad), Thakarwal, Lalton Kalan and Threeke within about 2.3 km of our pin in a straight line.

Q: What is Red Wood Farm's full address on Pakhowal Road?
A: 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, Opp. Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana, Punjab 142022.

Pakhowal Road is one of the roads that runs from Ludhiana city outwards, past the built-up neighborhoods and on towards Daad village. Routes from Ferozepur Road, Model Town, Sarabha Nagar and the railway station all feed into it. Near Daad, OpenStreetMap labels its outer stretch "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road". Red Wood Farm sits on that stretch.

This guide pieces the road together from real route data: OSRM routes over OpenStreetMap, checked on 17 Nov 2026. We describe only what that data shows, so treat it as a map reader's guide rather than a local history.

## Where is Pakhowal Road in Ludhiana?

Think of it as a road with an inner city part and an outer part.

**The inner part** is where the city's roads meet it. In our route data:

- From **Ferozepur Road**, the routes from the railway station and from Bharat Nagar Chowk turn onto Pakhowal Road after a short run of under 1.5 km on Ferozepur Road.
- From **Sarabha Nagar**, a short stretch that OpenStreetMap calls "Rotary Club" leads onto it.
- From **Model Town** and the **ISBT bus stand**, Krishna Mandir Road connects to it.
- Near **Hero Bakery Chowk** on Satpal Mittal Road, routes step off Pakhowal Road and rejoin it through Satpal Mittal Road and Krishna Mandir Road.

**The outer part** begins where OpenStreetMap switches the name. Every city route we checked ends with the same 2.8 km on "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road" before reaching Red Wood Farm. Around here, OpenStreetMap shows villages such as Daad, Thakarwal, Lalton Kalan and Threeke, along with residential areas like Palam Vihaar, Omaxe Royal Residency and Basant Avenue.

## Why the map shows two names

You will find the same road under two names. Signboards, addresses and conversation use "Pakhowal Road". OpenStreetMap, and apps built on it, may show "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road" for the outer stretch near Daad. Both lead to the same place. If your maps app shows the second name when you are looking for the first, you are on the right road.

There is a similar quirk with the village. Our address says Daad. OpenStreetMap spells it "Dad". It is the same village, about 0.8 km from our pin in a straight line.

## Pakhowal Road distances: how far is it from common starting points?

These are road distances to Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road, with OSRM's time estimates. OSRM assumes no traffic, so real trips take longer, especially at peak hours.

| Starting point | By road | OSRM time, no traffic |
|---|---|---|
| Ludhiana Railway Station | 10.7 km | about 16 min |
| Bharat Nagar Chowk, Ferozepur Road | 9.5 km | about 14 min |
| ISBT Ludhiana bus stand | 8.2 km | about 13 min |
| Model Town | 6.9 km | about 11 min |
| Sarabha Nagar | 6.8 km | about 11 min |
| Dugri | 6.5 km | about 12 min |
| Hero Bakery Chowk, Satpal Mittal Road | 6.1 km | about 10 min |
| Daad village | 1.2 km | about 2 min |
| Omaxe Royal Residency | 0.8 km | about 2 min |

Each figure is measured from the point OpenStreetMap uses for that place, so your own street may add or take off a little.

Turn-by-turn pages exist for five of these: the [railway station](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-railway-station/), [Bharat Nagar Chowk on Ferozepur Road](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-ferozepur-road/), [Model Town](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-model-town/), [Sarabha Nagar](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-sarabha-nagar/) and [Dugri](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-dugri/). Dugri is the odd one out. Its route uses Jawadi Road and joins Pakhowal Road only on the outer stretch, skipping the inner city part.

## Landmarks on the outer stretch

When you reach the Daad end of the road, three names from our address help you place yourself:

1. **Omaxe Flats**, the Omaxe Royal Residency development. OSRM lists it on Thakarwal Link Road, about 0.8 km from us by road.
2. **Daad village.** OSRM's route from the village uses Dad Link Road for about 0.3 km before joining Jodhan - Ludhiana Road.
3. **Cerajot Tiles.** Red Wood Farm is directly opposite.

Our gate opens off the road opposite Cerajot Tiles. Inside you will find a green hedge arch with flowers, a "Red Wood Farm" name arch, and garden paths lit by lamp posts at night.

## What Red Wood Farm is, for anyone new to this end of the road

Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant first and a party lawn second. We serve North Indian, tandoor and Indo-Chinese food from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day, on an open lawn with tables under palm trees and string lights. Takeaway can be ordered by phone or message. On Google we had a rating of 4.2 from 72 reviews when we checked on 14 Nov 2026.

There is no wheelchair access at Red Wood Farm, which matters if you are planning a visit for someone who uses a wheelchair.

## Before you set out on Pakhowal Road

Send us a message at 096467 13555 and ask us to share our location. A pin is more reliable than any road name on this stretch, and it saves guests from asking for directions on the roadside. Forward it to anyone joining you, especially relatives who don't know this end of the city. To book a table or a party, include your date, time and number of guests, or simply call. The [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/) has the address, hours and a summary of every route.

## Paneer Dishes at Red Wood Farm, Ludhiana, With Every Price
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/paneer-dishes/

In short: Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road, Ludhiana has 16 dishes with paneer in the name. Paneer Tikka and Paneer Achari Tikka cost ₹375 each, twelve paneer gravies run from ₹295 to ₹395 for a Full, and six of them come as a Half from ₹225. Prices include GST.

Q: Which paneer dishes come in a Half portion?
A: Six do: Palak Paneer, Shahi Paneer, Kadhai Paneer, Paneer Butter Masala and Lahori Paneer at ₹225 for a Half, and Paneer Lababdar at ₹255. The other paneer gravies come in a Full only.

Q: What is the cheapest paneer main course at Red Wood Farm?
A: Palak Paneer has the lowest Full price at ₹295, and its Half is ₹225. Lemon Paneer is next at ₹300 for a Full.

Q: Is Chilli Paneer a starter or a main course here?
A: On our menu Chilli Paneer sits in the vegetarian main course at ₹375 for a Full. It is cooked in the Indo-Chinese chilli style, so it also works as a shared plate before the other mains.

Q: Are Cheese Chilli and Cheese Tomato made with paneer?
A: The menu calls them cheese and does not say more. Ask us at 096467 13555 and we'll tell you what goes into them.

Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road has 16 dishes with paneer in the name. Two are tandoor starters at ₹375. Twelve are main-course gravies priced from ₹295 to ₹395 for a Full, and six of those also come as a Half from ₹225. Paneer Paratha (₹55) and Paneer Jalebi with Rabri (₹75) complete the list. Prices include GST.

## Paneer starters from the tandoor

The Tandoori section has two paneer starters, and they cost the same.

- **Paneer Tikka, ₹375.** Cubes of paneer marinated and cooked in the tandoor, the clay oven, which gives them charred edges.
- **Paneer Achari Tikka, ₹375.** The same idea with achari spices, the flavors used in Indian pickles. Expect more tang and heat.

Both come in one size. Order them first and share them while the mains are cooked. If you like food from the clay oven, our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/tandoor-guide/) covers the rest of that section, including the veg and non-veg kebabs.

## Paneer main course with Half and Full prices

These twelve gravies all sit in the vegetarian main course and carry the green veg mark.

| Dish | Half | Full |
|---|---|---|
| Palak Paneer | ₹225 | ₹295 |
| Shahi Paneer | ₹225 | ₹375 |
| Kadhai Paneer | ₹225 | ₹375 |
| Paneer Butter Masala | ₹225 | ₹345 |

| Lahori Paneer | ₹225 | ₹395 |
| Paneer Do Pyaza | Full only | ₹375 |

The Half sizes make it easy to try two paneer gravies at once without over-ordering. Two Halves of Palak Paneer and Kadhai Paneer, for example, come to ₹450.

## How do the paneer gravies differ?

The menu gives no recipes, so here is what each name usually means in North Indian cooking. Ask us if you want the details of how our kitchen makes a dish.

### Named for a vegetable or a flavor

- **Palak Paneer:** paneer in a spinach gravy. It is usually milder and lighter than the cream-based dishes.
- **Paneer Do Pyaza:** "do pyaza" points to onions used twice, typically cooked into the gravy and added again in larger pieces.
- **Lemon Paneer:** the name points to lemon, so expect a sharper, tangier dish.

### Named for a cooking pot

- **Kadhai Paneer:** cooked in a kadhai, the deep iron wok of Punjabi kitchens. It is usually made with onion and capsicum and has a thicker, drier gravy.
- **Matka Paneer:** named for the matka, a clay pot.

### Rich and creamy by name

- **Shahi Paneer:** "shahi" means royal, and the dish is usually a rich, cream-based gravy.
- **Paneer Korma:** korma is generally a mild, creamy gravy.
- **Paneer Butter Masala:** a tomato and butter gravy, often a little sweet. It is usually the safest order for someone who doesn't like much heat.

### Other styles

- **Paneer Bhurji:** crumbled paneer cooked with spices, closer to a dry scramble than a curry. At ₹395 it is one of the highest-priced paneer dishes.
- **Chilli Paneer:** the Indo-Chinese dish of paneer tossed in a chilli sauce. Our [Indo-Chinese page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/indo-chinese/) lists the rest of that side of the menu.

### Names that don't explain themselves

Paneer Lababdar and Lahori Paneer sit at the top of the paneer price list, at ₹395 for a Full. Lahori refers to the city of Lahore, but neither name tells you much about the gravy. Ask us and we'll describe them.

## Paneer outside the main course

Paneer turns up in two more places on the menu.

- **Paneer Paratha, ₹55,** in the Breads section. A stuffed flatbread that works as a meal with Plain Curd (₹125) or a pickle.
- **Paneer Jalebi with Rabri, ₹75,** in the Dessert section. It is a sweet made with paneer and served with rabri, a thickened sweet milk. See our [desserts page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/desserts/) for the other sweets.

## What to order for a paneer-loving table

For two or three people, a starter plus two Half gravies keeps the table varied. One example:

1. Paneer Tikka, ₹375
2. Paneer Butter Masala, Half ₹225
3. Kadhai Paneer, Half ₹225
4. Butter Naan, ₹45 each, or Garlic Naan, ₹55 each

Add Jeera Rice (₹230) if your group eats rice. If some of you want a break from paneer, Dal Makhni (₹275) and Malai Kofta (₹275) are in the same vegetarian main course. The [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/vegetarian-guide/) covers the full meat-free menu.

Two dishes on the menu say cheese in the name: Cheese Chilli (₹325) in the appetizers and Cheese Tomato (Half ₹200, Full ₹375) in the main course. We haven't counted them here because the menu doesn't say they are made with paneer.

## Booking a table or ordering paneer to take home

Send your order or table request to 096467 13555 with the time and the number of people. You can see every section with prices on our [menu page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/).

## What is paneer jalebi with rabri?

In North Indian sweet shops, paneer jalebi is a jalebi made with paneer worked into the batter. It's fried, soaked in sugar syrup and usually softer and denser than the thin, crisp jalebi sold on the street. Rabri is milk cooked down slowly until it turns thick and sweet. The two go together because the cold, creamy rabri cuts the heat and sugar of the jalebi.

On our menu the dish is listed as Paneer Jalebi with Rabri, at ₹75. If you want to know exactly how our kitchen makes it, ask us and we'll tell you.

## Which desserts are seasonal?

Two desserts are marked seasonal on the menu:

- **Gajrela, 100 g (seasonal), ₹75.** Gajrela is grated carrot cooked slowly with milk and sugar until it turns soft and deep orange. In Punjab it's a cold-weather sweet. Ours is sold by weight, 100 g a serving.
- **Malpua Rabri (seasonal), ₹65.** Malpua is a small fried pancake soaked in syrup, served here with rabri.

"Seasonal" means the dish isn't guaranteed every day of the year. The fastest way to check is a message on the day.

## How do the ice creams work?

The Ice Creams section is priced per scoop. Order one scoop or several and the bill adds up scoop by scoop.

- Vanilla: ₹50 a scoop
- Strawberry: ₹50 a scoop
- Chocolate: ₹55 a scoop
- Tutti Frutti: ₹55 a scoop
- Ice Cream with Brownie: ₹95

Two scoops of Chocolate come to ₹110. One Vanilla and one Strawberry come to ₹100.

The Ice Cream with Brownie is the one exception on the veg marks. It carries the non-veg mark until we confirm the brownie is eggless. If your family avoids egg, pick one of the four plain flavors instead.

## Are the desserts vegetarian?

All eight items in the Dessert section carry the green veg mark. So do the four plain ice creams: Vanilla, Strawberry, Chocolate and Tutti Frutti. The only sweet with a non-veg mark is Ice Cream with Brownie, and that's a cautious mark while we check the brownie. A strictly vegetarian table can order any dessert on the list except that one. If anyone in your group has a dairy allergy, tell us when you order, because sweets like these are usually made with milk.

## Kheer or Kesar Kheer: what's the difference?

Both are rice cooked slowly in milk and sugar. Kesar Kheer adds saffron, which gives it a pale gold color and a light floral smell. On our menu Kheer is ₹65 and Kesar Kheer is ₹75, so the saffron version costs ₹10 more.

## Which dessert fits which kind of meal?

A few pairings that work, based on how the menu is built:

- **After tandoor and dal.** A heavy meal of kebabs, Dal Makhni and naan sits well with something cold. Rasmalai at ₹45 or a scoop of Vanilla at ₹50 is enough. Our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/tandoor-guide/) covers what to order before it.
- **For a sweet-tooth table.** Paneer Jalebi with Rabri at ₹75 is the richest choice on the list. Share one if you've eaten a lot.
- **For children.** A single scoop of Strawberry or Chocolate is the simplest order. Our page on [dishes children like](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/kids-favourites/) has more ideas.
- **On a winter evening.** If Gajrela is on that day, it's the seasonal choice. Ask before you order.

## How do desserts work for a party?

Ask us how desserts fit into your party order. For a birthday, a simple approach is to count guests and pick one or two sweets almost everyone eats, such as Gulab Jamun at ₹35 and a scoop of Vanilla at ₹50. If you're planning a birthday with us, our [birthday party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/birthday-party-venues-ludhiana/) explains how bookings work.

We don't list cakes on the menu. If you want to bring a cake for a celebration, ask us first.

## Plan your dessert stop

Red Wood Farm is open from 10 AM to 11 PM every day at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles. To check if Gajrela or Malpua Rabri is on today, or to book a table, message us on [096467 13555](https://wa.me/919646713555). You'll find every other sweet and savory dish in our [food guides](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Party planning checklist: how much food per guest for an Indian party
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/party-planning-checklist/

In short: a common rule of thumb for an Indian party is 6 to 8 starter pieces, 2 to 3 breads, a small bowl of dal and about 100 to 150 grams of each main dish per adult, with children under ten counted as half. These are general planning figures. For ordering at Red Wood Farm, ask us at 096467 13555.

Q: How many starters should I serve at an Indian party?
A: As general guidance, three or four starter varieties adding up to about 6 to 8 pieces per adult is a common plan when a full meal follows. Serve more if starters run for a long time before dinner.

Q: How much rice should I plan per person?
A: A common rule of thumb is about 100 to 150 grams of cooked rice per adult when breads are also served, and a little more when rice is the main carb.

Q: How many rotis or naans should I plan per guest?
A: Plan about 2 to 3 breads per adult as general guidance. Naan is heavier than roti, so lean lower if the bread is mostly naan.

Q: How do I work out how much to order at Red Wood Farm?
A: Send us your headcount and the veg and non-veg split at 096467 13555. Many mains come in half and full portions, and our group ordering guide explains how to size them.

A common rule of thumb for an Indian party is 6 to 8 starter pieces, 2 to 3 breads, one small bowl of dal and about 100 to 150 grams of each main dish per adult guest. Count children under ten as roughly half an adult. Treat these as general planning figures, separate from Red Wood Farm's own portion sizes.

## Food per guest: a quick reference

These quantities are general guidance used widely for home parties and catering in North India. They are starting points to adjust for your crowd. They are not the portion sizes of any dish on our menu.

| Item | Per adult guest (general guidance) | Adjust when |
|---|---|---|
| Starters | 6 to 8 pieces across all varieties | Starters run long before dinner: go higher |
| Dal | About 100 to 150 g cooked, one small bowl | Two dals on the menu: split the amount |
| Each main dish (paneer, chicken, mutton) | About 100 to 150 g | Four or more mains: reduce each |
| Rice | About 100 to 150 g cooked | Rice is the main carb: go higher |
| Breads | 2 to 3 pieces | Mostly naan: go lower |
| Raita | About half a cup | Hot weather: go higher |
| Salad | About 50 to 75 g | Heavy starters: go lower |
| Dessert | 1 to 2 pieces, or one portion | Two desserts: smaller of each |

A few patterns hold at most parties. Guests who wait a long time for dinner tend to eat more than the table suggests. Lunch parties usually eat a little less than dinner parties. People eat more of the first dish served and less of the fifth, so a long menu needs smaller quantities of each item.

## Buffet or served meal: how the quantities change

The difference is small. At a buffet, guests take a spoon of almost everything, so each dish needs to cover most of the room even if it is a side. Plan the full per-guest figure for every main. When food is served to the table, hosts can watch what runs out and order more, so it is easier to start lower and add.

Leftovers are the other side of the same sum. Ordering mains in smaller portions first and adding a second round wastes less than ordering everything large at the start. Ask your venue how quickly a second round can come out.

## How much dal makhani per person?

As general guidance, plan about 100 to 150 grams of cooked dal makhani per adult, which is roughly one small bowl. If it is the only dal, stay near the top of that range, because many guests take a second helping with naan. If there is a second dal or a kadhi on the menu, plan less of each.

At Red Wood Farm, **Dal Makhni** is ₹275 on the menu, sold in one size. How many people one order serves depends on what else is on the table, so ask us when you book. Our [dal makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/dal-makhani/) covers the dish in more detail.

## Headcount: build in a buffer

Food quantities only work if the headcount is right. A few habits help:

- **Count confirmed guests, then add a buffer.** Many hosts plan for 5 to 10 percent more than their confirmed number to cover extra arrivals.
- **Split veg and non-veg early.** It changes how many of each main you need.
- **Count children separately.** Small children eat far less than adults, and teenagers often eat more.
- **Give the venue a final number** two or three days before the party, and ask how late you can change it.

## A simple party planning timeline

**Four to six weeks before:** fix the date, a rough guest list and your budget. Shortlist venues and check availability. Our guide on [choosing a party venue in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/how-to-choose-a-party-venue-ludhiana/) helps with this step.

**Two to three weeks before:** book the venue, send invitations and pick a theme or decoration plan. Shortlist the menu.

**One week before:** chase replies, confirm the cake and any decorator, and settle the menu.

**Two to three days before:** give the venue your final headcount and veg split. Share the location pin with guests.

**On the day:** arrive early to check the set-up, keep one phone number for the venue, and name one family member to handle questions.

For costs, our [birthday party budget guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/birthday-party-budget/) shows how to plan the spend line by line.

## What to ask a venue before you book

- Is the space private for your group, and does it fit your headcount comfortably?
- What happens if the weather changes, for an outdoor area?
- When does your slot start and end, and can you arrive early to set up?
- Can you see the menu in writing, with prices, and is GST included?
- Are veg and non-veg dishes clearly marked?
- What decoration, cake or music can you bring?
- How much is the advance, and what happens if you change the date?
- Is there wheelchair access for older guests?
- Who is your contact on the day?

## Ordering for a party at Red Wood Farm

On our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/), every price includes GST and every dish carries a veg or non-veg mark. Many main-course dishes come in half and full portions, which makes it easier to match an order to your group. For example, **Kadhai Paneer** is ₹225 half and ₹375 full, and **Butter Chicken** is ₹415 half and ₹695 full. Breads are priced singly, from **Tandoori Roti** at ₹20 to **Butter Naan** at ₹45.

Our [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/group-ordering-guide/) walks through sizing an order for a table at Red Wood Farm. A note for older guests: there is no wheelchair access here.

## Next step

Send your date, time, headcount and veg split to 096467 13555, and we'll reply with what works for your party. We are open every day from 10 AM to 11 PM. See past set-ups on our [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Punjabi Winter Food: Saag, Gajrela, Pinni and What to Order
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/punjabi-winter-food/

Punjabi winter food follows the cold-season harvest: mustard greens for saag, red carrots for gajrela, fresh peas, fenugreek and cauliflower, plus ghee-rich sweets like pinni. At Red Wood Farm the seasonal Saag is ₹275 and Gajrela, 100 g is ₹75; makki di roti and pinni are not on our menu.

Q: Is gajrela the same as gajar halwa?
A: Yes. Gajrela is the Punjabi name for the slow-cooked carrot and milk dessert. Ours is sold as Gajrela, 100 g (seasonal) at ₹75.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm sell pinni or panjiri?
A: No. Neither is on our menu. For a warm winter dessert, try Malpua Rabri (seasonal) at ₹65 or Kesar Kheer at ₹75.

Q: Can I take saag home from Red Wood Farm?
A: We do takeaway when you order by phone or message on 096467 13555. Saag is seasonal, so ask first whether it's being cooked that day.

Q: Which month does saag season start in Punjab?
A: Mustard greens are a cold-season crop in Punjab, so homes start cooking saag as the weather turns cool in late autumn and keep at it through the winter.

Punjabi winter food follows the cold-season harvest: mustard greens for sarson da saag, maize flour for makki di roti, red carrots for gajrela, plus peas, fenugreek, radish and cauliflower. Ghee, jaggery and nuts go into sweets like pinni and panjiri. On our menu, the seasonal Saag (₹275) and Gajrela, 100 g (₹75) carry the season.

## Why does Punjab eat differently in winter?

Ludhiana's winter nights get cold, and December and January often bring thick fog. Food changes to match. Kitchens cook heavier dishes, use more ghee and butter, and make sweets that are meant to be eaten a little at a time over weeks.

The vegetables change too. Summer gourds and okra give way to leafy greens, carrots, peas and cauliflower. In many Punjabi homes, the first big pot of saag marks the start of winter.

## How are sarson da saag and makki di roti made?

Saag starts with mustard leaves, usually mixed with spinach and a wild green called bathua. The greens are chopped, boiled for a long time and mashed or churned until smooth. A spoon of maize flour thickens it. A final tempering of ghee, ginger, garlic, onion and green chilli goes on top, followed by white butter at the table.

Makki di roti is a flatbread made from maize flour. The dough has no gluten, so it cracks easily and is patted out by hand. It's cooked on a griddle and eaten hot, often with jaggery and a glass of buttermilk on the side.

At Red Wood Farm, Saag (seasonal) is ₹275 on the menu. Makki di roti is not on our menu. Most guests pair the saag with Missi Roti at ₹30, Butter Roti at ₹25 or Tandoori Roti at ₹20. Add a Laccha Onion Salad at ₹125 and it makes a full winter meal.

## Which winter sweets does Punjab make?

**Gajrela.** Grated red carrots are cooked slowly in milk until the milk disappears, then finished with sugar, ghee and dry fruit. Some families stir it for over an hour. Our Gajrela, 100 g (seasonal) is ₹75.

**Pinni.** Roasted wheat flour, ghee, sugar or jaggery and nuts, pressed into round balls. Families make a big batch and keep a tin in the kitchen all winter.

**Panjiri.** A loose, roasted mix of wheat flour, ghee, sugar and dry fruit, eaten by the spoonful.

**Lohri treats.** Around Lohri in January, homes hand out peanuts, popcorn, gachak and til rewari made with sesame and jaggery.

Pinni, panjiri and the Lohri treats are not on our menu. What we do have for a cold evening is Malpua Rabri (seasonal) at ₹65, Kesar Kheer at ₹75 and Gulab Jamun at ₹35. Our [desserts page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/desserts/) has more on our sweets. If you're planning a Lohri get-together, read our [Lohri celebration page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/lohri-celebration-ludhiana/).

## What winter vegetables and parathas should you try?

Winter is paratha season. Cauliflower, radish and fenugreek all get stuffed into dough or kneaded into it, and a plate with curd and butter makes breakfast or a late lunch.

- Gobi Paratha with Butter: ₹55
- Mix Paratha with Butter: ₹55
- Aloo Paratha with Butter: ₹50

We don't list a radish paratha.

Peas are everywhere in a Punjabi winter. Matar Methi, peas with fenugreek leaves, is ₹255, and Matar Pulao is ₹260. Spinach shows up in many dishes:

- Palak Paneer: ₹225 half, ₹295 full
- Palak Naan: ₹45
- Palak Chicken: ₹415 half, ₹695 full
- Palak Mutton: ₹325 half, ₹645 full

Bhartha, the mashed and spiced eggplant dish, is ₹230.

## Hot dishes for a cold evening

When the temperature drops after sunset, people start with a soup. Our Tomato Shorba and Hot & Sour are ₹145 each, Sweet Corn Soup is ₹155, and the non-veg Smoked Chicken soup is ₹265.

Mutton is another cold-weather favorite in Punjabi homes. Mutton Rogan Josh is ₹345 half and ₹645 full, and Shahi Mutton is ₹325 half and ₹695 full.

Fried and spiced fish is a classic winter order across Punjab. Our menu marks its whole fish section as seasonal. When it's on, Tawa Fish Fry is ₹565 and Fish Tikka Masala is ₹575.

Straight from the tandoor, Tandoori Chicken (₹375) and Paneer Tikka (₹375) arrive hot, which matters on an open lawn in December.

## What does "seasonal" mean on our menu?

A few dishes on our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) carry the word seasonal: Saag, Bhindi, Gajrela, Malpua Rabri and the fish dishes. It means they're cooked when the ingredients are right, and availability can change from week to week. If you're driving out for one particular dish, send us a message on 096467 13555 first and we'll tell you whether it's on.

All our prices include GST.

## Eating winter food on the lawn

Red Wood Farm is a garden restaurant with dining tables on an open lawn, under string lights and palms wrapped in fairy lights. On winter evenings that's part of the appeal. Dress warmly and bring a shawl for older relatives. Our page on [winter evenings on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/winter-evenings-on-the-lawn/) has more on dining outdoors after dark.

You'll find us at 676, VPO Daad, on Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles. We're open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM. Book a table by message or phone with your date, time and number of guests. For the year-round Punjabi favorites, see our [Ludhiana food guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/ludhiana-food-guide/).

## Should a retirement party be a lunch or a dinner?

It depends on who is retiring and who is coming. A send-off for someone who spent decades in one office usually draws colleagues who are still on duty, so a long lunch on a working day lets them attend without giving up their evening. A school principal or a bank manager with a large family often prefers dinner, when spouses and grown children can come along.

At Red Wood Farm the kitchen starts at 10 AM, so a lunch can begin before noon and still leave room for speeches. By day the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating. After dark the palms along the driveway and the trees are wrapped in fairy lights, and the lawn has low seating under string lights. Decide on the mood first, then pick the hour.

## How do you seat colleagues and family together?

Farewells mix two groups who often have never met. Office staff cluster by department, and the family wants to sit close to the guest of honor. Ask us for one long table, or a run of joined tables, with the retiring person in the middle. The family can take one side and colleagues the other, and nobody has to shout across the lawn during the speeches.

For a large group, give us the number when you message. We will reply with what the lawn can take on your date. This page doesn't quote a fixed figure because the layout changes with each event.

## What should a farewell menu include for an office group?

Office groups are always mixed. Some people are vegetarian, some eat chicken but skip mutton, one person avoids spice and the younger staff want Indo-Chinese. Every dish on the [Red Wood Farm menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) carries a veg or non-veg mark, which helps the person ordering for a whole floor of colleagues.

A balanced spread could look like this:

- **Starters to pass around:** Paneer Tikka (₹375), Hariyali Tikka (₹325), Tandoori Chicken (₹375) and Chicken Popcorn (₹385).
- **Mains:** Dal Makhni (₹275), Shahi Paneer (₹225 half, ₹375 full) and Butter Chicken (₹415 half, ₹695 full).
- **One showpiece dish:** Atta Chicken (₹925), chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough.
- **Breads and rice:** Butter Naan (₹45), Laccha Paratha (₹45) and Jeera Rice (₹230).
- **Dessert:** Rasmalai (₹45) or Kesar Kheer (₹75).

Many main-course dishes come in half portions, so a smaller table can still try several curries. For help working out quantities, the [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party-planning-checklist/) goes through food per guest.

## Where do the speeches, the cake and the memento fit?

Most retirement parties follow a short program. The boss says a few words, the person retiring replies, someone hands over a shawl or a framed memento, and a cake gets cut. Run the program before the food arrives, while everyone is still seated and listening. Once the main course lands, attention drifts to the plates.

In your message, mention the cake, any banner or memento, and the time the speeches will start. If you want a microphone or music, ask about that too. We will tell you what is possible and where it can go.

## What about older guests and the drive out?

Retirement parties bring out older relatives and former colleagues who retired years ago. Two things matter for them. First, Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access, so check with any guest who uses a wheelchair before you fix the venue.

Second, the drive. We are at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats. From Sarabha Nagar it is about 6.8 km and from Model Town about 6.9 km, roughly 11 minutes each without traffic. Leave extra time on a weekday evening. The [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/) has the map pin to forward to your guest list.

## How is an office farewell different from a retirement?

A farewell for a colleague moving to another city or company is usually smaller and younger. It often happens at lunch on the person's last working day, with no formal program at all. The lawn makes an easy break from the office for that kind of goodbye. Order a couple of platters to share, such as the Tandoori Veg Platter (₹525) or the Non-Veg Platter (₹775), add Hakka Noodles (₹255) and French Fries (₹195), and let people come and go. Our page on [office team lunches](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/office-team-lunch-ludhiana/) covers weekday group lunches in more detail.

## Booking the farewell

Message 096467 13555, or call, with the date, the start time and roughly how many guests. Add whether it is a lunch or a dinner and whether there will be speeches or a cake. We reply with what is possible that day. Bookings don't go through the website, so a message is the quickest route. You can see more of the lawn on the [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Reunion and Get-Together Venue in Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/reunion-get-together/

For a school, college or family reunion in Ludhiana, Red Wood Farm offers a garden lawn with dining tables, a fairy-light tunnel for the group photo and a full menu with GST-inclusive prices. It is on outer Pakhowal Road, about 6.5 to 6.9 km from Dugri, Sarabha Nagar and Model Town. Book at 096467 13555.

Q: How far is Red Wood Farm from Ludhiana Railway Station?
A: About 10.7 km by road, roughly 16 minutes without traffic, by way of Ferozepur Road and Pakhowal Road. Allow extra time at busy hours.

Q: Can we bring a banner or a cake to the reunion?
A: Tell us at 096467 13555 what you want to bring, and we will tell you what is possible for your date.

Q: Is there space for children at a family reunion?
A: There is space on the grass for children to move around. There is no play area and there are no rides, so an adult should keep an eye on the little ones.

Q: What are Red Wood Farm's opening hours?
A: 10 AM to 11 PM, every day of the week.

Red Wood Farm is a garden restaurant and party lawn on outer Pakhowal Road that suits school batch, college and family reunions in Ludhiana. Your group gets tables on an open lawn, a lit tunnel for the group photo and a menu covering veg, chicken, mutton and Indo-Chinese dishes. Book at 096467 13555 with your date and numbers.

## Which kinds of reunions does the lawn suit?

### School and college batches

A batch reunion is loud and long. People arrive at different times, hug, change seats and pass phones around to show pictures of their kids. An open lawn handles that kind of movement more easily than a fixed restaurant booth.

### Cousins and the extended family

Family reunions often happen when relatives visit from abroad in winter. Grandparents, parents and children all need something on the menu, and the grass gives kids room to move. There is no play area and there are no rides, so they will need watching.

### Old colleagues

Former office teams who scattered years ago meet more easily on neutral ground. A weekend lunch on the lawn gives them a few hours to catch up without anyone having to host at home.

## How do you get a scattered group to turn up?

Attendance is the hardest part of any reunion. Fix the date at least three weeks out, put one person in charge of the list, and share the exact location before you share anything else. People decide on distance.

Here is how far Red Wood Farm is by road from common starting points. The times assume no traffic, so add a margin.

| From | Distance | About |
|---|---|---|
| Dugri | 6.5 km | 12 min |
| Sarabha Nagar | 6.8 km | 11 min |
| Model Town | 6.9 km | 11 min |
| ISBT bus stand | 8.2 km | 13 min |
| Bharat Nagar Chowk, Ferozepur Road | 9.5 km | 14 min |
| Ludhiana Railway Station | 10.7 km | 16 min |

Classmates coming in by train or bus for the day can take a cab from the station or the ISBT. The [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/) has the pin and directions for the group chat. The address to paste is 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats.

## What should a reunion group order when nobody agrees?

Reunion orders go wrong when one person orders for everyone from memory. Order in rounds instead. Start with platters while people are still arriving, then call for mains once you know who actually came.

Good opening rounds from our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/):

- Chinese Veg Platter (₹575) and Tandoori Non-Veg (₹725) for the table to share
- Honey Chilli Potato (₹255) and Chilli Paneer (₹375) for the college crowd
- Malai Champ (₹275) or Afghani Champ (₹275), both soya chaap and both vegetarian

For mains, put one dal, one paneer and one chicken or mutton dish on each table. Dal Makhni (₹275), Paneer Butter Masala (₹225 half, ₹345 full) and Mutton Rogan Josh (₹345 half, ₹645 full) cover most tastes. Half portions let a small table try more. Our [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/group-ordering-guide/) explains half and full sizes.

## How long can a reunion run?

We are open from 10 AM to 11 PM every day. A lunch reunion that starts at noon can stretch into the late afternoon, and a dinner can carry on until closing. Tell us your expected start and finish when you book, so the tables are ready and the kitchen can plan for several rounds of orders. If the group grows on the day, message us as soon as you know.

## Where do you take the group photo?

Every reunion ends with someone trying to fit every face into one frame. The fairy-light tunnel at Red Wood Farm is the spot guests photograph most. It is a walk-through tunnel of warm white lights over a red carpet, with green uplights in the trees. A line of old friends walking through it makes a livelier picture than a row of people squinting at a table.

For a daytime shot, the green hedge entrance arch and the "Red Wood Farm" name arch both work. You can read more about the [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/). Take the group photo early, before anyone has to leave.

## Planning the reunion with us

Send the date, a start time and a rough headcount to 096467 13555, or call the same number. If the count is still moving, give us a range and update it two days before. Mention anything you plan to bring, like a banner or a cake, and we will tell you what is possible. More on events at Red Wood Farm is on the [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

## Sarabha Nagar to Red Wood Farm, Pakhowal Road near Daad
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/from-sarabha-nagar/

Red Wood Farm is about 6.8 km from Sarabha Nagar by road. OSRM routes you along a short stretch OpenStreetMap labels Rotary Club, then Pakhowal Road out to Daad, in about 11 minutes with no traffic. We are opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats.

Q: How many minutes is Red Wood Farm from Sarabha Nagar?
A: OSRM estimates about 11 minutes for the 6.8 km drive, with no traffic. Leave a margin for signals and evening traffic.

Q: Do I need to go through the city center from Sarabha Nagar?
A: No. In OSRM's route you join Pakhowal Road after a short first stretch and stay on it, so you never go towards the railway station area.

Q: Can I order takeaway and pick it up on the way back to Sarabha Nagar?
A: Yes, takeaway is available. Order by phone or message on 096467 13555 and tell us when you will arrive.

Q: Which village is Red Wood Farm closest to?
A: Daad. OpenStreetMap places Daad village (spelled Dad on the map) about 0.8 km from our pin in a straight line.

From Sarabha Nagar, Red Wood Farm is about 6.8 km by road and takes about 11 minutes when the roads are clear. You need only three roads: a short link that OpenStreetMap calls Rotary Club, then Pakhowal Road, then its outer stretch towards Daad. We are opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats.

## The route at a glance

| Order | Road (as named on OpenStreetMap) | About |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rotary Club | 0.8 km |
| 2 | Pakhowal Road | 2.0 km |
| 3 | Jodhan - Ludhiana Road (outer Pakhowal Road) | 2.8 km |
| | **Total by road** | **6.8 km** |

Source: OSRM route, checked on 17 Nov 2026. The three named roads cover about 5.6 km. The remaining 1.2 km is lanes inside Sarabha Nagar and short junction links, which OSRM includes in the total but doesn't name.

## Where does the route start?

OSRM measured from the point OpenStreetMap uses as the center of Sarabha Nagar. Your own block may be a few hundred meters closer or farther, so the total for you could differ by a little. The order of roads stays the same for most of the neighborhood, because every route out of here meets Pakhowal Road early.

## Leg by leg

### Rotary Club, about 0.8 km

"Rotary Club" is the label OpenStreetMap gives this first stretch. It is an unusual name for a road and you may not see it on a signboard, so follow your navigation for this part. It is the shortest leg and it ends where you join Pakhowal Road.

### Pakhowal Road, about 2.0 km

This is the inner part of Pakhowal Road. Traffic here is city traffic, with junctions and signals. Stay on it and keep heading away from the city.

### Outer Pakhowal Road, about 2.8 km

OpenStreetMap switches the name to "Jodhan - Ludhiana Road" for this last stretch. Locals and our own address still call it Pakhowal Road. You are on the right road as long as you haven't turned off since the previous leg.

## How accurate is the 11-minute estimate?

OSRM calculates time with no traffic at all. On a Sunday morning you may come close to it. On a weekday evening, or the night of a big festival, expect it to take longer. Allow extra time at peak hours, especially if you have a table booked or guests waiting at a party.

Sarabha Nagar sits among the closer neighborhoods in our route data. For comparison, OSRM gives the same 11 minutes from [Model Town](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/from-model-town/) at 6.9 km, and 12 minutes from Dugri at 6.5 km.

## Spotting Red Wood Farm on the last stretch

Three markers tell you that you are almost there:

- **Omaxe Flats**, also called Omaxe Royal Residency, just off the road. OSRM puts it about 0.8 km from us by road.
- **Daad village**, which OpenStreetMap spells "Dad", under a kilometer from our pin.
- **Cerajot Tiles**, directly across the road from us.

When you reach Cerajot Tiles, Red Wood Farm is on the opposite side. Turn in at the garden gate. You will pass the green hedge arch with flowers, and in the evening the lamp-lit stone path takes you into the grounds.

Red Wood Farm does not have wheelchair access, so please plan ahead if someone in your group uses a wheelchair.

## Coming by cab or auto

If you are not driving, a cab or an auto booked through an app works well for a trip this short. Ask us on 096467 13555 to share our location, then forward that pin to your driver. It removes any doubt about which side of the road to stop on.

## Heading back to Sarabha Nagar

The return trip normally retraces the same three roads: outer Pakhowal Road, then inner Pakhowal Road, then the short link into Sarabha Nagar. Your maps app may choose a different line through a junction or two at night, which is fine. We close at 11:00 PM, so if you are booking a late dinner, plan the drive home with that in mind. If you came by cab, book the ride back from our gate and give the driver "opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats" as the pickup, so they stop on the right side of the road.

## What people from Sarabha Nagar come out for

Most visits from the city are a family meal on the lawn or a small party. A few things are worth knowing before you set off:

- We are open 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day.
- The [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) runs from ₹20 for a Tandoori Roti to ₹925 for the Atta Chicken, with GST included in every price.
- A weekend [Sunday lunch with the family](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/sunday-family-lunch/) is an easy plan from here, since the drive is one of the shorter ones in our route data.

To book a table or ask about a party, send your date, time and number of guests to 096467 13555, or call the same number. For other starting points, and for a wider look at the road itself, see the [Pakhowal Road guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/pakhowal-road-guide/) or go back to the [Visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/).

Q: Can teachers come to a student farewell at Red Wood Farm?

Q: Is there a minimum spend for a student group?

## Why hold a farewell in the daytime?

Most school farewells finish before dark because parents want their children home at a sensible hour. College groups often face the same rule from hostels and families. A late-morning or afternoon party settles that. The kitchen at Red Wood Farm opens at 10 AM, and in daylight the lawn has long wooden tables and lounge seating. Red Wood Farm's own photos include a kite-theme backdrop with flowers made for a daytime party, which shows how the lawn looks dressed for a day event.

Daylight also helps the photos. Farewell outfits, sarees and suits get photographed far more than the food. By day, the green hedge entrance arch, the stone garden path and the name arch all make easy backdrops.

## How do students keep the bill inside a budget?

Students usually split the cost, so the plan has to work for the person with the least pocket money. Build the meal around low-priced basics and add a few shared dishes on top.

Low-cost basics on our menu:

- Tandoori Roti (₹20), Butter Naan (₹45) and Aloo Paratha with Butter (₹50)
- Rajmah (₹230), Yellow Dal Tadka (₹245) and Dal Makhni (₹275)
- French Fries (₹195), Honey Chilli Potato (₹255) and Hakka Noodles (₹255)
- Gulab Jamun (₹35), Rasmalai (₹45) and Vanilla ice cream (₹50 a scoop)

Here is one sample order, priced item by item from the menu, to show how the numbers add up. One Dal Makhni (₹275), one full Kadhai Paneer (₹375), one Honey Chilli Potato (₹255), one Hakka Noodles (₹255), one Jeera Rice (₹230), twelve Butter Naan (₹45 each, so ₹540) and twelve Gulab Jamun (₹35 each, so ₹420). The total is ₹2,350, with GST already in it. This is regular menu pricing and not a package. Ask us how far each portion goes for your group before you lock the order.

## How should a big student group order?

A whole class calling out orders at once confuses everyone, the class included. Pick one person to collect choices a day ahead in the class group chat. Ask two questions only: veg or non-veg, and Indian or Indo-Chinese. Every dish on our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) carries a veg or non-veg mark, so the organizer can check in seconds. Vegetarian students have plenty to pick from, and our [vegetarian guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/vegetarian-guide/) lists the paneer, champ and dal dishes.

Order shared dishes for each table instead of individual plates. Farewells in Punjab usually include titles like Mr and Ms Farewell, a few performances and a lot of photos. Let the starters arrive while the titles are being announced, then send for the mains.

## What should parents and teachers know?

Parents usually ask four things: where it is, when it ends, who is in charge and what kind of place it is. Send the answers before they ask.

- **Where:** 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles, near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana. From Dugri it is about 6.5 km, and from Model Town about 6.9 km, around 11 to 12 minutes without traffic.
- **When:** a fixed start and finish time. A daytime slot gets everyone home before evening.
- **Who:** one student organizer and one teacher, with their phone numbers.
- **What kind of place:** Red Wood Farm is a family restaurant first, with a garden lawn for parties. Teachers and parents are welcome to come along.

One more point for the organizers: there is no wheelchair access, which matters if a teacher or student uses a wheelchair.

## Can a farewell have decorations, titles and music?

Most farewells have all three. Tell us what you are planning, such as a banner, a balloon arch, a spot for the titles or a speaker for music. Real photos from Red Wood Farm show balloon arches and decorated backdrops at past parties. For your own date, ask us what is possible on the lawn and we will give you a straight answer.

## Booking the farewell

Choose two possible dates, then message 096467 13555 with the date, the start time and the number of students and staff. A teacher or parent can make the booking if that is easier for the school. Past functions here have used a mehndi stage, draped set-ups and buffet counters on the grass. Send your numbers for a set-up suggestion.

## What past functions on our lawn looked like

Everything in this section comes from Red Wood Farm's own photos of real events.

- **A mehndi stage.** A flower-framed swing under a draped canopy, with flower beds along the front.
- **Draped function set-ups.** Canopies and curtains with green garland trim over the serving area.
- **Buffet counters on the lawn.** A long line of counters along one side, with round tables on the grass in front.
- **A covered tent dining area with chandeliers.** This was seen at one event, so ask whether it suits your date and size.
- **Decorated entry gates.** Guests walk in under a dressed gate before reaching the lawn.

Those set-ups were made for those families. Yours depends on the date, your guest count and what you want, so treat the photos as a starting point for the conversation. One guest wrote that it's "Good space for small function parties.." (Inderpreet Singh, Google review).

## Planning a roka

A roka is usually small and short, with close family from both sides, a simple ceremony and a meal. A daytime slot gives you natural light for family photos on the lawn.

A few things that help:

- Set one table for the elders of both families near the ceremony area, so they can see without standing.
- Mix the seating at lunch so the two families talk to each other.
- Keep the ceremony and the meal in one area of the lawn, which saves older relatives a walk.

## Planning an engagement

An engagement usually has a longer guest list and needs a focal point for the ring exchange: a stage, a decorated corner or a backdrop where the couple stands. An evening engagement gets the string lights and the fairy-light tunnel, which makes a good spot for couple photos between the ceremony and dinner. A daytime engagement gets the long wooden tables and lounge seating on the lawn.

Tell us which you prefer when you message, along with any decoration you plan to bring or arrange, and we'll confirm what works.

## Smaller get-togethers

Not every family function has a name. Relatives visiting from abroad, a cousins' lunch, or a gathering after a family milestone all need the same things: one long table, easy food and enough space for the children to wander on the grass. For a couple's milestone, see our page on [anniversary dinners](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/anniversary-dinner-ludhiana/). For a mother-to-be, see the [baby shower guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/baby-shower-venue-ludhiana/).

## How to plan a small function, step by step

1. **Fix the date and the time of day.** Daytime and evening feel very different on a lawn.
2. **Count guests by group.** Write down adults, elders and children separately, and for a roka or engagement, each family's side too.
3. **Decide how food is served.** Some families order from the menu; larger groups may want buffet counters. Ask us what suits your number.
4. **Say if the function is vegetarian only.** Every dish on our menu carries a veg or non-veg mark, which makes planning a mixed or all-veg spread simple.
5. **List your decoration.** A stage, drapes, an entry gate or flowers. Tell us early so we can confirm what's possible.
6. **Share the location with older relatives.** We're at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles. There is no wheelchair access.
7. **Confirm everything in writing.** Keep the final details in one message thread.

Our [party planning checklist](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party-planning-checklist/) helps with how much food to order per guest.

## What is the lawn like in the daytime?

By day the lawn is laid out with long wooden tables and lounge seating, with trees around the edges and a stone path running through the grounds. It suits a long, unhurried family meal where the children can get up between courses and walk on the grass. In the warmer months, ask for a table under the palm trees when you book. In winter, the midday sun is the reason to come for lunch instead of dinner. Bring a light layer anyway, because the shade under the trees cools down quickly once the afternoon moves on. Grandparents who feel the cold may prefer a table in the open sun.

## Vegetarian and non-vegetarian at one table

## Tandoori food on Pakhowal Road: a guide to our tandoor menu
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/tandoor-guide/

In short: Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road serves Tandoori Chicken at ₹375, with eight veg and nine non-veg dishes in its Tandoori section. The Tandoori Veg Platter is ₹525 and the Tandoori Non-Veg platter is ₹725. Breads start at ₹20 for a Tandoori Roti, and all prices include GST.

Q: How much is Tandoori Chicken at Red Wood Farm?
A: Tandoori Chicken is ₹375 on our current menu, and the price includes GST. The menu lists one portion size for it, with no half portion.

Q: Which tandoori dish should a first-time visitor order?
A: Most tables start with Tandoori Chicken (₹375) or Paneer Tikka (₹375). If your group can't agree, the Tandoori Non-Veg platter (₹725) or the Tandoori Veg Platter (₹525) lets everyone try more than one item.

Q: Is there vegetarian tandoori food at Red Wood Farm?
A: Yes. The Tandoori section has eight veg dishes, from Aloo Nazakat (₹245) to Mushroom Tikka (₹395), and the Champ section adds ten soya chaap dishes. Every dish carries a veg or non-veg mark.

Q: Can I order tandoori food for takeaway?
A: Yes. Call or message 096467 13555 with your order and a pickup time. We are open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

Red Wood Farm, on outer Pakhowal Road near Daad, serves Tandoori Chicken at ₹375 and a full tandoori section of eight veg and nine non-veg dishes, plus two tandoori platters and breads like Tandoori Roti at ₹20. Every price on this page comes from our current menu and includes GST.

## What makes a good tandoori chicken?

Tandoori food takes its name from the tandoor, the tall clay oven used across Punjab. The oven runs very hot, so meat and paneer cook fast and pick up dark, charred edges. Tandoori chicken is usually marinated in yogurt and spices before it goes in, which gives it the red color most people picture.

Which tandoori chicken is best comes down to taste. Some people want more char, some want more spice. A few things are worth checking at any restaurant: the chicken should be cooked through, the outside should have real color, and it should come to the table hot.

We won't tell you ours is the best on the road. What we can share is that Red Wood Farm held a Google rating of 4.2 from 72 reviews on 14 Nov 2026, and one reviewer, Gurveer Singh, wrote that the "food was absolutely delicious, fresh, and full of flavor." The fairest test is a plate of your own.

## The non-veg tandoori dishes and prices

- **Tandoori Chicken** ₹375

- **Chicken Cheese Kabab** ₹375
- **Bhatti Da Murg** ₹395

- **Pindi Seekh Kabab** ₹395

- **Punjabi Murg Tikka** ₹415

If two people are sharing, one chicken dish and one kabab gives you a contrast without overordering. Tandoori Chicken and Pindi Seekh Kabab together come to ₹770.

## Breads that go with tandoori starters

## How to order tandoori food for a table

Tandoori dishes work best as the first course. A simple way to order for a family of four:

1. Pick one veg and one non-veg tandoori dish. Paneer Tikka and Tandoori Chicken are ₹375 each.
2. Add a dal or a curry for the main course. **Dal Makhni** is ₹275. Many curries come in half and full portions, such as **Butter Chicken** at ₹415 half and ₹695 full.
3. Order one bread per person to start, such as four Butter Naan at ₹45 each.
4. Ask for more bread when the curries arrive.

That first order comes to ₹1,205 with GST already included. For six or more people, swap the two single dishes for a platter and add a second curry.

For a bigger group, such as a birthday or a family dinner of fifteen, message us first with the date, time and number of guests so the kitchen knows what's coming.

## The Fairy-Light Tunnel at Red Wood Farm, Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/

Red Wood Farm on Pakhowal Road has a walk-through tunnel of warm white fairy lights over a red carpet, with green uplights in the trees around it. It looks best after dark, and it's the part of the garden guests photograph most. We're open daily until 11 PM.

Q: Where is the fairy-light tunnel?
A: It's at Red Wood Farm, 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats, Ludhiana 142022.

Q: How late can I visit to see the lights?
A: Red Wood Farm is open every day until 11 PM, opening at 10 AM. Plan a dinner table for the evening and take photos before or after your meal.

Q: Is the tunnel wheelchair accessible?
A: No. Red Wood Farm has no wheelchair access, so plan around that before you travel.

Q: Do I need to book to see the tunnel in the evening?
A: We take table bookings by message or phone at 096467 13555. Send the date, time and number of guests.

The fairy-light tunnel at Red Wood Farm is a walk-through tunnel of warm white fairy lights over a red carpet, with green uplights shining up into the trees around it. It's at our garden restaurant on outer Pakhowal Road, near Daad village. Come after dark to see it properly. We're open every day until 11 PM.

## What does the fairy-light tunnel look like?

Picture an arched walkway hung with strings of small warm white bulbs. In our photos the strings run overhead and hang down both sides, so you're inside a soft glow once you step in. Underfoot is a red carpet that runs the length of the tunnel. Around it, green uplights light the trees from below, which adds a cool green edge to the warm white.

It's the spot guests photograph more than any other part of the garden. What you can count on is what's in our own photos: warm white lights, the red carpet and the green-lit trees.

## When is the best time to see the tunnel?

After dark. Small bulbs barely register against daylight. Once the sky goes dark, the warm white lights take over and the green uplights in the trees show up.

Sunset in Ludhiana comes earlier in winter and later in summer, so the time to arrive shifts through the year. A good plan is to book a dinner table for shortly after sunset. You get a few minutes of deep blue sky, which photographs well, and then full darkness while you eat.

If other guests are taking photos when you arrive, wait for a gap and give each group a turn. A clear shot of the empty carpet is worth a short wait.

## How do you take good photos in a fairy-light tunnel?

These are general tips for any phone in low light. They work well in a tunnel like ours.

**Set up the phone**

- Wipe the lens first. Fingerprints turn every bulb into a smear.
- Turn the flash off. Flash lights the person's face flat and drowns out the glow of the bulbs.
- Use night mode if your phone has it, and hold still for the full count.
- Tap on the person's face to focus, then drag the exposure down a little so the bulbs don't turn into white blobs.

**Frame the shot**

- Shoot down the length of the tunnel. The lines of lights and the red carpet lead the eye toward the person.
- Crouch low to get more of the red carpet in the frame.
- Have your subject stand a few steps inside, with the tunnel stretching out behind them. Distant bulbs blur into soft circles, especially in portrait mode.
- Leave space above the head so the arch of lights shows.

**Think about color**

- The light in the tunnel is warm white, so skin looks warm. If photos look too orange, adjust the warmth slider afterward.
- The carpet is red. Clothes in white, cream, gold or dark green stand out against it. A red outfit tends to blend into the carpet.

**For video**

- Walk slowly toward the camera, or have the person filming walk slowly backward down the carpet.
- Keep the phone at chest height and move smoothly. Short clips of 5 to 10 seconds are easier to keep steady.

## What else lights up in the garden at night?

Other parts of the grounds light up too. Palms along the driveway are wrapped in fairy lights, and so are several trees. Garden paths have lamp posts, and the lawn has low lounge seating under string lights. There's also a green neon "RED WOOD FARM" sign that makes a simple backdrop for a group photo. Our page on [an evening on the lawn](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/an-evening-on-the-lawn/) walks through a night visit, and [open-air dining in Ludhiana](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/open-air-dining-ludhiana/) covers the tables outside.

## Can the tunnel be part of a party evening?

Our own photos show birthday set-ups and small family functions on the lawn. If you're planning one, ask us how the lit garden and the tunnel fit into your evening, and how timing works for photos before guests sit down to eat. Our [party page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/) explains how bookings work.

## What should you know before you go?

- **Hours:** 10 AM to 11 PM, every day.
- **Access:** there's no wheelchair access.
- **Food:** plan your photos around a meal. Our [menu](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/) lists every dish with prices.
- **Getting here:** from Sarabha Nagar it's about 6.8 km and 11 minutes, from Dugri about 6.5 km and 12 minutes, and from Ludhiana Railway Station about 10.7 km and 16 minutes. Those times assume no traffic, so leave extra time in the evening.

## Book an evening table

Send your date, time and number of guests to [096467 13555](https://wa.me/919646713555) to book a table after dark. For directions, see our [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/). We're at 676, VPO Daad, Pakhowal Road, opposite Cerajot Tiles.

An easy weekend plan on the outskirts of Ludhiana starts with a drive out along Pakhowal Road to Daad, about 6.5 to 7 km from Dugri, Sarabha Nagar or Model Town. Visit a nearby gurdwara, then spend the afternoon or evening at Red Wood Farm, our garden restaurant, open from 10 AM to 11 PM daily.

## Why outer Pakhowal Road suits a short weekend

A weekend does not have to mean a long highway drive. Outer Pakhowal Road is close enough that you spend minutes in the car instead of hours, yet the built-up city gives way to villages and open ground along the way. You can leave after a late breakfast and be back home for the evening, or go out at sunset and be home by bedtime.

The drive is simple from several city neighborhoods. According to OpenStreetMap and OSRM routing, checked on 17 November 2026:

- **From Model Town** (6.9 km, about 11 minutes with no traffic): Model Town Road, Krishna Mandir Road, then Pakhowal Road.
- **From Dugri** (6.5 km, about 12 minutes): Phase 1 Road and Jawadi Road before you join the main road.
- **From Sarabha Nagar** (6.8 km, about 11 minutes): a short hop onto Pakhowal Road.

Every route ends on the same stretch, which OpenStreetMap names Jodhan - Ludhiana Road. Those times assume empty roads, so leave extra time. Our [Pakhowal Road guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/pakhowal-road-guide/) explains how the road runs out of the city.
