## A Saturday plan: gurdwara in the morning, lunch on the lawn

1. **Morning.** Visit Gurdwara Bhai Bala Sahib Ji, about 1.6 km from us on the map. Carry a scarf or handkerchief to cover your head, as at any gurdwara.
2. **Late morning.** Drive the short distance to Red Wood Farm. We open at 10 AM.
3. **Lunch.** Sit at the long wooden tables on the daytime lawn. Start with a Tandoori Veg Platter at ₹525 or a Non-Veg Platter at ₹775, then share a Dal Makhni at ₹275 and a half Paneer Lababdar at ₹255 with a basket of breads.
4. **Afternoon.** Walk the stone garden path through the grounds before heading home.

## A Sunday plan: late afternoon into the evening

1. **Around 4 or 5 PM.** Arrive while there is still daylight on the lawn and order something light, such as Honey Chilli Potato at ₹255 or a Masala Papad at ₹75.
2. **Dusk.** Watch the palms on the driveway and the trees light up. The fairy-light tunnel, warm white lights over a red carpet, is where most people take photos.
3. **Dinner.** Move to the tandoor and the curries. Our house signature, Farm to Table Special Chicken, is ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full.
4. **Home.** We close at 11 PM, which leaves time for an unhurried meal before an early Monday.

With children along, our page on a [family outing with kids](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/family-outing-with-kids/) adjusts these plans for younger legs.

## Planning a weekend get-together with friends

A weekend lunch is a good excuse to gather old classmates or the cousins who never make it to the same city at once. For a group, send us the date, time and number of guests, and tell us if it is a reunion or a celebration. Our page on [reunions and get-togethers](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/reunion-get-together/) explains how we host groups on the lawn.

## What about a weekend getaway near Ludhiana?

Searches for weekend getaways near Ludhiana usually turn up hill towns that take most of a day to reach. This page covers the other kind of weekend: a few hours out of the city and home the same night. Red Wood Farm serves meals, so plan a day or evening visit and drive back after dinner.

## Practical notes for the drive

- Open 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, every day of the week.
- There is no wheelchair access.
- Weekend tables are booked by message or phone at 096467 13555.
- Takeaway orders go the same way if you would rather eat at home.

## What Is Famous to Eat in Ludhiana: A Visitor's Food Guide
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/ludhiana-food-guide/

Ludhiana eats classic Punjabi food: dal makhani, tandoori chicken and paneer tikka, saag with makki di roti in winter, chole, stuffed parathas with butter, and lassi. At Red Wood Farm you can order most of the curries, tandoor dishes and parathas at listed prices, while lassi, kulcha, bhature and makki di roti are not on our menu.

Q: Does Red Wood Farm serve lassi?
A: No. Lassi is not on our menu. Our dessert list starts at ₹35 for Gulab Jamun and includes Rasmalai at ₹45 and Kheer at ₹65.

Q: Can I get makki di roti with saag at Red Wood Farm?
A: Makki di roti is not on our menu. Saag (seasonal) is listed at ₹275, and it goes well with Missi Roti at ₹30 or Tandoori Roti at ₹20. Ask us on 096467 13555 whether saag is on that day.

Q: Which single dish is Punjab best known for?
A: There isn't one answer. Dal makhani, butter chicken, tandoori chicken and sarson da saag with makki di roti are the dishes people name most often when they talk about Punjabi food.

Q: Do Red Wood Farm menu prices include GST?
A: Yes. Every price on our menu includes GST, so the listed price is the price of the dish.

Ludhiana is famous for everyday Punjabi food cooked generously: dal makhani simmered for hours, tandoori chicken and paneer tikka from the clay oven, sarson da saag with makki di roti in winter, chole, stuffed parathas topped with butter, and tall glasses of lassi. Most of it started as home cooking, and restaurants simply make it in bigger pots.

This guide explains what each dish is, so a first-time visitor knows what to order. Where Red Wood Farm cooks a version of it, you'll see our exact menu price. Where we don't, we say so.

## Which Punjabi dishes should a first-time visitor try?

Start with the dishes that show up on almost every Punjabi table.

- **Dal makhani.** Whole black lentils and a few kidney beans, cooked slowly, then finished with butter and cream. It is the dish most families order without looking at the menu.
- **Butter chicken.** Tandoor-cooked chicken in a mild tomato and butter gravy. It suits children and anyone who avoids heat.
- **Tandoori chicken.** Chicken marinated in yogurt and spices, then roasted on skewers in a clay oven until the edges char.
- **Sarson da saag with makki di roti.** Mustard greens cooked down to a thick puree, eaten with flat cornmeal bread and a lump of white butter. It's a winter dish.
- **Chole.** Spiced chickpeas, usually eaten with kulcha or bhature, or with rice at home.
- **Stuffed parathas.** Wheat flatbread filled with potato, cauliflower, radish or paneer, cooked on a griddle and served with curd and pickle.
- **Lassi.** A thick yogurt drink, sweet or salted.

## What does Ludhiana eat in the morning?

Parathas are the classic late-morning meal across Punjab. A plate usually means one or two stuffed parathas, a cube of butter melting on top, a bowl of curd and some pickle on the side.

Our doors open at 10:00 AM. The cheapest stuffed option is Aloo Paratha with Butter (₹50). Gobi Paratha with Butter and Mix Paratha with Butter cost ₹55 each, and the Cheese Paratha with Butter is ₹60. For the curd-and-pickle side, Plain Curd is ₹125 and Rajasthani Hari Mirch Masala Pickles are ₹65.

## What tandoor food is Ludhiana known for?

The clay oven is the center of Punjabi restaurant cooking. Meat and paneer go in on long skewers, breads stick to the hot inner wall, and everything picks up a smoky edge.

On our menu, Tandoori Chicken is ₹375, Punjabi Murg Tikka is ₹415, Bhatti Da Murg is ₹395 and Pindi Seekh Kabab is ₹395. Vegetarians can order Paneer Tikka at ₹375, Hariyali Tikka at ₹325 or Mushroom Tikka at ₹395. Tandoori Roti costs ₹20 and Butter Naan ₹45. Our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/tandoor-guide/) goes through the full list and what to order first.

Soya chaap also deserves a mention. Grilled or cooked in a creamy marinade, it is a common vegetarian order in north Indian cities. We list it as Champ: Malai Champ and Afghani Champ are ₹275 each, Achari Champ is ₹245 and Stuffed Champ is ₹300.

## Which curries and dals do people order most?

Dal makhani leads, and our Dal Makhni is ₹275. The [dal makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/dal-makhani/) covers how it's cooked and how much to order per person.

Butter Chicken is ₹415 for a half and ₹695 for a full. If you want something less rich, Chicken Curry is ₹395 half and ₹665 full. Kadhai Paneer and Shahi Paneer are each ₹225 half and ₹375 full.

Then there are the home-style dishes that many Ludhiana families eat on weekdays:

- Rajmah, kidney beans in an onion and tomato gravy, at ₹230. Pair it with Steamed Rice at ₹180 or Jeera Rice at ₹230.
- Kadhi Pakoda, a yogurt and gram flour curry with fritters, at ₹230.
- Chana Masala, our chickpea curry, at ₹275. We don't serve kulcha or bhature, so most guests eat it with naan or rice.

## What sweets is Punjab famous for?

Punjabi meals end with milk sweets. Gulab jamun, rasmalai and kheer are year-round favorites. Jalebi with rabri is a common treat, and in winter the carrot dessert gajrela and the wheat-and-ghee ball called pinni appear in most homes.

Our dessert list has Gulab Jamun at ₹35, Rasmalai at ₹45, Raj Bhog at ₹55, Kheer at ₹65 and Kesar Kheer at ₹75. Paneer Jalebi with Rabri is ₹75. Gajrela, 100 g is ₹75 and only in season. Pinni is not on our menu. For more on cold-weather dishes, read our [Punjabi winter food guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/punjabi-winter-food/).

## What's on the Red Wood Farm menu, and what isn't?

We cook North Indian, tandoor and Indo-Chinese food. The full list with prices is on our [menu page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/menu/), and every price includes GST. Every dish carries a veg or non-veg mark.

Here is the honest list of famous Ludhiana foods we do not serve:

- Lassi
- Makki di roti
- Kulcha and bhature
- Pinni

Saag is listed as Saag (seasonal) at ₹275, so call or message before you come for it.

Indo-Chinese is part of many Punjabi family dinners, and we cook it too. Hakka Noodles are ₹255, Honey Chilli Potato is ₹255, Manchurian Dry is ₹275 and Chilli Paneer is ₹375.

Two dishes are our own. Farm to Table Special Chicken, our house signature chicken, is ₹415 half and ₹695 full. Atta Chicken, chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough, is ₹925. Ask for our Farm to Table Special Herbs Chutney at ₹75 with your tandoor order.

One guest, Gurveer Singh, wrote on Google that the "food was absolutely delicious, fresh, and full of flavor."

## Where to eat it at Red Wood Farm

Red Wood Farm is a garden family restaurant at 676, VPO Daad, on Pakhowal Road opposite Cerajot Tiles and near Omaxe Flats. We're open from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM every day. You can eat in on the lawn or order takeaway by phone or message on 096467 13555. Directions from the railway station, Sarabha Nagar, Dugri and Model Town are on our [visit page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/visit/).

## What to Order at Red Wood Farm on Your First Visit
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/first-visit-what-to-order/

On a first visit to Red Wood Farm, start with a soup or a starter, share one tandoor plate, then order Dal Makhni (₹275), one curry, a round of breads and a dessert. Non-veg tables should try the house Farm to Table Special Chicken (Half ₹415, Full ₹695).

Q: What is the house dish at Red Wood Farm?
A: Farm to Table Special Chicken is our house signature chicken. It costs ₹415 for a Half and ₹695 for a Full.

Q: What is Atta Chicken?
A: It's chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough. At ₹925 it's the highest-priced dish on the menu, so it suits a table that wants to share one showpiece.

Q: Do I need to book a table for a first visit?
A: You can book by message or phone at 096467 13555. Send the date, time and number of guests. Booking ahead means your table is planned before you arrive.

Q: Is there a good vegetarian first order?
A: Yes. 131 of the 187 dishes are veg. A simple first order is Tomato Shorba, Paneer Tikka, Dal Makhni, a Half Paneer Lababdar, naan and Paneer Jalebi with Rabri.

For a first visit to Red Wood Farm, build the meal in six steps: a soup or starter, one tandoor plate, Dal Makhni at ₹275, a curry, a round of breads and a dessert. Chicken eaters should make the curry our house Farm to Table Special Chicken, Half ₹415 or Full ₹695. All prices include GST.

## Where should the meal start?

Start light, because the tandoor and curries are filling. Pick one of these:

- **A soup.** Tomato Shorba and Lemon Coriander are ₹145. Cream of Tomato, Sweet Corn and Manchow are ₹155. For chicken eaters, Chicken Hot & Sour is ₹245 and Smoked Chicken is ₹265.
- **An Indo-Chinese starter.** Honey Chilli Potato is ₹255, Cheese Chilli ₹325 and Crispy Honey Chicken ₹375.
- **A salad.** Garden Fresh Kachumber is ₹125, if the table wants something fresh before the grill.

One soup or one starter per two people is usually enough at this stage.

## Which tandoor plate should you share?

Order one plate for the whole table to share. Paneer Tikka is ₹375 and Tandoori Chicken is ₹375. If you're curious about the Champ section, which is soya chaap, Malai Champ at ₹275 is an easy first try.

We've written a separate [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/tandoor-guide/) that compares the kebabs and tikkas in detail, so we won't repeat it here.

## Which dal belongs on the table?

Dal Makhni, at ₹275, is the one to order if you only order one. Dal makhani is traditionally whole black lentils and kidney beans, cooked slowly and finished with butter and cream. If you want a lighter second dal, Yellow Dal Tadka and Dal Missi Tadka are ₹245 each. Our [Dal Makhani page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/dal-makhani/) explains what to expect.

## Which curry should you order on a first visit?

This is where the house dishes come in.

**For non-veg tables:**

- **Farm to Table Special Chicken.** Our house signature chicken. Half ₹415, Full ₹695. If you only try one thing that's ours, make it this.
- **Atta Chicken, ₹925.** Chicken cooked sealed inside wheat-flour dough. It's the priciest dish on the menu and comes in one size, so it makes most sense when the whole table shares it.
- **Mutton Rogan Josh.** Half ₹345, Full ₹645, for a table that prefers mutton.

**For veg tables:**

- **Paneer Lababdar.** Half ₹255, Full ₹395.
- **Malai Kofta, ₹275.**
- **Saag (seasonal), ₹275.** It's marked seasonal, so check that it's on before you set your heart on it.

A Half lets a table of two or three try two curries instead of one. Our [group ordering guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/group-ordering-guide/) explains when Full is better value.

## Which breads should you mix?

Order a mixed round so everyone tastes a few:

- Butter Naan: ₹45
- Garlic Naan: ₹55
- Laccha Paratha: ₹45
- Missi Roti: ₹30
- Tandoori Roti: ₹20

Add a ₹75 bowl of Farm to Table Special Herbs Chutney on the side. It's our own herb chutney, made in the house, and it goes with the tandoor plate as well as the breads.

## What is the dessert to finish with?

Paneer Jalebi with Rabri, at ₹75, is the dessert to try first. Rasmalai at ₹45 is lighter. For children, a scoop of Vanilla is ₹50. The full list, including the seasonal Gajrela and Malpua Rabri, is on our [desserts page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/desserts/).

## What if your table mixes veg and non-veg eaters?

That's common, and the menu handles it well because every dish carries a veg or non-veg mark. Split the order down the middle. Share one veg starter and one non-veg starter, such as Paneer Tikka and Tandoori Chicken at ₹375 each. Put Dal Makhni in the center, since the whole table can eat it. Then order a Half of one veg curry and a Half of one chicken curry, for example Half Kadhai Paneer at ₹225 and Half Farm to Table Special Chicken at ₹415. Breads and the house herb chutney work for everyone.

## When is a good time for a first visit?

We're open every day from 10 AM to 11 PM. In daytime the lawn is set with long wooden tables and lounge seating. Dinner is when the garden lights come on, including the [fairy-light tunnel](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/fairy-light-tunnel/), so come a little after sunset if you want to see it lit.

## Winter evenings on the lawn: dinner outdoors in Ludhiana
URL: https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/garden/winter-evenings-on-the-lawn/

In short: Red Wood Farm on outer Pakhowal Road serves dinner on its garden lawn every evening until 11 PM, winter included. Dress warm for December and January, start with a hot soup from ₹145 and order from the tandoor. Message us before you leave to ask what is set up on the lawn that night.

Q: Is Red Wood Farm open for dinner in December and January?
A: Yes. We are open every day from 10:00 AM to 11:00 PM, and that includes the winter months.

Q: Can we eat outside on a cold January night?
A: The lawn is outdoors, so come in a warm jacket and closed shoes. Send us a message on 096467 13555 before you set out to ask what is set up that evening.

Q: Is Saag on the menu in winter?
A: Saag is on our menu at ₹275 and is marked seasonal. Ask us whether it is being served on the day you plan to come.

Q: Can I get soup and tandoor food as takeaway on a cold night?
A: Yes. Takeaway orders go by phone or message on 096467 13555. Soups on the menu start at ₹145.

For a winter dinner outdoors in Ludhiana, Red Wood Farm serves on its garden lawn on outer Pakhowal Road every evening until 11 PM. In December and January, dress warm, start with a hot soup priced ₹145 to ₹265 and order from the tandoor. Message us first to ask what is set up on the lawn that night.

## How cold does a winter night on the lawn feel?

December and January are the coldest part of the year in Ludhiana. Once the sun drops, an open lawn loses its warmth fast, and on some nights fog rolls in across the region. We are at Daad, on the edge of the city, with open sky above the tables. That is the charm of eating here, and it is also why a light sweater is not enough.

There is a good side to the early sunset. By the time most families sit down for dinner, the garden is already lit: palms along the driveway wrapped in fairy lights, lamp posts along the paths, trees strung with warm bulbs. In winter you get the whole lit garden at 7 PM instead of waiting for a late summer dusk.

## What should you wear for dinner outside?

- **A real jacket or a heavy shawl,** with a sweater underneath. Layers you can take off are easier than one thin coat.
- **Closed shoes and socks.** Grass can turn damp after dark in the cold months.
- **A cap or muffler** for children and grandparents, who tend to feel the cold first.
- **A blanket in the car** if small children are likely to fall asleep on the drive home.

If someone in your group feels the cold badly, plan a shorter sitting. Order the starters and mains together so the food arrives close to the time you sit down.

## What warming is set up at the venue?

We would rather tell you on the day than promise it on a web page. What we can set up for warmth changes from night to night, so send a message to 096467 13555 before you leave home and ask what is on the lawn that evening. If you are bringing older relatives, ask about the most sheltered table as well.

For some events we have put up a covered tent dining area with chandeliers. Whether anything covered is in place on an ordinary dinner night is another good question for the same message.

## Hot soups to start the meal

A bowl of soup is the quickest way to warm up while the tandoor dishes cook. Every soup on our menu comes as a single portion, and prices include GST.

**Vegetarian**
- Tomato Shorba, ₹145
- Lemon Coriander, ₹145
- Hot & Sour, ₹145
- Cream of Tomato, ₹155
- Cream of Mushroom, ₹155

- Manchow Soup, ₹155

**Non-vegetarian**
- Chicken Clear, ₹245
- Chicken Hot & Sour, ₹245
- Smoked Chicken, ₹265

## Tandoor dishes for a cold evening

Food from the clay oven reaches the table hot, which counts for a lot when the air is cold. Chicken eaters can pick Tandoori Chicken at ₹375, Bhatti Da Murg at ₹395, Pindi Seekh Kabab at ₹395 or Punjabi Murg Tikka at ₹415. On the vegetarian side, try Paneer Tikka at ₹375, Mushroom Tikka at ₹395, Hariyali Tikka at ₹325 or Aloo Nazakat at ₹245.

For a group, a platter saves passing plates around in the cold: the Tandoori Veg Platter is ₹525 and the Tandoori Non-Veg platter is ₹725. Sizzlers arrive on a hot plate, which suits a winter table well. The Veg Sizzler is ₹395 and the Non-Veg Sizzler is ₹475.

Keep the breads coming. Butter Naan is ₹45, Garlic Naan ₹55, Laccha Paratha ₹45 and Missi Roti ₹30. Our [tandoor guide](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/food/tandoor-guide/) goes through the whole section dish by dish.

## Seasonal winter dishes on our menu

Three dishes on our menu carry a seasonal mark, and all three belong to a Punjabi winter:

- **Saag (seasonal), ₹275.** Pair it with Missi Roti at ₹30 or Butter Roti at ₹25.
- **Gajrela, 100 g (seasonal), ₹75.** The slow-cooked carrot sweet that shows up on Punjabi tables once the cold sets in.
- **Malpua Rabri (seasonal), ₹65.** Fried malpua served with rabri.

Seasonal means these dishes are not on every day of the year. If one of them is the reason for your visit, ask us before you drive out. For more on what Punjab eats in the cold months, read our guide to [Punjabi winter food](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/guides/punjabi-winter-food/).

## Winter dates worth planning ahead

The cold months bring Christmas, New Year's Eve and Lohri in mid-January. These are the dates people most often plan family dinners and small get-togethers around. If you want a table, or space for a group, on one of them, send your date, time and number of guests early. Our [Lohri celebration page](https://bhapag.github.io/redwood-farm/party/lohri-celebration-ludhiana/) covers small Lohri gatherings on the lawn.
